With 'Stand erect, protect us from distress with your banner, burn down every ravenous demon; make us erect for walking, for living; find our worship among the gods'—[he offers] the third [oblation].

15.8.5.a.s: yasmād bhīṣāvāśiṣṭhās \\ iti dvitīyāṃ vāśyamāne yasmād bhīṣā samutkram̐sthās \\ iti dvitīyām ucchrayati //
15.8.5.a.d: यस्माद् भीषावाशिष्ठास् \\ इति द्वितीयां वाश्यमाने यस्माद् भीषा समुत्क्रम्̐स्थास् \\ इति द्वितीयाम् उच्छ्रयति ॥
15.8.5.a.m: 'From which fear you cried out...'—[he offers] the second [oblation] with this [verse] if it cries out. 'From which fear you reared up...'—[he offers] the second [oblation] if it rears up.

15.8.6.a.s: yasmād bhīṣāpalāyiṣṭhās \\ iti dvitīyāṃ palāyite 'nāgacchaty anyaṃ tadrūpaṃ tadvarṇaṃ tadvayasaṃ tajjātīyaṃ taddaivatam upākṛtya tena sam̐sthāpayet //
15.8.6.a.d: यस्माद् भीषापलायिष्ठास् \\ इति द्वितीयां पलायिते ऽनागच्छत्य् अन्यं तद्रूपं तद्वर्णं तद्वयसं तज्जातीयं तद्दैवतम् उपाकृत्य तेन सम्̐स्थापयेत् ॥
15.8.6.a.m: 'From which fear you ran away...'—[he offers] the second [oblation] with this [verse] if it has run away. If it does not return, having dedicated another [animal] of the same appearance, the same color, the same age, the same species, [and] dedicated to the same deity, he should conclude [the sacrifice] with it.

15.8.7.a.s: tajjātīye 'vidyamāne ajā avayo gāva ity anyonyasya pratinidhayo bhavanti //
15.8.7.a.d: तज्जातीये ऽविद्यमाने अजा अवयो गाव इत्य् अन्योन्यस्य प्रतिनिधयो भवन्ति ॥
15.8.7.a.m: If one of the same species is not available, goats, sheep, and cattle serve as substitutes for one another.

15.8.8.a.m: If these are not available, he should conclude the remainder [of the sacrifice] with clarified butter.

15.8.9.a.s: yasmād bhīṣā samajñāsthās \\ iti dvitīyām akāmasaṃjñapane //
15.8.9.a.d: यस्माद् भीषा समज्ञास्थास् \\ इति द्वितीयाम् अकामसंज्ञपने ॥
15.8.9.a.m: 'From which fear you were stilled...'—[he offers] the second [oblation] with this [verse] in the case of unintentional killing.

15.8.10.a.s: ya idam akas tasmai svāhā \\ iti sarvottamāṃ juhoti //
15.8.10.a.d: य इदम् अकस् तस्मै स्वाहा \\ इति सर्वोत्तमां जुहोति ॥
15.8.10.a.m: 'To him who did this, svāhā'—with this [verse] he offers the final oblation of all.

15.8.11.a.s: na vā uv etan mriyase / \ āśānāṃ tvā \ viśvā āśāḥ / \ āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvas \\ iti catasṛbhiḥ paśuṃ vyāpannam abhimantryāpo 'bhyavahṛtyānyaṃ tadrūpaṃ tadvarṇaṃ tadvayasaṃ tajjātīyaṃ taddaivatam upākṛtya tena sam̐sthāpayet / tajjātīye 'vidyamāne // palāyite vyākhyātam //
15.8.11.a.d: न वा उव् एतन् म्रियसे । \ आशानां त्वा \ विश्वा आशाः । \ आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुवस् \\ इति चतसृभिः पशुं व्यापन्नम् अभिमन्त्र्यापो ऽभ्यवहृत्यान्यं तद्रूपं तद्वर्णं तद्वयसं तज्जातीयं तद्दैवतम् उपाकृत्य तेन सम्̐स्थापयेत् । तज्जातीये ऽविद्यमाने ॥ पलायिते व्याख्यातम् ॥
15.8.11.a.m: Having addressed a stricken animal with the four [verses], 'You do not die at all in this way...', 'The quarters of the sky to you...', 'All the quarters...', and 'The waters are indeed refreshing...', and having thrown [it] into water, having dedicated another [animal] of the same appearance, the same color, the same age, the same species, [and] dedicated to the same deity, he should conclude [the sacrifice] with it. If one of the same species is not available, [the rule] has been explained under [the case of the animal that has] run away.

15.8.12.a.s: ukhām̐ sravantīm agadām akarma \\ agnir hotā pṛthivy antarikṣam \\ dyaur yataś cyutad agnāv eva tat \\ na tat prāpnoti nirṛtiṃ parācair iti paśūkhām̐ sravantīm abhimantrayeta //
15.8.12.a.d: उखाम्̐ स्रवन्तीम् अगदाम् अकर्म \\ अग्निर् होता पृथिव्य् अन्तरिक्षम् \\ द्यौर् यतश् च्युतद् अग्नाव् एव तत् \\ न तत् प्राप्नोति निरृतिं पराचैर् इति पशूखाम्̐ स्रवन्तीम् अभिमन्त्रयेत ॥
15.8.12.a.m: 'The leaking pot we have made sound; Agni is the hotṛ, the earth, the midspace, and the sky. Whence it dropped, into Agni alone it has gone; it does not reach Nirṛti, turned away'—with this [verse] he should address the animal-pot when it leaks.

15.8.13.a.s: yāvanti paśor avadānāni na vindeyus tāvat kṛtva ājyasyāvadyeta //
15.8.13.a.d: यावन्ति पशोर् अवदानानि न विन्देयुस् तावत् कृत्व आज्यस्यावद्येत ॥
15.8.13.a.m: As many portions of the animal as they might not find, so many times he should cut portions of clarified butter.

15.8.14.a.s: ye paśuṃ vimathnīran yas tān kāmayetārtim ārcheyur iti kuvid aṅga \\ iti namovṛktivatyarcāgnīdhre juhuyāt / āhavanīye śāmitre vā nirūḍhapaśubandhe //
15.8.14.a.d: ये पशुं विमथ्नीरन् यस् तान् कामयेतार्तिम् आर्छेयुर् इति कुविद् अङ्ग \\ इति नमोवृक्तिवत्यर्चाग्नीध्रे जुहुयात् । आहवनीये शामित्रे वा निरूढपशुबन्धे ॥
15.8.14.a.m: If [robbers] carry off the animal, and if he desires that they incur misfortune, he should offer in the āgnīdhra fire with the verse containing the word namovṛkti: 'Surely indeed...'. [He offers it] in the āhavanīye or the slaughtering fire in an independent animal sacrifice.

15.8.15.a.s: yady aṣṭāpadīty anubudhyeran dhātā rātiḥ \ sūryo devas \\ iti dvābhyāṃ gārhapatye juhoti //
15.8.15.a.d: यद्य् अष्टापदीत्य् अनुबुध्येरन् धाता रातिः \ सूर्यो देवस् \\ इति द्वाभ्यां गार्हपत्ये जुहोति ॥
15.8.15.a.m: If they discover that [the animal] has eight feet [being pregnant], he offers into the gārhapatya fire with two verses: 'Dhātṛ gives...' and 'The divine Sūrya...'.

15.8.16.a.s: yasyās te harito garbhas \\ ity abhimantrya \\ āvartana vartaya \\ iti pradakṣiṇaṃ garbham āvartayati //
15.8.16.a.d: यस्यास् ते हरितो गर्भस् \\ इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य \\ आवर्तन वर्तय \\ इति प्रदक्षिणं गर्भम् आवर्तयति ॥
15.8.16.a.m: Having addressed [it] with, 'Whose fetus is tawny...', he turns the fetus clockwise with, 'O turner, turn...'

15.8.17.a.s: vi te bhinadmi takarīm ity antarā śroṇī garbhaṃ niṣkhidati //
15.8.17.a.d: वि ते भिनद्मि तकरीम् इत्य् अन्तरा श्रोणी गर्भं निष्खिदति ॥
15.8.17.a.m: With 'I split apart your pudendum', he draws out the fetus between the thighs.

15.8.18.a.s: bahiste astu bāl ity āśayād garbhaṃ nirasya \\ urudrapso viśvarūpa indur iti rasāya pātram upayacchati / śūlena paśuśrapaṇe nihatya garbham̐ śrapayati //
15.8.18.a.d: बहिस्ते अस्तु बाल् इत्य् आशयाद् गर्भं निरस्य \\ उरुद्रप्सो विश्वरूप इन्दुर् इति रसाय पात्रम् उपयच्छति । शूलेन पशुश्रपणे निहत्य गर्भम्̐ श्रपयति ॥
15.8.18.a.m: With 'May the hair be outside', having cast the fetus out of the amnion, he holds a vessel beneath for the broth with 'The great drop, of manifold form, the moon...'. Having fastened it onto a spit at the animal-cooking place, he cooks the fetus.

15.8.19.a.s: paśupuroḍāśaṃ nirupya bhaktī dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ garbhapuroḍāśaṃ nirvapati //
15.8.19.a.d: पशुपुरोडाशं निरुप्य भक्ती द्यावापृथिवीयं गर्भपुरोडाशं निर्वपति ॥
15.8.19.a.m: Having apportioned the animal sacrificial cake, he separately portions out a fetus sacrificial cake for Heaven and Earth.

15.8.20.a.s: paśor avadānāny avadāya garbhasya purastān nābhyā anyad avadyed upariṣṭād anyad avadāya daivateṣv avadadhāti //
15.8.20.a.d: पशोर् अवदानान्य् अवदाय गर्भस्य पुरस्तान् नाभ्या अन्यद् अवद्येद् उपरिष्टाद् अन्यद् अवदाय दैवतेष्व् अवदधाति ॥
15.8.20.a.m: Having cut the portions of the animal, he should cut one [portion] from the front of the fetus's navel, and having cut another from above [it], he adds them to the portions for the deities.

15.8.21.a.s: rasaṃ traidhaṃ karoti / daivateṣu sauviṣṭakṛteṣv aiḍeṣu ca //
15.8.21.a.d: रसं त्रैधं करोति । दैवतेषु सौविष्टकृतेष्व् ऐडेषु च ॥
15.8.21.a.m: He divides the broth into three parts: for the deities, for the Sviṣṭakṛt offerings, and for the Iḍā portions.

15.8.22.a.m: When the vaṣaṭ-call has been uttered, he offers with 'Ekapadī, dvipadī...'.

15.8.23.a.s: vaṣaṭkṛte viṣṇo pra tat te adya śipiviṣṭa nāma \\ ity anyatarayā garbhasya dakṣiṇapūrvam̐ sakthiṃ juhoti //
15.8.23.a.d: वषट्कृते विष्णो प्र तत् ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट नाम \\ इत्य् अन्यतरया गर्भस्य दक्षिणपूर्वम्̐ सक्थिं जुहोति ॥
15.8.23.a.m: When the vaṣaṭ-call has been uttered, he offers the right fore-thigh of the fetus with either [verse beginning], 'O Viṣṇu, forth that name of yours today, Śipiviṣṭa...'.

15.8.24.a.s: dakṣiṇākāle 'ṣṭāprūḍḍhiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇā / tṛtīye 'ntarakośa uṣṇīṣeṇāviṣṭitaṃ bhavati / tad dadāti / vibalān kośān karoti //
15.8.24.a.d: दक्षिणाकाले ऽष्टाप्रूड्ढिरण्यं दक्षिणा । तृतीये ऽन्तरकोश उष्णीषेणाविष्टितं भवति । तद् ददाति । विबलान् कोशान् करोति ॥
15.8.24.a.m: At the time of the priestly gifts, an eight-prūḍa piece of gold is the priestly gift. In the third inner case it is wrapped in a turban. That he gives. He makes the cases of unequal strength.

15.8.25.a.s: maruto yasya hi kṣaye \ yajñair vā yajñavāhasas ity anyatarayā paśuśrapaṇe garbhaṃ juhoti //
15.8.25.a.d: मरुतो यस्य हि क्षये \ यज्ञैर् वा यज्ञवाहसस् इत्य् अन्यतरया पशुश्रपणे गर्भं जुहोति ॥
15.8.25.a.m: With either [verse], 'The Maruts, in whose dwelling...' or 'Or with sacrifices, O bearers of the sacrifice...', he offers the fetus at the animal-cooking place.

15.8.26.a.m: And he does not utter svāhā over the fetus sacrificial cake.

15.8.27.a.s: api vā mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca nas \\ iti paśuśrapaṇasya śīte bhasmani garbham upohati //
15.8.27.a.d: अपि वा मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नस् \\ इति पशुश्रपणस्य शीते भस्मनि गर्भम् उपोहति ॥
15.8.27.a.m: Or else, with 'Great heaven and earth for us...', he pushes the fetus into the cooled ashes of the animal-cooking place.

15.8.29.a.s: etaṃ yuvānaṃ pari vo dadāmi \\ iti // pañcabhir abhimantrya //
15.8.29.a.d: एतं युवानं परि वो ददामि \\ इति ॥ पञ्चभिर् अभिमन्त्र्य ॥
15.8.29.a.m: Having addressed [the animal] with the five [verses beginning], 'This youth I commit to you...',

15.8.30.a.s: yasyānapravṛtto yūpo virohet tasmim̐s tvāṣṭram̐ sāṇḍaṃ lomaśaṃ piṅgalaṃ bahurūpaṃ savanīyasyopalambhyaṃ kuryāt trayastrim̐śat tantavo ye vitatnire \\ iti juhuyāt //
15.8.30.a.d: यस्यानप्रवृत्तो यूपो विरोहेत् तस्मिम्̐स् त्वाष्ट्रम्̐ साण्डं लोमशं पिङ्गलं बहुरूपं सवनीयस्योपलम्भ्यं कुर्यात् त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शत् तन्तवो ये वितत्निरे \\ इति जुहुयात् ॥
15.8.30.a.m: If a sacrificial post that has not fallen should sprout, he should seize for it an uncastrated, hairy, reddish-brown, variegated animal sacred to Tvaṣṭṛ as an addition to the savanīya animal, and should offer with: 'The thirty-three threads which were stretched out...'.

15.8.31.a.s: yadi kṛṣṇaśakunir dhvam̐sayann uparyupari sadohavirdhānāny atipated bhaya utpanne śakye yaṣṭum̐ sarvebhyo havirbhyaḥ somebhyaś ca droṇakalaśe samavadāya ye devā yeṣām idaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ babhūva \ yeṣāṃ prayājā utānūyājāḥ / \ indrajyeṣṭhebhyo varuṇarājabhyas \\ agnihotṛbhyo devebhyaḥ svāhā \\ ity āhutiṃ juhoti //
15.8.31.a.d: यदि कृष्णशकुनिर् ध्वम्̐सयन्न् उपर्युपरि सदोहविर्धानान्य् अतिपतेद् भय उत्पन्ने शक्ये यष्टुम्̐ सर्वेभ्यो हविर्भ्यः सोमेभ्यश् च द्रोणकलशे समवदाय ये देवा येषाम् इदं भागधेयं बभूव \ येषां प्रयाजा उतानूयाजाः । \ इन्द्रज्येष्ठेभ्यो वरुणराजभ्यस् \\ अग्निहोतृभ्यो देवेभ्यः स्वाहा \\ इत्य् आहुतिं जुहोति ॥
15.8.31.a.m: If a black bird, shaking [its wings], should fly across over the sadas and the havirdhāna sheds, when danger has arisen, if it is possible to sacrifice, having collected together portions from all the sacrificial oblations and from the somas into the droṇakalaśa, he offers an oblation with: 'Those gods whose share this became, whose are the fore-offerings and after-offerings, to those gods whose eldest is Indra, whose king is Varuṇa, who have Agni as hotṛ, svāhā!'.

15.8.33.a.s: yady ṛkto yajñabhreṣa ṛcchet \\ bhūr iti gārhapatye juhuyāt / yadi yajuṣṭas \\ bhuvas \\ iti dakṣiṇāgnau / yadi sāmataḥ suvar ity āhavanīye / yadi sarvataḥ sarvābhir ekām āhavanīye brahmā vā juhuyāt //
15.8.33.a.d: यद्य् ऋक्तो यज्ञभ्रेष ऋच्छेत् \\ भूर् इति गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात् । यदि यजुष्टस् \\ भुवस् \\ इति दक्षिणाग्नौ । यदि सामतः सुवर् इत्य् आहवनीये । यदि सर्वतः सर्वाभिर् एकाम् आहवनीये ब्रह्मा वा जुहुयात् ॥
15.8.33.a.m: If a mishap in the sacrifice should occur through an ṛc, he should offer in the gārhapatya fire with 'Bhūḥ'. If through a yajus, in the dakṣiṇāgni fire with 'Bhuvaḥ'. If through a sāman, in the āhavanīya fire with 'Suvaḥ'. If from all, he should offer one [oblation] into the āhavanīya fire with all [three words], or the brahman priest should offer it.

15.8.35.a.s: audumbarī naśyed bhajyeta vānyāṃ pracchidya \\ ūrg asi \\ ūrjaṃ mayi dhehi \ śriyo tiṣṭha pratiṣṭhitā \ divam̐ stabdhāntarikṣaṃ ca pṛthivyāṃ ca dṛḍhā bhava \ dhamitrī dharitrī janitrī \\ ity ucchrayati //
15.8.35.a.d: औदुम्बरी नश्येद् भज्येत वान्यां प्रच्छिद्य \\ ऊर्ग् असि \\ ऊर्जं मयि धेहि \ श्रियो तिष्ठ प्रतिष्ठिता \ दिवम्̐ स्तब्धान्तरिक्षं च पृथिव्यां च दृढा भव \ धमित्री धरित्री जनित्री \\ इत्य् उच्छ्रयति ॥
15.8.35.a.m: If the audumbarī post should be lost or broken, after cutting another one, he erects it with: "You are strength; place strength in me! Stand established for prosperity! Support the sky and the intermediate space, and be firm upon the earth! O blower, sustainer, generator!"

15.8.36.a.m: The adhvaryu, the sacrificer, or the brahman priest erects [it].

15.8.37.a.m: He addresses [the post] that has been measured with the regular yajus mantra.

15.8.38.a.s: yadi havirdhāne padyeyātāṃ dakṣiṇām adhvaryur udgṛhṇīyāt pratiprasthātopastabhnuyāt / uttaraṃ pratiprasthātodgṛhṇīyād adhvaryur upastabhnuyāt //
15.8.38.a.d: यदि हविर्धाने पद्येयातां दक्षिणाम् अध्वर्युर् उद्गृह्णीयात् प्रतिप्रस्थातोपस्तभ्नुयात् । उत्तरं प्रतिप्रस्थातोद्गृह्णीयाद् अध्वर्युर् उपस्तभ्नुयात् ॥
15.8.38.a.m: If the two havirdhāna carts should collapse, the adhvaryu should lift up the southern one, [and] the pratiprasthātṛ should prop it up; the pratiprasthātṛ should lift up the northern one, [and] the adhvaryu should prop it up.

15.8.39.a.m: Both prop [them] up with [a verse] addressed to Viṣṇu; he fastens [them] with [a verse] addressed to Viṣṇu; both touch [them] with [a verse] addressed to the Aśvins.

15.8.40.a.s: agne vājasya gomatas \\ iti tisṛbhir uṣṇigbhir adhvaryur āgnīdhre juhoti / kakudbhiḥ pratiprasthātā // bhadro no agnir āhutas \\ bhadrā rātiḥ subhaga bhadro adhvaraḥ / \ bhadrā uta praśastayaḥ / \ bhadrā uta praśastayas \\ bhadraṃ manaḥ kṛṇuṣva vṛtratūrye / \ yenā samatsu sāsahaḥ / \ yenā samatsu sāsahas \\ ava sthirā tanuhi bhūri śardhatām / \ vanemā te abhiṣṭibhir ity etā āmnātā bhavanti //
15.8.40.a.d: अग्ने वाजस्य गोमतस् \\ इति तिसृभिर् उष्णिग्भिर् अध्वर्युर् आग्नीध्रे जुहोति । ककुद्भिः प्रतिप्रस्थाता ॥ भद्रो नो अग्निर् आहुतस् \\ भद्रा रातिः सुभग भद्रो अध्वरः । \ भद्रा उत प्रशस्तयः । \ भद्रा उत प्रशस्तयस् \\ भद्रं मनः कृणुष्व वृत्रतूर्ये । \ येना समत्सु सासहः । \ येना समत्सु सासहस् \\ अव स्थिरा तनुहि भूरि शर्धताम् । \ वनेमा ते अभिष्टिभिर् इत्य् एता आम्नाता भवन्ति ॥
15.8.40.a.m: The adhvaryu offers into the āgnīdhra fire with three uṣṇih verses: "O Agni, of prize, rich in cattle..."; the pratiprasthātṛ with kakubh verses: "Auspicious to us is Agni when invoked, / auspicious the gift, O fortunate one, auspicious the sacrifice; / auspicious also the praises. / Auspicious also the praises: / make an auspicious mind at the slaying of Vṛtra, / wherewith you may overcome in battles. / Wherewith you may overcome in battles: / unbend the stiff [bows] of the many that are arrogant; / may we win through your assistances." Thus these are handed down in the sacred text.

15.8.41.a.s: śiro yajñasya pratidhīyatām \ amṛtaṃ devatāmayam \\ vaiṣṇavyā kriyatām̐ śiras \\ āśvinyā pratidhīyatām iti caturgṛhītaṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ vā gṛhītvā samānau homau juhutaḥ //
15.8.41.a.d: शिरो यज्ञस्य प्रतिधीयताम् \ अमृतं देवतामयम् \\ वैष्णव्या क्रियताम्̐ शिरस् \\ आश्विन्या प्रतिधीयताम् इति चतुर्गृहीतं पञ्चगृहीतं वा गृहीत्वा समानौ होमौ जुहुतः ॥
15.8.41.a.m: Having taken four ladlings or five ladlings, both make identical offerings with: "May the head of the sacrifice be set on, immortal, consisting of deities; let the head be made with [a verse] addressed to Viṣṇu; let it be set on with [a verse] addressed to the Aśvins!"

15.8.42.a.s: yady āgniky ukhāmā bhidyeta saṃkṛṣya punaḥ kuryāt //
15.8.42.a.d: यद्य् आग्निक्य् उखामा भिद्येत संकृष्य पुनः कुर्यात् ॥
15.8.42.a.m: If the unbaked ukhā pot related to the fire-altar should break, having scraped it together, he should make it again.

15.8.43.a.s: yadi pakvā bhidyeta tair eva kapālaiḥ supiṣṭair anyāṃ mṛdam̐ sam̐sṛjya kuryāt //
15.8.43.a.d: यदि पक्वा भिद्येत तैर् एव कपालैः सुपिष्टैर् अन्यां मृदम्̐ सम्̐सृज्य कुर्यात् ॥
15.8.43.a.m: If the baked one should break, he should make it by mixing other clay with those very pot-sherds well ground.

15.8.44.a.s: yasyāgnir ukhya udvāyed āhavanīyaṃ praṇīya sa eva punaḥ parīdhyaḥ //
15.8.44.a.d: यस्याग्निर् उख्य उद्वायेद् आहवनीयं प्रणीय स एव पुनः परीध्यः ॥
15.8.44.a.m: For whomever the fire in the ukhā pot should go out, having brought forward the āhavanīya fire, that very one is to be enclosed again.

15.8.45.a.s: kṛṣṇaṃ vāso deyam / kṛṣṇā dhenuḥ kṛṣṇo vā gauḥ śatamānaṃ ca hiraṇyam //
15.8.45.a.d: कृष्णं वासो देयम् । कृष्णा धेनुः कृष्णो वा गौः शतमानं च हिरण्यम् ॥
15.8.45.a.m: A black garment is to be given, a black milk-cow or a black bull, and gold weighing a hundred mānas.

15.8.46.a.s: yat pūrvasminn ahany uttarasmā ahne yajñāyajñiyaṃ prati vasatīvarīr gṛhṇāti / tenāhar abhyāsajati / tena yajñam̐ saṃtanoti //
15.8.46.a.d: यत् पूर्वस्मिन्न् अहन्य् उत्तरस्मा अह्ने यज्ञायज्ञियं प्रति वसतीवरीर् गृह्णाति । तेनाहर् अभ्यासजति । तेन यज्ञम्̐ संतनोति ॥
15.8.46.a.m: Because on the preceding day he takes the vasatīvarī waters in view of the yajñāyajñiya chant for the subsequent day, thereby he links the day; thereby he extends the sacrifice.

15.8.47.a.s: yat pūrvasminn ahany uttarasmā ahne stotryam anurūpaṃ kṛtvā śam̐sati / tenāhar abhyāsajati / tena yajñam̐ saṃtanoti / yad atipreṣyati tenāhar abhyāsajati tena yajñam̐ saṃtanotīti //
15.8.47.a.d: यत् पूर्वस्मिन्न् अहन्य् उत्तरस्मा अह्ने स्तोत्र्यम् अनुरूपं कृत्वा शम्̐सति । तेनाहर् अभ्यासजति । तेन यज्ञम्̐ संतनोति । यद् अतिप्रेष्यति तेनाहर् अभ्यासजति तेन यज्ञम्̐ संतनोतीति ॥
15.8.47.a.m: Because on the preceding day he recites making the stotriya verse corresponding for the subsequent day, thereby he links the day; thereby he extends the sacrifice. Because he sends forth the call beyond, thereby he links the day; thereby he extends the sacrifice—so [it is said].

15.8.48.a.s: eteṣām ekasminn akriyamāṇe namo brahmaṇe namo astv agnaye \ namaḥ pṛthivyai nama oṣadhībhyaḥ / \ namo vāce namo vācaspataye \ namo viṣṇave bṛhate karomi svāhā \\ ity etat prāyaścittaṃ juhuyād etat prāyaścittaṃ juhuyāt //
15.8.48.a.d: एतेषाम् एकस्मिन्न् अक्रियमाणे नमो ब्रह्मणे नमो अस्त्व् अग्नये \ नमः पृथिव्यै नम ओषधीभ्यः । \ नमो वाचे नमो वाचस्पतये \ नमो विष्णवे बृहते करोमि स्वाहा \\ इत्य् एतत् प्रायश्चित्तं जुहुयाद् एतत् प्रायश्चित्तं जुहुयात् ॥
15.8.48.a.m: When one of these is not performed, he should make this expiatory offering: "Homage to the brahman, homage be to Agni, / homage to the earth, homage to the plants; / homage to speech, homage to the lord of speech; / homage to great Viṣṇu I make, svāhā!" He should make this expiatory offering.

16.1.1.a.m: By means of the twelve-day rite, he indeed prospers with offspring.

16.1.2.a.s: jyaiṣṭhyam aśnute sa hy enam anubhavati //
16.1.2.a.d: ज्यैष्ठ्यम् अश्नुते स ह्य् एनम् अनुभवति ॥
16.1.2.a.m: He attains pre-eminence, for it conforms to him.

16.1.4.a.m: Its procedure for the fire has been explained.

16.1.5.a.m: Those who have attained prosperity should sacrifice with the metre.

16.1.6.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta cchandasā yajate so 'smai kāmaḥ samṛdhyate / yajate yajanta iti codanaṃ yo 'tapasvī syād asam̐śliṣṭo 'sya yajñaḥ syāt tapasvī syād yajñam eva tat sam̐śleṣayatīti vijñāyate //
16.1.6.a.d: यं कामयेत च्छन्दसा यजते सो ऽस्मै कामः समृध्यते । यजते यजन्त इति चोदनं यो ऽतपस्वी स्याद् असम्̐श्लिष्टो ऽस्य यज्ञः स्यात् तपस्वी स्याद् यज्ञम् एव तत् सम्̐श्लेषयतीति विज्ञायते ॥
16.1.6.a.m: Whatever desire he may have, who sacrifices with the metre, that desire is fulfilled for him. "He sacrifices", "they sacrifice" is the injunction. He who might be without ascetic heat, his sacrifice would be unjoined; he should have ascetic heat: thereby he joins the sacrifice—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

16.1.7.a.m: Fat, he undergoes consecration; lean, he sacrifices.

16.1.8.a.m: One should know [the numbers as] optional; he causes forty-eight to pass.

16.1.9.a.m: Fifteen should undergo consecration, having the half-month as their domain.

16.1.11.a.s: ekavim̐śatim̐ rukkāmāḥ / trayovim̐śatiṃ pratiṣṭhākāmāḥ / caturvim̐śatiṃ brahmavarcasakāmāḥ / trim̐śataṃ māsāyatanāḥ / trayastrim̐śatam ojaskāmāḥ / catvārim̐śatam indriyakāmāḥ / catuścatvārim̐śataṃ vīryakāmāḥ / aṣṭācatvārim̐śataṃ paśukāmāḥ //
16.1.11.a.d: एकविम्̐शतिम्̐ रुक्कामाः । त्रयोविम्̐शतिं प्रतिष्ठाकामाः । चतुर्विम्̐शतिं ब्रह्मवर्चसकामाः । त्रिम्̐शतं मासायतनाः । त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शतम् ओजस्कामाः । चत्वारिम्̐शतम् इन्द्रियकामाः । चतुश्चत्वारिम्̐शतं वीर्यकामाः । अष्टाचत्वारिम्̐शतं पशुकामाः ॥
16.1.11.a.m: Twenty-one, if desiring brightness; twenty-three, if desiring stability; twenty-four, if desiring holy lustre; thirty, having the month as their domain; thirty-three, if desiring vigor; forty, if desiring faculty of the senses; forty-four, if desiring virility; forty-eight, if desiring cattle.

16.1.12.a.m: "An unlimited number should undergo consecration," they say at the end.

16.1.13.a.m: They too occupy the place of the sacrificer in the ahīna.

16.1.14.a.s: brāhmaṇā ṛtvijo dīkṣitānām adīkṣitānām ahīnasya tena yājayanti //
16.1.14.a.d: ब्राह्मणा ऋत्विजो दीक्षितानाम् अदीक्षितानाम् अहीनस्य तेन याजयन्ति ॥
16.1.14.a.m: The brāhmaṇa priests officiate for consecrated or unconsecrated [sacrificers] of an ahīna with that [rite].

16.1.15.a.s: tasmād dvādaśāhena na yājyaṃ pāpmano vyāvṛttyā iti
16.1.15.a.d: तस्माद् द्वादशाहेन न याज्यं पाप्मनो व्यावृत्त्या इति
16.1.15.a.m: Therefore one should not officiate at the twelve-day rite, for the sake of separation from evil—so [says the Brāhmaṇa].

16.1.16.a.m: He who, knowing thus, sacrifices with the twelve-day rite—

16.1.18.a.m: He who, knowing thus, accepts [dakṣiṇās] at the twelve-day rite—

16.1.19.a.m: [The Brāhmaṇa] speaks referring both to the priests and to the sacrificer.

16.1.20.a.s: brāhmaṇānāṃ tu satram ato dīkṣitānām̐ saptadaśānām āsata upayanti //
16.1.20.a.d: ब्राह्मणानां तु सत्रम् अतो दीक्षितानाम्̐ सप्तदशानाम् आसत उपयन्ति ॥
16.1.20.a.m: A satra, however, belongs to brāhmaṇas; hence, seventeen consecrated persons sit, enter upon [it].

16.1.21.a.m: The injunction is that all have performed their first sacrifice, or the master of the house [has].

16.1.22.a.m: All should perform the duties of the sacrificer that are not in conflict with the duties of an officiating priest.

16.1.23.a.s: gṛhapatiḥ parārthāni yathā yūpāñjanam ṛtuyājyām ity evam̐rūpāṇi dharmapratiṣedhe bhūyasāṃ dharmo 'nugrahyate ( gṛhapater vā ) //
16.1.23.a.d: गृहपतिः परार्थानि यथा यूपाञ्जनम् ऋतुयाज्याम् इत्य् एवम्̐रूपाणि धर्मप्रतिषेधे भूयसां धर्मो ऽनुग्रह्यते ( गृहपतेर् वा ) ॥
16.1.23.a.m: The master of the house performs those for the sake of others, such as the anointing of the sacrificial post and the seasonal offering verses; in such cases, when there is an incompatibility of ritual practices, the practice of the majority is adopted (or that of the master of the house).

16.1.24.a.m: They should perform according to the procedure of the enkindling verses of the master of the house alone.

16.1.25.a.s: tvaṃ varuṇas \\ iti vasiṣṭharājanyānām̐ sāmidhenīparidhānīyā / ājuhota \\ itītareṣāṃ gotrāṇām //
16.1.25.a.d: त्वं वरुणस् \\ इति वसिष्ठराजन्यानाम्̐ सामिधेनीपरिधानीया । आजुहोत \\ इतीतरेषां गोत्राणाम् ॥
16.1.25.a.m: "You are Varuṇa..." is the concluding enkindling verse for descendants of Vasiṣṭha and royals; "Offer ye..." for other lineages.

16.1.26.a.s: nārāśaṃso dvitīyaḥ prayājo vasiṣṭhaśunakānām / tanūnapād itareṣāṃ gotrāṇām //
16.1.26.a.d: नाराशंसो द्वितीयः प्रयाजो वसिष्ठशुनकानाम् । तनूनपाद् इतरेषां गोत्राणाम् ॥
16.1.26.a.m: Nārāśaṃsa is the second fore-offering for descendants of Vasiṣṭha and Śunaka; Tanūnapāt for other lineages.

16.1.27.a.m: About to offer the Sāvitra offerings, they should bring [their fires] together; having offered, they should separate them.

16.1.28.a.s: paśubhir yakṣyamāṇāḥ saṃnivaperann iṣṭvā nivaperan gṛhapatir vāraṇyoḥ saṃnivaperan //
16.1.28.a.d: पशुभिर् यक्ष्यमाणाः संनिवपेरन्न् इष्ट्वा निवपेरन् गृहपतिर् वारण्योः संनिवपेरन् ॥
16.1.28.a.m: About to sacrifice with animals, they should bring [their fires] together; having sacrificed, they should separate them; or they should bring them together in the two kindling sticks of the master of the house.

16.1.29.a.s: ya ito 'gnir janiṣyate sa naḥ sarveṣām \\ yad anena yajñena jeṣyāmo 'nena paśubandhena tan naḥ saha \ saha naḥ sādhutulyā \ ya evaṃ pāpaṃ karavat tasyaiva tat \\ ity uktam //
16.1.29.a.d: य इतो ऽग्निर् जनिष्यते स नः सर्वेषाम् \\ यद् अनेन यज्ञेन जेष्यामो ऽनेन पशुबन्धेन तन् नः सह \ सह नः साधुतुल्या \ य एवं पापं करवत् तस्यैव तत् \\ इत्य् उक्तम् ॥
16.1.29.a.m: "Which fire shall be produced from here, that belongs to all of us. What we shall win by this sacrifice, by this animal sacrifice, that is together for us. Together for us be the equal share of goodness. Whoever may do wrong in this manner, his alone it shall be"—thus it is declared.

16.1.30.a.s: gṛhaptiḥ samāropayate / svayam itare gṛhapatir vā //
16.1.30.a.d: गृहप्तिः समारोपयते । स्वयम् इतरे गृहपतिर् वा ॥
16.1.30.a.m: The master of the house mounts [the fire into the kindling sticks]; or the others themselves, or the master of the house [does so for them].

16.1.32.a.s: śiśire dīkṣante / vasanta uttiṣṭhata iti vijñāyate //
16.1.32.a.d: शिशिरे दीक्षन्ते । वसन्त उत्तिष्ठत इति विज्ञायते ॥
16.1.32.a.m: They undergo consecration in the cool season; they conclude in the spring—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

16.1.33.a.s: śiśiro vai tasya prāyaṇaṃ vasanta udayanam //
16.1.33.a.d: शिशिरो वै तस्य प्रायणं वसन्त उदयनम् ॥
16.1.33.a.m: The cool season is indeed its starting point, the spring its conclusion.

16.1.34.a.s: ṛdhnuvante ya evaṃ vidvām̐saḥ śiśire dīkṣante vasanta uttiṣṭhantīti vijñāyate //
16.1.34.a.d: ऋध्नुवन्ते य एवं विद्वाम्̐सः शिशिरे दीक्षन्ते वसन्त उत्तिष्ठन्तीति विज्ञायते ॥
16.1.34.a.m: They thrive who, knowing thus, undergo consecration in the cool season and conclude in the spring—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

16.1.35.a.m: When six days have dawned in the waxing fortnight, those who are about to pile [the fire-altar] should undergo consecration.

16.1.36.a.s: saṃvādam̐ saṃnivapanaṃ kṛtvā dīkṣaṇīyāprabhṛtīni karmāṇi kurvate / ya ito 'gnir janiṣyate sa naḥ sarveṣām \\ yad anena yajñena jeṣyāmo 'nena satreṇa \\ iti //
16.1.36.a.d: संवादम्̐ संनिवपनं कृत्वा दीक्षणीयाप्रभृतीनि कर्माणि कुर्वते । य इतो ऽग्निर् जनिष्यते स नः सर्वेषाम् \\ यद् अनेन यज्ञेन जेष्यामो ऽनेन सत्रेण \\ इति ॥
16.1.36.a.m: Having made the agreement and the bringing together [of the fires], they perform the rites beginning with the consecration-offering, saying: "Which fire shall be produced from here, that belongs to all of us; what we shall win by this sacrifice, by this satra..."

16.1.36.b.s: atra saṃvāde brūyur adhvaryur gṛhapatiṃ dīkṣayitvā madhyataḥ kāriṇo dīkṣayati hotāraṃ brahmāṇam udgātāram / pratiprasthātādhvaryuṃ dīkṣayitvārdhino dīkṣayati maitrāvaruṇaṃ brāhmaṇāccham̐sinaṃ stotāram / neṣṭā pratiprasthātāraṃ dīkṣayitvā tṛtīyino dīkṣayati / acchāvākam āgnīdhraṃ pratihartāram / unnetā neṣṭāraṃ dīkṣayitvā pādino dīkṣayati grāvastutaṃ potāraṃ subrahmaṇyam / tatas taṃ pratiprasthātā dīkṣayati / anyo vā dīkṣito brāhmaṇa evam anupūrvaṃ dīkṣeran / nātantrībhāvād ekaikam apavargayati / anyagotravyavāyāt / samānagotrāṇām ārṣeyāṇām abhyāvartate / patnīnām ekasthāne patnīr dīkṣayanti / tāsāṃ yājamānair dharmā vyākhyātāḥ //
16.1.36.b.d: अत्र संवादे ब्रूयुर् अध्वर्युर् गृहपतिं दीक्षयित्वा मध्यतः कारिणो दीक्षयति होतारं ब्रह्माणम् उद्गातारम् । प्रतिप्रस्थाताध्वर्युं दीक्षयित्वार्धिनो दीक्षयति मैत्रावरुणं ब्राह्मणाच्छम्̐सिनं स्तोतारम् । नेष्टा प्रतिप्रस्थातारं दीक्षयित्वा तृतीयिनो दीक्षयति । अच्छावाकम् आग्नीध्रं प्रतिहर्तारम् । उन्नेता नेष्टारं दीक्षयित्वा पादिनो दीक्षयति ग्रावस्तुतं पोतारं सुब्रह्मण्यम् । ततस् तं प्रतिप्रस्थाता दीक्षयति । अन्यो वा दीक्षितो ब्राह्मण एवम् अनुपूर्वं दीक्षेरन् । नातन्त्रीभावाद् एकैकम् अपवर्गयति । अन्यगोत्रव्यवायात् । समानगोत्राणाम् आर्षेयाणाम् अभ्यावर्तते । पत्नीनाम् एकस्थाने पत्नीर् दीक्षयन्ति । तासां याजमानैर् धर्मा व्याख्याताः ॥
16.1.36.b.m: At this dialogue they should say: having consecrated the master of the house, the adhvaryu consecrates those who act in the middle: the hotṛ, the brahman, [and] the udgātṛ. Having consecrated the adhvaryu, the pratiprasthātṛ consecrates the half-share holders: the maitrāvaruṇa, the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, [and] the stotṛ. Having consecrated the pratiprasthātṛ, the neṣṭṛ consecrates the third-share holders: the acchāvāka, the āgnīdhra, [and] the pratihartṛ. Having consecrated the neṣṭṛ, the unnetṛ consecrates the quarter-share holders: the grāvastut, the potṛ, [and] the subrahmaṇya. Then the pratiprasthātṛ consecrates him. Or another consecrated brāhmaṇa [does so]. In this order they should be consecrated. Because it is not a state of separate frameworks, he finishes [consecrating] each one individually; because of the intervention of different gotras; among those of the same gotra, of common ṛṣi-ancestry, he returns [to the order]. In the place of the wives, they consecrate the wives. Their duties are explained by the duties of the sacrificer.

16.1.37.a.m: Some authorities prescribe a consecration day by day.

16.1.38.a.s: dvyahe tryaha iti krāmayati ā dvādaśāhāt //
16.1.38.a.d: द्व्यहे त्र्यह इति क्रामयति आ द्वादशाहात् ॥
16.1.38.a.m: He causes [the consecration] to proceed by two-day periods [or] three-day periods up to twelve days.

16.1.39.a.s: upasatsu trayodaśo dīkṣeta / tena brāhmaṇā bhavitavyam upadīkṣamāṇā agnīn upavapan nyupyātmasam̐skāreṇa prakrāmed dvādaśa dīkṣāḥ //
16.1.39.a.d: उपसत्सु त्रयोदशो दीक्षेत । तेन ब्राह्मणा भवितव्यम् उपदीक्षमाणा अग्नीन् उपवपन् न्युप्यात्मसम्̐स्कारेण प्रक्रामेद् द्वादश दीक्षाः ॥
16.1.39.a.m: During the upasads a thirteenth [person] may be consecrated. There should be a brāhmaṇa for that purpose; being additionally consecrated, strewing the fires, having poured them down, he should proceed through the twelve consecrations by means of personal purification.

16.1.40.a.m: There is no order to bring dakṣiṇā gifts when it has become a sacrificial session (satra).

16.1.42.a.m: He purchases King [Soma] sufficient for twelve days.

16.1.44.a.m: Following the upasads, he piles the fire-altar.

16.1.47.a.m: Up to a three-night period the fast-milk portions are four-teated.

16.1.49.a.s: bhūyo vratam icchan dadhna ekam̐ sruvam abhyunnayeta //
16.1.49.a.d: भूयो व्रतम् इच्छन् दध्न एकम्̐ स्रुवम् अभ्युन्नयेत ॥
16.1.49.a.m: If he desires more fast-food, he may ladle up one sruva-spoon of curd.

16.1.51.a.m: The two pressing boards are perforated through.

16.2.2.a.s: yadi yūpaikādaśinī syād anvaham ekaikaṃ yūpam̐ saṃminuyāt sarvān vā //
16.2.2.a.d: यदि यूपैकादशिनी स्याद् अन्वहम् एकैकं यूपम्̐ संमिनुयात् सर्वान् वा ॥
16.2.2.a.m: If there should be an eleven-post set, he should erect one sacrificial post day by day, or all of them [at once].

16.2.3.a.s: aupavasathye 'hany anvahaṃ mīyamāneṣv aharahar upaśayo 'bhyāvarteta // agniṣṭha evodayanīye paśum upākuryāt //
16.2.3.a.d: औपवसथ्ये ऽहन्य् अन्वहं मीयमानेष्व् अहरहर् उपशयो ऽभ्यावर्तेत ॥ अग्निष्ठ एवोदयनीये पशुम् उपाकुर्यात् ॥
16.2.3.a.m: On the day of preparation, while they are being measured day by day, the extra post would return day by day. Only at the post standing nearest the fire should he dedicate the animal on the concluding day.

16.2.4.a.m: On the next day the Jyotiṣṭoma is extended.

16.2.5.a.s: vaiśvānaro 'tirātraḥ upāvaharaṇakāle yāvān ekāhāyāptas tāvantam̐ rājānam anyasmin vāsasy upanahyopāvaharati //
16.2.5.a.d: वैश्वानरो ऽतिरात्रः उपावहरणकाले यावान् एकाहायाप्तस् तावन्तम्̐ राजानम् अन्यस्मिन् वासस्य् उपनह्योपावहरति ॥
16.2.5.a.m: An Atirātra dedicated to Vaiśvānara [is performed]. At the time of taking down [the soma], tying up in another cloth as much of King [Soma] as is sufficient for one day, he brings it down.

16.2.6.a.m: Having tied up the other portion again, he puts it away.

16.2.7.a.m: Thus it is done day by day. Day by day [take place] the yoking and unyoking [of the press].

16.2.8.a.d: प्रथमे ऽहनि युनक्ति । उत्तमे विमुञ्चतीत्य् एकेषाम् ॥
16.2.8.a.m: On the first day he yokes; on the last he unyokes—according to some teachers.

16.2.9.a.s: prāyaṇīyodayanīyayor atirātrayor daśame cāhni pṛśniprāṇagrahān gṛhṇāty abhiṣavamāṇena prākṛtasya yajurmānasya prathamena mantreṇa mītvā vāyur asi prāṇo nāma \\ iti daśabhir mantrair daśa pṛśnimānāni mimīte //
16.2.9.a.d: प्रायणीयोदयनीययोर् अतिरात्रयोर् दशमे चाह्नि पृश्निप्राणग्रहान् गृह्णात्य् अभिषवमाणेन प्राकृतस्य यजुर्मानस्य प्रथमेन मन्त्रेण मीत्वा वायुर् असि प्राणो नाम \\ इति दशभिर् मन्त्रैर् दश पृश्निमानानि मिमीते ॥
16.2.9.a.m: On the introductory and concluding Atirātra days and on the tenth day, he draws the pṛśni and prāṇa cups. Having measured with the first mantra of the standard yajus-measurement for the one being pressed, he measures out the ten pṛśni measures with the ten mantras: "You are Vāyu, Prāṇa by name...".

16.2.10.a.s: uttareṇottareṇa yajurmānena mītvā \\ ayaṃ puro bhuvas \\ iti daśabhir mantrair daśa prāṇagrahamānāni mimīte //
16.2.10.a.d: उत्तरेणोत्तरेण यजुर्मानेन मीत्वा \\ अयं पुरो भुवस् \\ इति दशभिर् मन्त्रैर् दश प्राणग्रहमानानि मिमीते ॥
16.2.10.a.m: Having measured with each subsequent yajus-measurement, he measures out the ten prāṇa-cup measures with the ten mantras: "This one in front, Bhuvas...".

16.2.11.a.m: He interweaves them with each subsequent yajus-measurement.

16.2.12.a.s: aindravāyavāgrau prāyaṇīyodayanīyāv atirātrau daśamaṃ cāhaḥ / athetareṣāṃ navānām aindravāyavāgraṃ prathamam ahar atha śukrāgram athāgrayaṇāgram evaṃ tryanīkās triḥ parivartante samūḍhaṃ chandasi //
16.2.12.a.d: ऐन्द्रवायवाग्रौ प्रायणीयोदयनीयाव् अतिरात्रौ दशमं चाहः । अथेतरेषां नवानाम् ऐन्द्रवायवाग्रं प्रथमम् अहर् अथ शुक्राग्रम् अथाग्रयणाग्रम् एवं त्र्यनीकास् त्रिः परिवर्तन्ते समूढं छन्दसि ॥
16.2.12.a.m: The introductory and concluding Atirātras and the tenth day have the Aindravāyava cup first. Now of the other nine days, the first day has the Aindravāyava first, then the Śukra first, then the Āgrayaṇa first; thus having three fronts they revolve three times in the samūḍha arrangement of metres.

16.2.13.a.s: atha vyūḍhaṃ chandasy aindravāyavāgrau prāyaṇīyodayanīyāv atirātrāv athetareṣāṃ daśānām aindravāyavāgraṃ prathamam ahaḥ / atha śukrāgram atha dve āgrayaṇāgre / athaindravāyavāgram atha dve śukrāgre / athāgrayaṇāgram atha dve aindra
16.2.13.a.d: अथ व्यूढं छन्दस्य् ऐन्द्रवायवाग्रौ प्रायणीयोदयनीयाव् अतिरात्राव् अथेतरेषां दशानाम् ऐन्द्रवायवाग्रं प्रथमम् अहः । अथ शुक्राग्रम् अथ द्वे आग्रयणाग्रे । अथैन्द्रवायवाग्रम् अथ द्वे शुक्राग्रे । अथाग्रयणाग्रम् अथ द्वे ऐन्द्र
16.2.13.a.m: Now in the vyūḍha arrangement of metres, the introductory and concluding Atirātras have the Aindravāyava first. Now of the other ten days, the first day has the Aindravāyava first, then the Śukra first, then two having the Āgrayaṇa first, then the Aindravāyava first, then two having the Śukra first, then the Āgrayaṇa first, then two having the Aindra[vāyava first]...

16.2.14.a.s: tatra bhakṣamantrāḥ pavamānābhimantraṇāni ca yenayena cchandasā nigadāś ca tasya sthāne tābhiḥ saṃnameta vyūhena vyākhyātam //
16.2.14.a.d: तत्र भक्षमन्त्राः पवमानाभिमन्त्रणानि च येनयेन च्छन्दसा निगदाश् च तस्य स्थाने ताभिः संनमेत व्यूहेन व्याख्यातम् ॥
16.2.14.a.m: There, the consumption mantras, the invocations over the purifying [soma], and the prose calls with whichever metre [they are associated], one should adapt to them in place of that [standard one]; it has been explained by the rearrangement (vyūha).

16.2.15.a.s: evam uttareṣu pṛṣṭhyāheṣu trīn atigrāhyān gṛhṇāti / āgneyam ekavim̐śe / aindraṃ triṇave / sauryaṃ trayastrim̐śe //
16.2.15.a.d: एवम् उत्तरेषु पृष्ठ्याहेषु त्रीन् अतिग्राह्यान् गृह्णाति । आग्नेयम् एकविम्̐शे । ऐन्द्रं त्रिणवे । सौर्यं त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शे ॥
16.2.15.a.m: In this manner, on the subsequent days of the Pṛṣṭhya [ṣaḍaha], he draws three atigrāhya cups: one dedicated to Agni on the twenty-one-fold [day], one dedicated to Indra on the twenty-seven-fold [day], and one dedicated to Sūrya on the thirty-three-fold [day].

16.2.16.a.s: pūrvasmiṃs tryahe vājasaneyinaḥ samāmananti / yatra gauravītam̐ sāma tatra sarvān pūrṇān grahān gṛhṇīyāt //
16.2.16.a.d: पूर्वस्मिंस् त्र्यहे वाजसनेयिनः समामनन्ति । यत्र गौरवीतम्̐ साम तत्र सर्वान् पूर्णान् ग्रहान् गृह्णीयात् ॥
16.2.16.a.m: The Vājasaneyins teach: In the first three-day period, wherever there is the Gauravīta sāman, there he should draw all the cups full.

16.2.17.a.s: atha paśukḷptir āgneyaṃ prāyaṇīyo 'tirātra ālabhante śvo bhūte sārasvatīṃ meṣīm / evam̐ hi vihatān aikādaśinān anvaham ālabhanta āgneyam udayanīye sauryaṃ brahmavarcasakāmānām //
16.2.17.a.d: अथ पशुकॢप्तिर् आग्नेयं प्रायणीयो ऽतिरात्र आलभन्ते श्वो भूते सारस्वतीं मेषीम् । एवम्̐ हि विहतान् ऐकादशिनान् अन्वहम् आलभन्त आग्नेयम् उदयनीये सौर्यं ब्रह्मवर्चसकामानाम् ॥
16.2.17.a.m: Now the arrangement of animals: on the introductory Atirātra they seize an animal dedicated to Agni; on the next day, a female sheep dedicated to Sarasvatī. In this way, indeed, distributed day by day, they seize the eleven animals; on the concluding day, one dedicated to Agni, [or] one dedicated to Sūrya for those who desire spiritual splendour.

16.2.18.a.d: दक्षिणाकाले ऽन्वहं द्वादश शतान्य् अहीनभूते ददाति ॥
16.2.18.a.m: At the time of the dakṣiṇā gifts, day by day he gives twelve hundred [cows], when it is an ahīna sacrifice.

16.2.19.a.s: satre tu dākṣiṇau homau hutvā \\ idam ahaṃ māṃ kalyāṇyai kīrtyai svargāya lokāya dakṣiṇāṃ nayāmi \\ iti yajamānāḥ kṛṣṇājināni dhūnvanta udañco dakṣiṇāpathenātiyanti //
16.2.19.a.d: सत्रे तु दाक्षिणौ होमौ हुत्वा \\ इदम् अहं मां कल्याण्यै कीर्त्यै स्वर्गाय लोकाय दक्षिणां नयामि \\ इति यजमानाः कृष्णाजिनानि धून्वन्त उदञ्चो दक्षिणापथेनातियन्ति ॥
16.2.19.a.m: In a sacrificial session (satra), however, having offered the two dakṣiṇā offerings, reciting: "Here I lead myself as dakṣiṇā toward auspicious fame, toward the heavenly world," the sacrificers, shaking their black-antelope skins, pass northward along the dakṣiṇā-path.

16.2.21.a.m: On the last day they throw away the black-buck horns.

16.2.23.a.s: pūrvasminn ahany uttarasmā ahne yajñāyajñīyaṃ prati vasatīvarīr gṛhṇāti //
16.2.23.a.d: पूर्वस्मिन्न् अहन्य् उत्तरस्मा अह्ने यज्ञायज्ञीयं प्रति वसतीवरीर् गृह्णाति ॥
16.2.23.a.m: On the preceding day, at the time of the Yajñāyajñīya [sāman], he draws the vasatīvarī waters for the following day.

16.2.24.a.s: pūrvasminn ahany uttarasmā ahne stotrīyam anurūpaṃ kṛtvā śam̐sati //
16.2.24.a.d: पूर्वस्मिन्न् अहन्य् उत्तरस्मा अह्ने स्तोत्रीयम् अनुरूपं कृत्वा शम्̐सति ॥
16.2.24.a.m: On the preceding day he recites [the śastra] for the following day after making the stotriya [hymn] into the anurūpa.

16.3.1.a.m: While the Atirātra is going on, he directs the milks.

16.3.2.a.s: śvaḥsutyām indrāgnibhyāṃ viśvebhyo devebhyo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ somapebhyaḥ somaṃ prabrūtāt \\ iti maitrāvaruṇenocyamāne svam agāraṃ praviśyāgnīdhraḥ śvaḥsutyām indrāgnibhyāṃ viśvebhyo devebhyo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ somapebhyaḥ somaṃ prabravīmi \ brahman vācaṃ yaccha \ subrahmaṇya subrahmaṇyām āhvaya \\ iti saṃpreṣyati //
16.3.2.a.d: श्वःसुत्याम् इन्द्राग्निभ्यां विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सोमपेभ्यः सोमं प्रब्रूतात् \\ इति मैत्रावरुणेनोच्यमाने स्वम् अगारं प्रविश्याग्नीध्रः श्वःसुत्याम् इन्द्राग्निभ्यां विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सोमपेभ्यः सोमं प्रब्रवीमि \ ब्रह्मन् वाचं यच्छ \ सुब्रह्मण्य सुब्रह्मण्याम् आह्वय \\ इति संप्रेष्यति ॥
16.3.2.a.m: When it is said by the maitrāvaruṇa: "For tomorrow's pressing announce the soma to Indra and Agni, to the All-Gods, to the soma-drinking brāhmaṇas!", the āgnīdhra, having entered his own shed, issues the direction: "For tomorrow's pressing I announce the soma to Indra and Agni, to the All-Gods, to the soma-drinking brāhmaṇas. O brahman, restrain your speech! O subrahmaṇya, call out the Subrahmaṇyā litany!"

16.3.3.a.s: adyasutyām etasminn ahani brūyāl lupyeta vā śvaḥsutyām itareṣu //
16.3.3.a.d: अद्यसुत्याम् एतस्मिन्न् अहनि ब्रूयाल् लुप्येत वा श्वःसुत्याम् इतरेषु ॥
16.3.3.a.m: On this day he should say, "for today's pressing," or on the other [days] "for tomorrow's pressing" may be omitted.

16.3.4.a.m: The day concludes with the offerings to the wives of the gods (patnīsaṃyājas).

16.3.5.a.m: When it is concluded, the brahman releases his speech.

16.3.6.a.m: They carry around water for the wives.

16.3.8.a.m: Having returned, they put sticks of firewood onto the āhavanīya fire.

16.3.9.a.m: Thus they should do day by day.

16.3.10.a.m: On that day [begins] the Pṛṣṭhya six-day period (ṣaḍaha).

16.3.11.a.m: It is a ninefold Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara sāman.

16.3.12.a.m: With the sound of a chariot he brings near (upākaroti) the stotra of the Māhendra cup.

16.3.13.a.m: The sound is a modification of the upākaraṇa mantra.

16.3.14.a.m: The fifteenfold [day] is an Ukthya having the Bṛhat sāman.

16.3.15.a.m: With the sound of a war-drum he brings near the stotra of the Māhendra cup.

16.3.16.a.s: yadi stanayitnur bhavati sa eva syād upākaraṇamantrasya śabdo vikāraḥ //
16.3.16.a.d: यदि स्तनयित्नुर् भवति स एव स्याद् उपाकरणमन्त्रस्य शब्दो विकारः ॥
16.3.16.a.m: If there should be thunder, that itself would be the modification of the sound of the upākaraṇa mantra.

16.3.17.a.m: The seventeenfold [day] is an Ukthya having the Vairūpa sāman.

16.3.18.a.m: With a whisk (ādhāva) he brings near the stotra of the Māhendra cup.

16.3.19.a.s: barhiṣo vikāras tasminn upākṛte prastuta udgātādhāvena dhunute //
16.3.19.a.d: बर्हिषो विकारस् तस्मिन्न् उपाकृते प्रस्तुत उद्गाताधावेन धुनुते ॥
16.3.19.a.m: It is a modification of the barhis grass; when that is brought near and the prastāva has been chanted, the udgātṛ shakes [it] with the whisk.

16.3.20.a.m: [The fourth day is] a twenty-one-fold ṣoḍaśin having the Vairāja sāman.

16.3.21.a.m: There is a nyūṅkha; during the haviṣkṛt call, the call, and the counter-call, he performs the nyūṅkha at the response.

16.3.22.a.s: araṇībhyāṃ māhendrasya stotram upākaroti barhiṣo vikāraḥ //
16.3.22.a.d: अरणीभ्यां माहेन्द्रस्य स्तोत्रम् उपाकरोति बर्हिषो विकारः ॥
16.3.22.a.m: With two fire-churning sticks he introduces the chant of the Māhendra cup; this is a modification of the sacrificial grass.

16.3.23.a.m: When it has been introduced and the prologue chanted,

16.3.24.a.s: udgātā dakṣiṇam ūrum avakābhir avacchādya tatrāraṇī saṃnidhāyāgniṃ manthati //
16.3.24.a.d: उद्गाता दक्षिणम् ऊरुम् अवकाभिर् अवच्छाद्य तत्रारणी संनिधायाग्निं मन्थति ॥
16.3.24.a.m: the udgātṛ, having covered his right thigh with avakā plants and placed the two fire-churning sticks there, churns fire.

16.3.25.a.m: Over the generated [fire], the udgātṛ utters the sound hiṃ and hands it to the prastotṛ.

16.3.27.a.s: tam̐ so 'greṇa dhiṣṇiyān paryāhṛtyāhavanīye 'nuprahṛtya preddho agne dīdihi \\ iti virājābhijuhoti //
16.3.27.a.d: तम्̐ सो ऽग्रेण धिष्णियान् पर्याहृत्याहवनीये ऽनुप्रहृत्य प्रेद्धो अग्ने दीदिहि \\ इति विराजाभिजुहोति ॥
16.3.27.a.m: Having carried it around in front of the dhiṣṇya hearths and cast it into the āhavanīya fire, he offers upon it with a Virāj verse: "Kindled, O Agni, shine brightly!"

16.3.28.a.m: [The fifth day is] a twenty-seven-fold ukthya having the Śākvara sāman.

16.3.29.a.s: adbhir avakāvās tābhir māhendrasya stotram upākaroti / barhiṣo vikāras tasminn upākṛte prastute //
16.3.29.a.d: अद्भिर् अवकावास् ताभिर् माहेन्द्रस्य स्तोत्रम् उपाकरोति । बर्हिषो विकारस् तस्मिन्न् उपाकृते प्रस्तुते ॥
16.3.29.a.m: With water containing avakā plants he introduces the chant of the Māhendra cup; this is a modification of the sacrificial grass. When it has been introduced and the prologue chanted,

16.3.30.a.s: tisraḥ saharṣabhā gāvo 'greṇa sado 'pareṇāgnīdhram udīcīnaṃ dakṣiṇāpathenātikramayanti //
16.3.30.a.d: तिस्रः सहर्षभा गावो ऽग्रेण सदो ऽपरेणाग्नीध्रम् उदीचीनं दक्षिणापथेनातिक्रमयन्ति ॥
16.3.30.a.m: they cause three cows accompanied by a bull to cross from south to north in front of the sadas and to the west of the Āgnīdhra along the southern pathway.

16.3.31.a.m: [The sixth day is] a thirty-three-fold ukthya having the Raivata sāman.

16.3.33.a.m: There is a self-performed ṛtuyāja offering.

16.3.34.a.s: adhvaryū yajatam ity ucyamāne havirdhāne praviśyādhvaryuḥ praiṣottarayarcā yajati ṛguttareṇa vā praiṣeṇa //
16.3.34.a.d: अध्वर्यू यजतम् इत्य् उच्यमाने हविर्धाने प्रविश्याध्वर्युः प्रैषोत्तरयर्चा यजति ऋगुत्तरेण वा प्रैषेण ॥
16.3.34.a.m: When "O two adhvaryus, offer!" is said, the adhvaryu, entering the havirdhāna shed, offers with a verse whose direction follows, or with a direction whose verse follows.

16.3.35.a.s: aśvinā pibataṃ sutam \\ dīdyagnī śucivratā / \ ṛtunā yajñavāhasā / \ ṛtunā somaṃ pibatam \\ vauṣaṭ \\ iti yady avyūḍhaḥ //
16.3.35.a.d: अश्विना पिबतं सुतम् \\ दीद्यग्नी शुचिव्रता । \ ऋतुना यज्ञवाहसा । \ ऋतुना सोमं पिबतम् \\ वौषट् \\ इति यद्य् अव्यूढः ॥
16.3.35.a.m: If it is not transposed: "O Aśvins, drink the pressed soma, O gleaming with fires, pure in vows, / In due season, O conveyors of the sacrifice! / In due season drink the soma, vauṣaṭ!"

16.3.36.a.s: vyūḍhe tu \\ arvāñcam adya yayyaṃ nṛvāhaṇam \\ rathaṃ yuñjāthām iha vāṃ vimocanam / \ pṛṅktam̐ havīm̐ṣi madhunā hi kaṃ gatam \ athā somaṃ pibataṃ vājinīvasū / \ ṛtunā somaṃ pibatam \\ vauṣaṭ \\ iti tasya pracaritaṃ marutvatīyair bhavati //
16.3.36.a.d: व्यूढे तु \\ अर्वाञ्चम् अद्य यय्यं नृवाहणम् \\ रथं युञ्जाथाम् इह वां विमोचनम् । \ पृङ्क्तम्̐ हवीम्̐षि मधुना हि कं गतम् \ अथा सोमं पिबतं वाजिनीवसू । \ ऋतुना सोमं पिबतम् \\ वौषट् \\ इति तस्य प्रचरितं मरुत्वतीयैर् भवति ॥
16.3.36.a.m: When it is transposed, however: "Hitherward today your chariot bringing men, fit to go, / harness ye; here is your unyoking. / Mix the oblations with honey, for go ye to delight, / then drink the soma, O possessors of abundant wealth! / In due season drink the soma, vauṣaṭ!" With this, its performance belongs with the Marutvatīya cups.

16.3.37.a.s: yat prāṅ māhendrāt tasmin kṛte pratiprasthātāpareṇāgnīdhram udīcīṃ tantiṃ vitatya tasyāṃ vatsān badhnāti //
16.3.37.a.d: यत् प्राङ् माहेन्द्रात् तस्मिन् कृते प्रतिप्रस्थातापरेणाग्नीध्रम् उदीचीं तन्तिं वितत्य तस्यां वत्सान् बध्नाति ॥
16.3.37.a.m: Whatever [rites take place] prior to the Māhendra [stotra], when that is completed, the pratiprasthātṛ, having stretched a northward tether-rope west of the Āgnīdhra, binds calves to it.

16.3.38.a.m: South of the mārjālīya, they shut in the mothers [the cows].

16.3.39.a.s: barhiḥsthāne 'dbhir dūrvāvāstābhir māhendrasya stotram upākaroti / barhiṣo vikāraḥ //
16.3.39.a.d: बर्हिःस्थाने ऽद्भिर् दूर्वावास्ताभिर् माहेन्द्रस्य स्तोत्रम् उपाकरोति । बर्हिषो विकारः ॥
16.3.39.a.m: In place of the sacrificial grass, he introduces the chant of the Māhendra cup with water containing dūrvā grass; this is a modification of the sacrificial grass.

16.3.40.a.s: tasminn upākṛte prastute vatsān pramucya mātṛbhiḥ sam̐sṛjyodīcīras tasya dakṣiṇāpathena saṃcāryamānā ativitsanti ( saṃtiṣṭhate pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ ) //
16.3.40.a.d: तस्मिन्न् उपाकृते प्रस्तुते वत्सान् प्रमुच्य मातृभिः सम्̐सृज्योदीचीरस् तस्य दक्षिणापथेन संचार्यमाना अतिवित्सन्ति ( संतिष्ठते पृष्ठ्यः षडहः ) ॥
16.3.40.a.m: When it has been introduced and the prologue chanted, having released the calves and united them with their mothers, [the cows,] led northward across along the southern pathway, bypass [the shed]. (The Pṛṣṭhya six-day period is concluded.)

16.4.1.a.s: sam̐sthite pṛṣṭhye ṣaḍahe / ghṛtaṃ madhu vā prāśnanti //
16.4.1.a.d: सम्̐स्थिते पृष्ठ्ये षडहे । घृतं मधु वा प्राश्नन्ति ॥
16.4.1.a.m: When the Pṛṣṭhya six-day period has concluded, they partake of ghee or honey.

16.4.2.a.m: Day after day the three Chandoma days are ukthya sacrifices.

16.4.3.a.s: caturvim̐śaś catuścatvārim̐śo 'ṣṭācatvārim̐śaś caturvim̐śam avivākyam // daśamam ahar agniṣṭomaḥ somo rathaṃtarasāmā //
16.4.3.a.d: चतुर्विम्̐शश् चतुश्चत्वारिम्̐शो ऽष्टाचत्वारिम्̐शश् चतुर्विम्̐शम् अविवाक्यम् ॥ दशमम् अहर् अग्निष्टोमः सोमो रथंतरसामा ॥
16.4.3.a.m: The twenty-four-fold, the forty-four-fold, [and] the forty-eight-fold; the twenty-four-fold day is not to be spoken about. The tenth day is an agniṣṭoma soma sacrifice having the Rathaṃtara sāman.

16.4.4.a.m: Here no one speaks discordant words to anyone.

16.4.5.a.s: ye bāhyā dṛśīkavaḥ syus te vibrūyur yadi tatra na vindeyur antaḥsadasād vyucyam //
16.4.5.a.d: ये बाह्या दृशीकवः स्युस् ते विब्रूयुर् यदि तत्र न विन्देयुर् अन्तःसदसाद् व्युच्यम् ॥
16.4.5.a.m: Those who may be outsiders possessing clear sight, they may speak out; if they do not find any there, it is to be spoken by one within the sadas.

16.4.6.a.s: yadi tatra na vindeyur gṛhapatinā vyucyam //
16.4.6.a.d: यदि तत्र न विन्देयुर् गृहपतिना व्युच्यम् ॥
16.4.6.a.m: If they do not find one there, it is to be spoken by the master of the house.

16.4.7.a.m: Having spoken an anuṣṭubh verse to the master of the house, he should speak it.

16.4.8.a.s: yasminn upahvayaty etāv api vā tenaiva sahānuṣṭubham̐ saṃpādayet // dvayor etad ahaḥ samidha āharanti //
16.4.8.a.d: यस्मिन्न् उपह्वयत्य् एताव् अपि वा तेनैव सहानुष्टुभम्̐ संपादयेत् ॥ द्वयोर् एतद् अहः समिध आहरन्ति ॥
16.4.8.a.m: In which he invites, these two also, or along with that he should accomplish the anuṣṭubh. On this day they bring two kinds of firewood:

16.4.11.a.m: North of the āhavanīya fire, they set down those of udumbara wood.

16.4.12.a.s: amūr yā upa sūrye \ yābhir vā sūryaḥ saha / \ tā no hinvanty adhvaram \ iha ratir \ iha rantir \ iha ramadhvam \ iha rantir \ iha ramatir \ iha ramadhvam \ iha vo ramatiḥ / \ upasṛjaṃ dharuṇam iti dvābhyāṃ gārhapatye juhoti //
16.4.12.a.d: अमूर् या उप सूर्ये \ याभिर् वा सूर्यः सह । \ ता नो हिन्वन्त्य् अध्वरम् \ इह रतिर् \ इह रन्तिर् \ इह रमध्वम् \ इह रन्तिर् \ इह रमतिर् \ इह रमध्वम् \ इह वो रमतिः । \ उपसृजं धरुणम् इति द्वाभ्यां गार्हपत्ये जुहोति ॥
16.4.12.a.m: With two [verses], "Those [waters] which are near the sun, or with which the sun is associated, may they speed our sacrifice; here is rest, here is delight, here delight yourselves; here is delight, here is resting, here delight yourselves, here is your resting; emitting the supporter...", he offers into the gārhapatya fire.

16.4.13.a.s: ayam̐ sahasramānavo dṛśaḥ kavīnāṃ matir jyotir vidharmā \ dadhruḥ samīcīr uṣasaḥ samairayat \\ arepasaḥ samokasaḥ saretasaḥ sacetasaḥ svaramanyumantaś cidākos \\ ity aticchandasarcāhavanīyam upatiṣṭhante //
16.4.13.a.d: अयम्̐ सहस्रमानवो दृशः कवीनां मतिर् ज्योतिर् विधर्मा \ दध्रुः समीचीर् उषसः समैरयत् \\ अरेपसः समोकसः सरेतसः सचेतसः स्वरमन्युमन्तश् चिदाकोस् \\ इत्य् अतिच्छन्दसर्चाहवनीयम् उपतिष्ठन्ते ॥
16.4.13.a.m: With the aticchandas verse, "This insight of the poets, possessing a thousand minds, light, distributor, he directed the matching dawns, spotless, having the same abode, of the same seed, of common mind, possessing heaven's ardour...", they attend upon the āhavanīya fire.

16.4.14.a.m: They glide forward for the mind-cup for Prajāpati.

16.4.15.a.s: prasṛpteṣu \\ anayā tvā pātreṇa \\ iti pṛthivīṃ manasā dhyāyan prajāpataye manave juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmi \\ iti prājāpatyaṃ manograhaṃ gṛhṇāti / yathārūpam ākāśāt / tārtīyasavanikād vā somāt pariśāyayed yāvān ekasmai camasagaṇāyāptaḥ //
16.4.15.a.d: प्रसृप्तेषु \\ अनया त्वा पात्रेण \\ इति पृथिवीं मनसा ध्यायन् प्रजापतये मनवे जुष्टं गृह्णामि \\ इति प्राजापत्यं मनोग्रहं गृह्णाति । यथारूपम् आकाशात् । तार्तीयसवनिकाद् वा सोमात् परिशाययेद् यावान् एकस्मै चमसगणायाप्तः ॥
16.4.15.a.m: When they have glided forward, meditating in mind upon the earth with "With this vessel...", he draws the mind-cup for Prajāpati with "I take you, agreeable to Prajāpati, the wise Manu," according to form from the ether; or he should leave over from the soma of the third pressing as much as is sufficient for one set of goblets.

16.4.16.a.s: tasmād vopām̐śupātreṇa gṛhṇīyād dhotṛcamasamukhyām̐ś camasān unnayati //
16.4.16.a.d: तस्माद् वोपाम्̐शुपात्रेण गृह्णीयाद् धोतृचमसमुख्याम्̐श् चमसान् उन्नयति ॥
16.4.16.a.m: Or from that he should draw with the upāṃśu cup; he draws the goblets headed by the hotṛ's goblet.

16.4.18.a.m: All of it is performed in the mind.

16.4.19.a.m: He introduces the chant in the mind.

16.4.23.a.m: In the mind he responds six times to the three Sārparājñī verses.

16.4.24.a.s: yady ardharcaśaḥ śam̐sati navakṛtvo yadi pacchas \\ om̐ hotar iti daśahotuḥ pratigaraḥ / tathā \\ iti caturhotuḥ / om iti pañcahotuḥ / tathā \\ iti ṣaḍḍhotuḥ / arātsma hotar iti saptahotuḥ //
16.4.24.a.d: यद्य् अर्धर्चशः शम्̐सति नवकृत्वो यदि पच्छस् \\ ओम्̐ होतर् इति दशहोतुः प्रतिगरः । तथा \\ इति चतुर्होतुः । ओम् इति पञ्चहोतुः । तथा \\ इति षड्ढोतुः । अरात्स्म होतर् इति सप्तहोतुः ॥
16.4.24.a.m: If he recites by half-verses, [he responds] nine times if by quarter-verses. "Om, O hotṛ" is the response to the daśahotṛ mantra; "So be it" to the caturhotṛ; "Om" to the pañcahotṛ; "So be it" to the ṣaḍḍhotṛ; "We have succeeded, O hotṛ" to the saptahotṛ.

16.4.25.a.s: manasāśrutapratyāśrute yājyā saṃpraiṣo vaṣaṭkāro bhakṣamantraś ca //
16.4.25.a.d: मनसाश्रुतप्रत्याश्रुते याज्या संप्रैषो वषट्कारो भक्षमन्त्रश् च ॥
16.4.25.a.m: In the mind are the call and the counter-call, the offering verse, the ritual direction, the vaṣaṭ-call, and the consumption mantra.

16.4.26.a.s: hutvā haranti bhakṣante yat samīkṣante sasamupahavadharmā bhavanti / gṛhapatiṃ paryupaviśya pṛcchanti //
16.4.26.a.d: हुत्वा हरन्ति भक्षन्ते यत् समीक्षन्ते ससमुपहवधर्मा भवन्ति । गृहपतिं पर्युपविश्य पृच्छन्ति ॥
16.4.26.a.m: Having offered, they carry [the cups] away and consume; that they look at one another has the nature of a mutual invitation. Sitting around the master of the house, they ask:

16.4.27.a.s: yad daśahotāraḥ satram āsata / kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvan / kena prajā asṛjanta \\ ity adhvaryuḥ pṛcchati //
16.4.27.a.d: यद् दशहोतारः सत्रम् आसत । केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन् । केन प्रजा असृजन्त \\ इत्य् अध्वर्युः पृच्छति ॥
16.4.27.a.m: "When the performers of the ten-hotṛ sacrifice held the satra, by what master of the house did they prosper, by whom did they create creatures?" asks the adhvaryu.

16.4.28.a.s: prajāpatinā vai te gṛhapatinārdhnuvan tena prajā asṛjanta \\ iti gṛhapatiḥ pratyāha //
16.4.28.a.d: प्रजापतिना वै ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन् तेन प्रजा असृजन्त \\ इति गृहपतिः प्रत्याह ॥
16.4.28.a.m: "Indeed, by Prajāpati as master of the house they prospered, through him they created creatures," the master of the house replies.

16.4.29.a.s: yac caturhotāraḥ satram āsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvan kenauṣadhīr asṛjanta \\ iti brahmā pṛcchati / somena vai te gṛhapatinārdhnuvan tenauṣadhīr asṛjanta \\ iti gṛhapatiḥ pratyāha //
16.4.29.a.d: यच् चतुर्होतारः सत्रम् आसत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन् केनौषधीर् असृजन्त \\ इति ब्रह्मा पृच्छति । सोमेन वै ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन् तेनौषधीर् असृजन्त \\ इति गृहपतिः प्रत्याह ॥
16.4.29.a.m: "When the performers of the four-hotṛ sacrifice held the satra, by what master of the house did they prosper, by whom did they create plants?" asks the brahman priest. "Indeed, by Soma as master of the house they prospered, through him they created plants," the master of the house replies.

16.4.30.a.s: yat pañcahotāraḥ satram āsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvan kenaibhyo lokebhyo 'surān prāṇudanta / kenaiṣāṃ paśūn avṛñjata \\ iti hotā pṛcchati / agninā vai te gṛhapatinārdhnuvan tenaibhyo lokebhyo 'surān prāṇudanta tenaiṣāṃ paśūn avṛñjata \\ iti gṛhapatiḥ pratyāha //
16.4.30.a.d: यत् पञ्चहोतारः सत्रम् आसत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन् केनैभ्यो लोकेभ्यो ऽसुरान् प्राणुदन्त । केनैषां पशून् अवृञ्जत \\ इति होता पृच्छति । अग्निना वै ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन् तेनैभ्यो लोकेभ्यो ऽसुरान् प्राणुदन्त तेनैषां पशून् अवृञ्जत \\ इति गृहपतिः प्रत्याह ॥
16.4.30.a.m: "When the performers of the five-hotṛ sacrifice held the satra, by what master of the house did they prosper, by whom did they drive the Asuras away from these worlds, by whom did they seize their cattle?" asks the hotṛ. "Indeed, by Agni as master of the house they prospered, through him they drove the Asuras away from these worlds, through him they seized their cattle," the master of the house replies.

16.4.31.a.s: yat ṣaḍḍhotāraḥ satram āsata kene te gṛhapatinārdhnuvan kenartūn akalpayanta \\ iti hotṛkāḥ pṛcchanti / dhātrā vai te gṛhapatinārdhnuvan tenartūn akalpayanta \\ iti gṛhapatiḥ pratyāha //
16.4.31.a.d: यत् षड्ढोतारः सत्रम् आसत केने ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन् केनर्तून् अकल्पयन्त \\ इति होतृकाः पृच्छन्ति । धात्रा वै ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन् तेनर्तून् अकल्पयन्त \\ इति गृहपतिः प्रत्याह ॥
16.4.31.a.m: "When the performers of the six-hotṛ sacrifice held the satra, by what master of the house did they prosper, by whom did they arrange the seasons?" ask the hotṛ's assistants. "Indeed, by Dhātṛ as master of the house they prospered, through him they arranged the seasons," the master of the house replies.

16.4.32.a.s: yat saptahotāraḥ satram āsata kena te gṛhapatinārdhnuvan kena suvar āyan kenemām̐l lokān samatanvan \\ ity udgātā pṛcchati / aryamṇā te gṛhapatinārdhnuvan tena suvar āyan tenemām̐l lokān samatanvan \\ iti gṛhapatiḥ pratyāha //
16.4.32.a.d: यत् सप्तहोतारः सत्रम् आसत केन ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन् केन सुवर् आयन् केनेमाम्̐ल् लोकान् समतन्वन् \\ इत्य् उद्गाता पृच्छति । अर्यम्णा ते गृहपतिनार्ध्नुवन् तेन सुवर् आयन् तेनेमाम्̐ल् लोकान् समतन्वन् \\ इति गृहपतिः प्रत्याह ॥
16.4.32.a.m: "When the saptahotṛs performed the sacrificial session, through what master of the house did they prosper? Through what did they reach heaven? Through what did they pervade these worlds?" the udgātṛ asks. "Through Aryaman as the master of the house did they prosper; through him they reached heaven; through him they pervaded these worlds," the master of the house replies.

16.4.34.a.s: akuśalo 'yaṃ prajāpatir yo dam̐śamaśakān sam̐sṛjed yaḥ stenān iti //
16.4.34.a.d: अकुशलो ऽयं प्रजापतिर् यो दम्̐शमशकान् सम्̐सृजेद् यः स्तेनान् इति ॥
16.4.34.a.m: "This Prajāpati is unskilled, who created biting flies and mosquitoes, who [created] thieves," [they say].

16.4.35.a.s: api vā prajāpatiparivādānāṃ mantrān adhīyate yad araṇyāni prajāpatiḥ \ puraś ca sasṛje girīn // \ kartāgniś ca tad bhadram \\ yad bhadraṃ tan ma ā suva // \ yad ūṣā tamasā yuktvā \ dine tekṣṇiṣṭham ātapat / \ ambhaś cātyati gharmaś ca \ tathā tat te prajāpatiḥ // \ yat stenān yad vṛkān dam̐śān \ maśakān yad adyāśavaḥ / \ tad u te vṛjinaṃ teṣām \\ tad viṣaṃ tena te 'mṛtam // \ prajāpatiṃ daśamam ahar bhajadhvam \\ matiṃ kavīnām ṛṣabhaṃ janānām / \ suṣukṣitim̐ sudraviṇaṃ dadhānas \\ vipāpmā loke nidadhāti devayum ity etaiḥ parivadeyuḥ //
16.4.35.a.d: अपि वा प्रजापतिपरिवादानां मन्त्रान् अधीयते यद् अरण्यानि प्रजापतिः \ पुरश् च ससृजे गिरीन् ॥ \ कर्ताग्निश् च तद् भद्रम् \\ यद् भद्रं तन् म आ सुव ॥ \ यद् ऊषा तमसा युक्त्वा \ दिने तेक्ष्णिष्ठम् आतपत् । \ अम्भश् चात्यति घर्मश् च \ तथा तत् ते प्रजापतिः ॥ \ यत् स्तेनान् यद् वृकान् दम्̐शान् \ मशकान् यद् अद्याशवः । \ तद् उ ते वृजिनं तेषाम् \\ तद् विषं तेन ते ऽमृतम् ॥ \ प्रजापतिं दशमम् अहर् भजध्वम् \\ मतिं कवीनाम् ऋषभं जनानाम् । \ सुषुक्षितिम्̐ सुद्रविणं दधानस् \\ विपाप्मा लोके निदधाति देवयुम् इत्य् एतैः परिवदेयुः ॥
16.4.35.a.m: Or rather, they recite the mantras of reproach to Prajāpati: "When Prajāpati created the forests, / and the cities and the mountains; / Agni was the doer, and that was good; / what is good, impel that to me. / When the dawn, united with darkness, / burned most intensely by day, / and water and heat were excessive, / thus did Prajāpati do to you. / When thieves, when wolves, / mosquitoes, when ravenous flies; / that indeed was their crookedness, / that was their poison, through which is your nectar. / Resort to Prajāpati on the tenth day, / the thought of the sages, the bull among men; / granting good dwelling and good wealth, / freed from evil in the world, he places him who seeks the gods." With these [verses] they should reproach [him].

16.4.37.a.d: अदो नो ऽस्तु \\ इति यत्कामा भवन्ति ॥
16.4.37.a.m: "May that be ours," whatever desire they have.

16.5.1.a.s: api vā yad evaitad bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ \ suprajāḥ prajayā bhūyāsam̐ suvīro vīraiḥ suvarcā varcasā supoṣaḥ poṣair iti tena caiṣām̐ sarve kāmā avaruddhā bhavanti //
16.5.1.a.d: अपि वा यद् एवैतद् भूर् भुवः सुवः \ सुप्रजाः प्रजया भूयासम्̐ सुवीरो वीरैः सुवर्चा वर्चसा सुपोषः पोषैर् इति तेन चैषाम्̐ सर्वे कामा अवरुद्धा भवन्ति ॥
16.5.1.a.m: Or, [with] this very [formula]: "Earth, atmosphere, heaven! May I be rich in offspring through offspring, rich in heroes through heroes, rich in luster through luster, rich in nourishment through nourishments!" And by this, all their desires are secured.

16.5.2.a.s: yathādhiṣṇiyaṃ patnīr vyāsādya dvārau saṃvṛtyāthaibhyo vācam upākaroti //
16.5.2.a.d: यथाधिष्णियं पत्नीर् व्यासाद्य द्वारौ संवृत्याथैभ्यो वाचम् उपाकरोति ॥
16.5.2.a.m: Having seated the wives according to their respective hearth-mounds and closed the two doors, he then initiates speech for them.

16.5.3.a.s: iha dhṛtir \ iha vidhṛtir \ iha rantir \ iha ramatir ity audumbarīṃ pariṣvajanta udarair ivopaspṛśantaḥ samanvārabhyaudumbarīm āsate yuvaṃ tam indrāparvatā puroyudhā \ yo naḥ pṛtanyād apa taṃtam id dhataṃ \ vajreṇa taṃtam id dhataṃ / \ dūre ca tāṃ yac chatsat \\ gahanaṃ yad inakṣat \\ asmākam̐ śatrūn pari śūra viśvatas \\ darmā darṣiṣṭha viśvatas \\ iti samanvārabdhā sarvān uttarasya havirdhānasya dakṣiṇaiḥ pāṇibhiḥ kaṭām̐s tejanībhir vā tiṣṭhamānā atiyanti // prāñca īṣad gatvā vāg aitu vāg vāg aitu vāg upaitu vāk samaitūpamaitu vāg \ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar iti pañca vacām̐si vyāharanti //
16.5.3.a.d: इह धृतिर् \ इह विधृतिर् \ इह रन्तिर् \ इह रमतिर् इत्य् औदुम्बरीं परिष्वजन्त उदरैर् इवोपस्पृशन्तः समन्वारभ्यौदुम्बरीम् आसते युवं तम् इन्द्रापर्वता पुरोयुधा \ यो नः पृतन्याद् अप तंतम् इद् धतं \ वज्रेण तंतम् इद् धतं । \ दूरे च तां यच् छत्सत् \\ गहनं यद् इनक्षत् \\ अस्माकम्̐ शत्रून् परि शूर विश्वतस् \\ दर्मा दर्षिष्ठ विश्वतस् \\ इति समन्वारब्धा सर्वान् उत्तरस्य हविर्धानस्य दक्षिणैः पाणिभिः कटाम्̐स् तेजनीभिर् वा तिष्ठमाना अतियन्ति ॥ प्राञ्च ईषद् गत्वा वाग् ऐतु वाग् वाग् ऐतु वाग् उपैतु वाक् समैतूपमैतु वाग् \ भूर् भुवः सुवर् इति पञ्च वचाम्̐सि व्याहरन्ति ॥
16.5.3.a.m: With "Here is support, here is separation, here is delight, here is resting," embracing the post of udumbara wood, touching it as it were with their bellies, holding on together to the post of udumbara wood, they sit. With "O Indra and Parvata, fighters in the van, him / who would wage war against us, slay that very one, / slay that very one with the thunderbolt; / and afar, where he would sing, / what deep place he would penetrate; / our enemies all around, o hero, / breaker, most destructive, from all sides," holding on together, they step beyond all the mats of the northern soma-cart on the south with their hands or with reed stalks while standing. Having moved slightly eastward, they utter the five utterances: "May speech come! Speech! May speech come! May speech approach! May speech unite! May speech approach! Earth, atmosphere, heaven!"

16.5.4.a.m: When the sun is over the trees, they release speech with the subrahmaṇyā litany.

16.5.5.a.m: The son of the udumbara woman puts on pieces of firewood.

16.5.6.a.m: On the next day is the udayanīyā; its form is already explained.

16.5.7.a.m: The prāyaṇīyā and the udayanīyā—here there are no continuities of an ahīna sacrifice.

16.5.8.a.s: pūrvasminn ahany uttarasmā ahne yajñāyajñīyaṃ prati vasatīvarīr gṛhṇāti //
16.5.8.a.d: पूर्वस्मिन्न् अहन्य् उत्तरस्मा अह्ने यज्ञायज्ञीयं प्रति वसतीवरीर् गृह्णाति ॥
16.5.8.a.m: On the previous day, for the next day, he draws the vasatīvarī waters in time with the yajñāyajñīya sāmān.

16.5.9.a.m: These are the continuities of an ahīna sacrifice.

16.5.10.a.s: uto tāny eva dīkṣitavasanāni paridhāya pracareyuḥ //
16.5.10.a.d: उतो तान्य् एव दीक्षितवसनानि परिधाय प्रचरेयुः ॥
16.5.10.a.m: And they should proceed having put on those very garments of the consecrated.

16.5.11.a.m: At the time of shaving, when it has become a sacrificial session, they have their heads shaved together with the topknot.

16.5.12.a.s: udavasānīyeṣv anyān ṛtvijo vṛtvā tān vā jyotiṣṭomenāgniṣṭomena pṛṣṭhaśamanīyena sahasradakṣiṇena sarvavedasadakṣiṇena vā nānā yajeran //
16.5.12.a.d: उदवसानीयेष्व् अन्यान् ऋत्विजो वृत्वा तान् वा ज्योतिष्टोमेनाग्निष्टोमेन पृष्ठशमनीयेन सहस्रदक्षिणेन सर्ववेदसदक्षिणेन वा नाना यजेरन् ॥
16.5.12.a.m: At the udavasānīyā rites, having chosen other priests, or they should sacrifice separately with those [former participants as priests] with a jyotiṣṭoma agniṣṭoma having the pṛṣṭha-śamanīya, with a thousand cows as the sacrificial gift, or with one's entire property as the sacrificial gift.

16.5.14.a.s: gavāmayanena prajāpatiṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchanty eṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti //
16.5.14.a.d: गवामयनेन प्रजापतिं भूमानं गच्छन्त्य् एषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठन्ति ॥
16.5.14.a.m: By means of the Gavāmayana, they go to Prajāpati, to abundance; they become established in these worlds.

16.5.15.a.m: Its procedure has been explained by means of the twelve-day sacrifice when it has become a sacrificial session.

16.5.16.a.m: They should undergo consecration four days before the full-moon day,

16.5.18.a.s: prāyaṇīyo 'tirātraś caturvim̐śa ukthya ārambhaṇīyas trivṛddhā te śaye dve ahanī bhavataḥ / jyotir agniṣṭomo rathaṃtarasāmā gaur ukthyo bṛhatsāmā āyur ukthyo rathaṃtarasāmā gaur ukthyo bṛhatsāmāyur ukthyo rathaṃtarasāmā jyotir agniṣṭomo bṛhatsāmeti //
16.5.18.a.d: प्रायणीयो ऽतिरात्रश् चतुर्विम्̐श उक्थ्य आरम्भणीयस् त्रिवृद्धा ते शये द्वे अहनी भवतः । ज्योतिर् अग्निष्टोमो रथंतरसामा गौर् उक्थ्यो बृहत्सामा आयुर् उक्थ्यो रथंतरसामा गौर् उक्थ्यो बृहत्सामायुर् उक्थ्यो रथंतरसामा ज्योतिर् अग्निष्टोमो बृहत्सामेति ॥
16.5.18.a.m: There are the introductory atirātra, the twenty-four-versed ukthya, the introductory day, the threefold-praised day, [and] those two stationary days: the jyotis agniṣṭoma with the Rathaṃtara sāmān, the go ukthya with the Bṛhat sāmān, the āyus ukthya with the Rathaṃtara sāmān, the go ukthya with the Bṛhat sāmān, the āyus ukthya with the Rathaṃtara sāmān, and the jyotis agniṣṭoma with the Bṛhat sāmān.

16.5.20.a.m: There are four abhiplavas arranged in this manner.

16.5.21.a.m: The pṛṣṭhya six-day period completes [the month].

16.5.22.a.s: sadvitīyaḥ satṛtīyaḥ sacaturthaḥ sapañcamaḥ saṃbhāryaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ //
16.5.22.a.d: सद्वितीयः सतृतीयः सचतुर्थः सपञ्चमः संभार्यः षष्ठः ॥
16.5.22.a.m: [This constitutes] the second [month], the third, the fourth, and the fifth; the sixth is the saṃbhārya [month].

16.5.25.a.m: The abhijit and the three svarasāmans are ukthyas or agniṣṭomas.

16.5.28.a.m: In the middle is the viṣūvant day, a twenty-one-versed agniṣṭoma, the great divākīrtya.

16.5.30.a.m: When the sun has completely risen, he initiates the morning chant.

16.5.32.a.m: The subsequent half-year is reversed: the three svarasāmans,

16.5.34.a.m: four stationary days, and the pṛṣṭhya six-day period beginning with the thirty-three-versed day.

16.5.35.a.m: There are four abhiplavas taken in reverse order; that forms the month.

16.5.36.a.m: [This constitutes] the second [month], the third, the fourth, and the fifth.

16.5.37.a.m: The saṃbhārya is the last: two abhiplavas,

16.5.39.a.m: the twelve days of the twelve-day sacrifice,

16.5.40.a.m: the mahāvrata, and the concluding atirātra.

16.6.1.a.m: Such are the twelve months according to the Śāṭhyāyanaka tradition.

16.6.2.a.m: According to the Tāṇḍaka tradition, the subsequent half-year has saṃbhāryas at both ends.

16.6.3.a.s: upariṣṭād viśvajitaḥ / pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahas trayo 'bhiplavā iti dvyūno māsa uttame saṃbhārye catvāro 'bhiplavā gauś cāyuś ca dve ahanī dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratodayanībhyāṃ dvyūno māsaḥ pūryate / atha ha bhāllāvike pūrvasmin pakṣe purastāt prathamāt pṛṣṭhyād abhijid agniṣṭomaḥ / uttarasmin pakṣa upariṣṭād uttamāt pṛṣṭhyād viśvajitaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaha āyurukthyaḥ sa ekasthāne gaur bhavati / samānam itarac chāṭyāyanakena //
16.6.3.a.d: उपरिष्टाद् विश्वजितः । पृष्ठ्यः षडहस् त्रयो ऽभिप्लवा इति द्व्यूनो मास उत्तमे संभार्ये चत्वारो ऽभिप्लवा गौश् चायुश् च द्वे अहनी द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतोदयनीभ्यां द्व्यूनो मासः पूर्यते । अथ ह भाल्लाविके पूर्वस्मिन् पक्षे पुरस्तात् प्रथमात् पृष्ठ्याद् अभिजिद् अग्निष्टोमः । उत्तरस्मिन् पक्ष उपरिष्टाद् उत्तमात् पृष्ठ्याद् विश्वजितः पृष्ठ्यः षडह आयुरुक्थ्यः स एकस्थाने गौर् भवति । समानम् इतरच् छाट्यायनकेन ॥
16.6.3.a.m: Above the viśvajit: the pṛṣṭhya six-day period and three abhiplavas—this is a month deficient by two days; in the final saṃbhārya, four abhiplavas, the two days go and āyus, the ten days of the twelve-day sacrifice—with the mahāvrata and the concluding day, the month deficient by two days is filled. Now, in the Bhāllāvika tradition, in the first half-year, before the first pṛṣṭhya, there is the abhijit agniṣṭoma; in the subsequent half-year, above the final pṛṣṭhya, after the viśvajit, is the pṛṣṭhya six-day period and the āyus ukthya; in one place it is the go [day]; the rest is the same as the Śāṭhyāyanaka tradition.

16.6.3.b.s: athaikeṣāṃ vijñāyate saṃvatsare sakṛt pṛṣṭhāny upayanti / dvādaśāhīne daśarātre / tatra pṛṣṭhyānām̐ sthāne 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaḍahā ūrdhvaṃ dvādaśāhīyāt / daśarātrān mahāvratam upayanti //
16.6.3.b.d: अथैकेषां विज्ञायते संवत्सरे सकृत् पृष्ठान्य् उपयन्ति । द्वादशाहीने दशरात्रे । तत्र पृष्ठ्यानाम्̐ स्थाने ऽभिप्लवाः षडहा ऊर्ध्वं द्वादशाहीयात् । दशरात्रान् महाव्रतम् उपयन्ति ॥
16.6.3.b.m: Now, it is known among some: they undertake the pṛṣṭhas once in a year, in the ten-night period of the twelve-day sacrifice; there, in place of the pṛṣṭhya six-day periods, there are abhiplava six-day periods; after the ten-night period of the twelve-day sacrifice, they undertake the mahāvrata.

16.6.4.a.d: श्वो भूते प्रतायते पञ्चविम्̐शो ऽग्निष्टोमो महाव्रतसामा ॥
16.6.4.a.m: On the next day is performed the twenty-five-versed agniṣṭoma having the Mahāvrata sāmān.

16.6.6.a.m: when that is done, the pratiprasthātṛ arranges the artistic items of the mahāvrata.

16.6.7.a.m: There are ten drilled holes in the neck of the lute.

16.6.8.a.m: In each hole he weaves ten strings.

16.6.9.a.m: That becomes a lute of a hundred strings.

16.6.10.a.m: Directly above the hotṛ's seat, they fasten a swing for the hotṛ.

16.6.11.a.m: He places a throne of udumbara wood near the udgātṛ.

16.6.12.a.m: [He places] two grass-cushion boards for the adhvaryu.

16.6.13.a.m: The hotrakas and choristers sit on grass cushions.

16.6.15.a.s: tam̐ saṃnayati vāk satyaṃ mano bhadraṃ tan no bhadram \ ā no bhadram iti triparvayotkaṭaśalākayā veṇuparvaṇā vetasaśākhyā vā vādayitvā bāṇena śatatantunā māhendrasya stotram upākaroti //
16.6.15.a.d: तम्̐ संनयति वाक् सत्यं मनो भद्रं तन् नो भद्रम् \ आ नो भद्रम् इति त्रिपर्वयोत्कटशलाकया वेणुपर्वणा वेतसशाख्या वा वादयित्वा बाणेन शततन्तुना माहेन्द्रस्य स्तोत्रम् उपाकरोति ॥
16.6.15.a.m: He leads it forward: having sounded it with a three-knotted reed-stalk, a bamboo node, or a reed branch with the mantras 'Speech is truth, mind is auspicious; auspicious to us is that...', 'Auspicious to us...', he inaugurates the Mahāmahendra chant with a hundred-stringed harp.

16.6.17.a.m: Having played it, the udgātṛ hands it to the prastotṛ.

16.6.20.a.s: tam̐ so 'greṇa sadaso dakṣiṇe dvārbāhau prativādayann āste //
16.6.20.a.d: तम्̐ सो ऽग्रेण सदसो दक्षिणे द्वार्बाहौ प्रतिवादयन्न् आस्ते ॥
16.6.20.a.m: Playing it in front of the sadas at the southern doorpost, he sits.

16.6.21.a.s: upagāyanti patnyo 'pāghāṭalikās tālukavīṇāḥ kāṇḍavīṇāḥ piccholā alābukapiśīrṣṇya iti //
16.6.21.a.d: उपगायन्ति पत्न्यो ऽपाघाटलिकास् तालुकवीणाः काण्डवीणाः पिच्छोला अलाबुकपिशीर्ष्ण्य इति ॥
16.6.21.a.m: The wives sing along with apāghāṭalikā lutes, palate-lutes, reed-lutes, piccholā flutes, and gourd lutes with monkey heads.

16.6.22.a.m: Playing, they talk together at the third all-crafts [session].

16.6.23.a.m: A harlot and a student of the Veda engage each other on the northern buttock of the vedi.

16.6.24.a.s: māgadhaḥ pum̐ścaluś ca dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇyāṃ pariśrayete //
16.6.24.a.d: मागधः पुम्̐श्चलुश् च दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोण्यां परिश्रयेते ॥
16.6.24.a.m: A Māgadha bard and a harlot screen themselves on the southern buttock of the vedi.

16.6.25.a.m: They strike drums set up in the cardinal directions,

16.6.27.a.s: apareṇāgnīdhram ardham antarvedy ardhaṃ bahirvedi jānudaghnam avaṭaṃ khātvārdreṇa carmaṇābhivitatya śaṅkubhiḥ pariṇihatya bhūmidundubhiḥ pucchakāṇḍena bhūmidundubhim āghnanti //
16.6.27.a.d: अपरेणाग्नीध्रम् अर्धम् अन्तर्वेद्य् अर्धं बहिर्वेदि जानुदघ्नम् अवटं खात्वार्द्रेण चर्मणाभिवितत्य शङ्कुभिः परिणिहत्य भूमिदुन्दुभिः पुच्छकाण्डेन भूमिदुन्दुभिम् आघ्नन्ति ॥
16.6.27.a.m: Behind the Āgnīdhra hall, having dug a knee-deep hole half inside the vedi and half outside the vedi, having covered it over with a wet hide and fastened it with pegs, they beat the earth-drum with the tail-joint [of an ox-tail].

16.6.28.a.m: Behind the Āgnīdhra hall, a Śūdra and an Ārya pull back and forth against each other for a round piece of hide.

16.6.29.a.m: It is white, wet, and circular.

16.6.30.a.m: The Brahmin stands inside the vedi; the Śūdra outside the vedi.

16.6.31.a.s: ime 'rātsur ime sabhūtam akran \\ iti brāhmaṇo brūyāt // ima udvāsīkāriṇa ime durbhūtam akran \\ iti śūdraḥ //
16.6.31.a.d: इमे ऽरात्सुर् इमे सभूतम् अक्रन् \\ इति ब्राह्मणो ब्रूयात् ॥ इम उद्वासीकारिण इमे दुर्भूतम् अक्रन् \\ इति शूद्रः ॥
16.6.31.a.m: The Brahmin should say: 'These have prospered, these have created good fortune.' The Śūdra [should say]: 'These are expellers, these have created misfortune.'

16.6.32.a.m: Having won it, the Brahmin tosses the hide onto the Āgnīdhra [shed].

16.6.33.a.s: agreṇāgnīdhraṃ kaṭasaṃghāte // tejanisaṃghāte vā / vitatyocchritaṃ lambayati //
16.6.33.a.d: अग्रेणाग्नीध्रं कटसंघाते ॥ तेजनिसंघाते वा । वितत्योच्छ्रितं लम्बयति ॥
16.6.33.a.m: In front of the Āgnīdhra shed, having stretched [a hide] upon a collection of reed-mats or on a bundle of sharp reeds, he hangs it raised up.

16.6.34.a.s: agreṇāhavanīyam̐ ratheṣu rājaputrāḥ kavacinaḥ saṃnahya vyathanārthaṃ carmānu parivartante //
16.6.34.a.d: अग्रेणाहवनीयम्̐ रथेषु राजपुत्राः कवचिनः संनह्य व्यथनार्थं चर्मानु परिवर्तन्ते ॥
16.6.34.a.m: In front of the āhavanīya, royal princes in chariots, having buckled on armor, drive around the hide to pierce it.

16.6.35.a.m: He directs each one of them:

16.6.36.a.m: 'Do not miss! Do not shoot beyond!'

16.6.37.a.m: Pierced, they do not let [the arrows] overshoot it.

16.6.38.a.d: उदञ्चो ऽपरिमितम् अवकाशं यात्वा प्रत्यायाय विमुञ्चन्ति ॥
16.6.38.a.m: Going north to an indefinite space, having returned, they unyoke.

16.6.39.a.s: aṣṭau dāsakumārya udakumbhāñ chīrṣann adhi nidhāya triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ mārjālīyaṃ dhiṣṇiyaṃ parinṛtyantīḥ pariyanti dakṣiṇān pado nighnatīr idaṃmadhu gāyantyas \\ vāg veda bhillukā sainān gāyatu prāṇasya vādite semān gītā yajamānān ihāvatu \\ iti //
16.6.39.a.d: अष्टौ दासकुमार्य उदकुम्भाञ् छीर्षन्न् अधि निधाय त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं मार्जालीयं धिष्णियं परिनृत्यन्तीः परियन्ति दक्षिणान् पदो निघ्नतीर् इदंमधु गायन्त्यस् \\ वाग् वेद भिल्लुका सैनान् गायतु प्राणस्य वादिते सेमान् गीता यजमानान् इहावतु \\ इति ॥
16.6.39.a.m: Eight maidservants, placing water-jars upon their heads, go around dancing thrice clockwise around the mārjālīya hearth, stamping their right feet and singing 'idam madhu': 'Speech knows the bhillukā; let it sing these; sounded by the breath, may it, having been sung, protect the sacrificers here!'

16.6.40.a.s: bhillukāṃ dve gāyataḥ / vāg veda hiṃbinī \\ iti dve vāg veda hastāvārām iti dve saṃvatsaragāthā dve etāḥ saṃvatsaragāthā bhavanti //
16.6.40.a.d: भिल्लुकां द्वे गायतः । वाग् वेद हिंबिनी \\ इति द्वे वाग् वेद हस्तावाराम् इति द्वे संवत्सरगाथा द्वे एताः संवत्सरगाथा भवन्ति ॥
16.6.40.a.m: Two sing the bhillukā; two sing 'Speech knows the hiṃbinī'; two sing 'Speech knows the hastāvārā'; two sing the year-songs. These are the year-songs:

16.6.41.a.s: gāva eva surabhayo gāvo gulgulugandhayaḥ / gāvo ghṛtasya mātaras tā iha santu bhūyasīḥ //
16.6.41.a.d: गाव एव सुरभयो गावो गुल्गुलुगन्धयः । गावो घृतस्य मातरस् ता इह सन्तु भूयसीः ॥
16.6.41.a.m: 'The cows alone are fragrant, the cows have the scent of bdellium; / the cows are mothers of ghee; let them be abundant here!'

16.6.41.b.s: nanu gāvo maṅkīrasya \ gaṅgāyā udakaṃ papuḥ / \ papuḥ sarasvatīṃ nadīm \\ prācīś cojjagāhire / \ imā vayaṃ plavāmahe \ śamyāḥ prataratām iva / \ nikīrya tubhyaṃ madhye \\ ākarśye karśyo yathā / \ yadā bhaṅgyaśvinau vadatas \\ ṛtaparṇaka yo 'vadhīḥ / \ āviṣkṛtasya dūṣaṇam \ ubhayor akutaḥ kṛtasya ca //
16.6.41.b.d: ननु गावो मङ्कीरस्य \ गङ्गाया उदकं पपुः । \ पपुः सरस्वतीं नदीम् \\ प्राचीश् चोज्जगाहिरे । \ इमा वयं प्लवामहे \ शम्याः प्रतरताम् इव । \ निकीर्य तुभ्यं मध्ये \\ आकर्श्ये कर्श्यो यथा । \ यदा भङ्ग्यश्विनौ वदतस् \\ ऋतपर्णक यो ऽवधीः । \ आविष्कृतस्य दूषणम् \ उभयोर् अकुतः कृतस्य च ॥
16.6.41.b.m: 'Surely the cows of Maṅkīra drank the water of the Gaṅgā; / they drank the river Sarasvatī, and they plunged into the eastern streams. / We float along these like yokes of those crossing over, / having poured out in the middle for you, as one lean into the emaciated. / When the Bhaṅgyaśvins speak: “O Ṛtaparṇaka, who struck down? / The fault of that made manifest, and of that which was made by neither?”'

16.6.41.c.s: yadā rākhāṭyau vadatas \\ grāmyamaṅkīradāśakau / \ kṣeme vṛddhe grāmeṇa \\ anaḍvāṃs tapyate vahan //
16.6.41.c.d: यदा राखाट्यौ वदतस् \\ ग्राम्यमङ्कीरदाशकौ । \ क्षेमे वृद्धे ग्रामेण \\ अनड्वांस् तप्यते वहन् ॥
16.6.41.c.m: 'When the two Rākhāṭīs say: / “The two Maṅkīra fishermen of the village; / when peace is increased by the village, / the ox suffers while drawing.”'

16.6.41.d.s: idaṃ kalmāṣyo apipan \\ idaṃ somo asūyata / \ idam̐ hiraṇyaiḥ khīlās \\ āvāyan sāsthibhañjanam //
16.6.41.d.d: इदं कल्माष्यो अपिपन् \\ इदं सोमो असूयत । \ इदम्̐ हिरण्यैः खीलास् \\ आवायन् सास्थिभञ्जनम् ॥
16.6.41.d.m: 'This the spotted cows drank; here soma was pressed; / here, pegs with gold pieces wove together bone-breaking [armor].'

16.6.41.e.s: haimahā idaṃ madhu hilluhillu \\ aham ahar mimi \\ iti hastāvārāś ca sarvāsv anuṣajante //
16.6.41.e.d: हैमहा इदं मधु हिल्लुहिल्लु \\ अहम् अहर् मिमि \\ इति हस्तावाराश् च सर्वास्व् अनुषजन्ते ॥
16.6.41.e.m: 'Haimahā, this is sweetness, hillu hillu, I measure day by day'—these hastāvārā [refrains] are attached to all [verses].

16.6.42.a.m: Pouring out the water-jars right there, they depart according to their business.

16.6.43.a.m: Following the Mahāmahendra chant, the clamors cease.

16.6.45.a.s: kūrcayoḥ phalakayor vā tiṣṭhann adhvaryuḥ pratigṛṇāti //
16.6.45.a.d: कूर्चयोः फलकयोर् वा तिष्ठन्न् अध्वर्युः प्रतिगृणाति ॥
16.6.45.a.m: Standing on the grass cushions or on the boards, the adhvaryu responds.

16.7.1.a.m: On the next day the udayanīya [rite takes place]; it has been explained.

16.7.2.a.m: What is the prāyaṇīya rite, that is the udayanīya rite.

16.7.3.a.m: On the three Paraḥsāman days, he draws three atigrāhya cups.

16.7.4.a.s: upayāmagṛhīto 'si \\ adbhyas tvauṣadhībhyo juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmi \\ iti prathame 'hani gṛhṇāti / upayāmagṛhīto 'si \\ oṣadhībhyas tvā prajābhyo juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmi \\ iti dvitīye \\ upayāmagṛhīto 'si \ prajābhyas tvā prajāpataye juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmi \\ ity etān evāvṛttān arvāksāmasu gṛhṇīyāt //
16.7.4.a.d: उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि \\ अद्भ्यस् त्वौषधीभ्यो जुष्टं गृह्णामि \\ इति प्रथमे ऽहनि गृह्णाति । उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि \\ ओषधीभ्यस् त्वा प्रजाभ्यो जुष्टं गृह्णामि \\ इति द्वितीये \\ उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि \ प्रजाभ्यस् त्वा प्रजापतये जुष्टं गृह्णामि \\ इत्य् एतान् एवावृत्तान् अर्वाक्सामसु गृह्णीयात् ॥
16.7.4.a.m: On the first day he draws with: 'You are taken with a support; I draw you pleasing to the waters, to the plants'; on the second with: 'You are taken with a support; I draw you pleasing to the plants, to the creatures'; with: 'You are taken with a support; I draw you pleasing to the creatures, to Prajāpati'—he should draw these very same ones in reverse order on the Arvāksāman days.

16.7.5.a.s: tān ubhayān ūrdhvān apravṛttāṃś ca viṣuvati \\ ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam iti teṣāṃ madhye sauryam̐ saptamaṃ madhyamaṃ gṛhṇāti //
16.7.5.a.d: तान् उभयान् ऊर्ध्वान् अप्रवृत्तांश् च विषुवति \\ उद् उ त्यं जातवेदसम् इति तेषां मध्ये सौर्यम्̐ सप्तमं मध्यमं गृह्णाति ॥
16.7.5.a.m: Both these, facing upwards and not previously employed, on the Viṣuvant day, [he draws, and] among them he draws the seventh, middle [cup], dedicated to Sūrya, with 'Up that all-knowing god...'
