16.7.6.a.s: vācaspatiṃ viśvakarmāṇam ūtaye \\ iti viśvajiti vaiśvakarmāṇam / mahīm ūṣu mātaram ity aparedyur ādityaṃ te ca vyatyāsamā mahāvratāt tāv ubhau saha mahāvrate gṛhyete //
16.7.6.a.d: वाचस्पतिं विश्वकर्माणम् ऊतये \\ इति विश्वजिति वैश्वकर्माणम् । महीम् ऊषु मातरम् इत्य् अपरेद्युर् आदित्यं ते च व्यत्यासमा महाव्रतात् ताव् उभौ सह महाव्रते गृह्येते ॥
16.7.6.a.m: On the Viśvajit day, [he draws] the cup dedicated to Viśvakarman with: 'The lord of speech, Viśvakarman, for aid...'; on the following day the cup dedicated to Āditya with: 'The great mother...'; and these two, alternating from then up to the Mahāvrata day, are both drawn together on the Mahāvrata day.

16.7.7.a.m: Thirty-three atigrāhya cups are drawn on this day.

16.7.8.a.s: prākṛtair vā vaikṛtāny abhyasyet / vaikṛtair vā prākṛtān daśāgneyān gṛhṇīyāt //
16.7.8.a.d: प्राकृतैर् वा वैकृतान्य् अभ्यस्येत् । वैकृतैर् वा प्राकृतान् दशाग्नेयान् गृह्णीयात् ॥
16.7.8.a.m: Or he should duplicate the modified cups with the primary ones; or he should draw ten cups dedicated to Agni [corresponding to] the modified with the primary,

16.7.9.a.s: daśaindrān daśa sauryān vaiśvakarmaṇādityagrahau prājāpatyaṃ ca //
16.7.9.a.d: दशैन्द्रान् दश सौर्यान् वैश्वकर्मणादित्यग्रहौ प्राजापत्यं च ॥
16.7.9.a.m: ten dedicated to Indra, ten dedicated to Sūrya, the cup to Viśvakarman, the cup to Āditya, and the cup to Prajāpati.

16.7.10.a.s: pañcapātram atigrāhyāyatane pratidiśaṃ catvāri pātrāṇi nihitāni bhavanti //
16.7.10.a.d: पञ्चपात्रम् अतिग्राह्यायतने प्रतिदिशं चत्वारि पात्राणि निहितानि भवन्ति ॥
16.7.10.a.m: There are five vessels; in the place of the atigrāhya cup four vessels are deposited, one in each direction,

16.7.12.a.s: indram id gāthinas \\ ity anudrutya \\ upayāmagṛhīto 'si \\ indrāya tvārkavate juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmi \\ iti pūrvārdhe gṛhṇāti / eṣa te yonir \ indrāya tvārkavate \\ iti sādayati //
16.7.12.a.d: इन्द्रम् इद् गाथिनस् \\ इत्य् अनुद्रुत्य \\ उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि \\ इन्द्राय त्वार्कवते जुष्टं गृह्णामि \\ इति पूर्वार्धे गृह्णाति । एष ते योनिर् \ इन्द्राय त्वार्कवते \\ इति सादयति ॥
16.7.12.a.m: Having recited 'Indra alone do the singers of hymns...', he draws in the eastern half with: 'You are taken with a support; I draw you pleasing to Indra accompanied by the arka'; he settles it with: 'This is your seat; for Indra accompanied by the arka.'

16.7.13.a.m: The drawing and the settling formulas are identical everywhere.

16.7.14.a.s: abhi tvā śūra nonumas \\ iti dakṣiṇārdhe / tvām id dhi havāmahe \\ iti paścārdhe //
16.7.14.a.d: अभि त्वा शूर नोनुमस् \\ इति दक्षिणार्धे । त्वाम् इद् धि हवामहे \\ इति पश्चार्धे ॥
16.7.14.a.m: In the southern half [he draws] with 'Towards you, O hero, we shout loudly...'; in the western half with 'You alone indeed do we invoke...';

16.7.15.a.s: imā nu kaṃ bhuvanā sīṣadhema \\ ity uttarārdhe // tad id āsu bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭham \\ yato jajña ugras tveṣanṛmṇaḥ / \ sadyo jajñāno niriṇāti śatrūn \ anu yaṃ viśve madanty ūmās \\ iti madhyame //
16.7.15.a.d: इमा नु कं भुवना सीषधेम \\ इत्य् उत्तरार्धे ॥ तद् इद् आसु भुवनेषु ज्येष्ठम् \\ यतो जज्ञ उग्रस् त्वेषनृम्णः । \ सद्यो जज्ञानो निरिणाति शत्रून् \ अनु यं विश्वे मदन्त्य् ऊमास् \\ इति मध्यमे ॥
16.7.15.a.m: in the northern half with 'Now indeed may we make these worlds successful...'; in the middle [he draws] with 'That indeed is the oldest among these worlds, / whence the fierce one of glittering valor was born; / born immediately, he crushes the enemies, / after whom all helpers exult.'

16.7.16.a.s: tān ekasmin pātre samavanīya tve kratum api vṛñjanti viśve \\ ity anudrutya \\ upayāmagṛhīto 'si \ prajāpataye tvā juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmi \\ iti madhyame pātre gṛhṇāti \\ eṣa te yoniḥ \ prajāpataye tvā \\ iti sādayati //
16.7.16.a.d: तान् एकस्मिन् पात्रे समवनीय त्वे क्रतुम् अपि वृञ्जन्ति विश्वे \\ इत्य् अनुद्रुत्य \\ उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि \ प्रजापतये त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णामि \\ इति मध्यमे पात्रे गृह्णाति \\ एष ते योनिः \ प्रजापतये त्वा \\ इति सादयति ॥
16.7.16.a.m: Having poured them together into a single vessel, having recited 'In you all also concentrate their resolve...', he draws into the middle vessel with: 'You are taken with a support; I draw you pleasing to Prajāpati'; he settles it with: 'This is your seat; for Prajāpati.'

16.7.17.a.s: yan nānā juhuyād ātmano 'ṅgāni vicchindyāt / samānīyāhutīḥ sam̐rundhyāt tad anu yajamānāḥ sam̐rundheran / stokā evātmānaṃ pratyānīya hotavyāḥ pratyaṅgāni dadhāti nāhutīḥ sam̐ruṇaddhi ( iti ) hutvā harati bhakṣam //
16.7.17.a.d: यन् नाना जुहुयाद् आत्मनो ऽङ्गानि विच्छिन्द्यात् । समानीयाहुतीः सम्̐रुन्ध्यात् तद् अनु यजमानाः सम्̐रुन्धेरन् । स्तोका एवात्मानं प्रत्यानीय होतव्याः प्रत्यङ्गानि दधाति नाहुतीः सम्̐रुणद्धि ( इति ) हुत्वा हरति भक्षम् ॥
16.7.17.a.m: 'If he were to offer them separately, he would cut off his own limbs. If he were to unite them, he would obstruct the offerings, and following that, the sacrificers would be obstructed. Having poured the drops back into oneself, they are to be offered: thus he places the limbs one by one and does not obstruct the offerings'—having offered [thus], he carries the portion for consumption.

16.7.18.a.s: taṃ bhakṣayati mahas te bhakṣayāmi \ garbhaṃ te bhakṣayāmi ( bhujaṃ te bhakṣayāmi ) bhuktis te bhakṣayāmi \ sarvaṃ te bhakṣayāmi sarvasyāptyai sarvasyāvaruddhyai \\ iti //
16.7.18.a.d: तं भक्षयति महस् ते भक्षयामि \ गर्भं ते भक्षयामि ( भुजं ते भक्षयामि ) भुक्तिस् ते भक्षयामि \ सर्वं ते भक्षयामि सर्वस्याप्त्यै सर्वस्यावरुद्ध्यै \\ इति ॥
16.7.18.a.m: He consumes it with: 'I consume your greatness; I consume your embryo; [I consume your arm;] I consume your enjoyment; I consume your all, for the attainment of everything, for the securing of everything.'

16.7.19.a.m: We shall explain the three-pointed arrangement [of grahas].

16.7.20.a.m: Their procedure is explained by the archetypal atigrāhya [cups].

16.7.21.a.s: aindravāyavāgraṃ prathamam ahar atha śukrāgram athāgrayaṇāgram //
16.7.21.a.d: ऐन्द्रवायवाग्रं प्रथमम् अहर् अथ शुक्राग्रम् अथाग्रयणाग्रम् ॥
16.7.21.a.m: The first day has the Aindravāyava cup first; next, the Śukra cup first; next, the Āgrayaṇa cup first.

16.7.22.a.s: evaṃ tryanīkāḥ parivartanta ita ūrdhvaṃ prāgviṣuvata ūrdhvaṃ viṣuvata āvṛttāvṛtteṣu //
16.7.22.a.d: एवं त्र्यनीकाः परिवर्तन्त इत ऊर्ध्वं प्राग्विषुवत ऊर्ध्वं विषुवत आवृत्तावृत्तेषु ॥
16.7.22.a.m: Thus the triads revolve from here onwards, before the Viṣuvant day, and after the Viṣuvant day in the reversed [orders].

16.7.23.a.s: śukrāgro viṣuvān ity ātreyaḥ / yathādṛṣṭam iti vādarāyaṇaḥ //
16.7.23.a.d: शुक्राग्रो विषुवान् इत्य् आत्रेयः । यथादृष्टम् इति वादरायणः ॥
16.7.23.a.m: 'The Viṣuvant day has the Śukra cup first,' says Ātreya. 'According as it is seen [in the ritual tradition],' says Bādarāyaṇa.

16.8.2.a.s: āgneyaṃ prāyaṇīye 'tirātra ālabhante / śvo bhūte sārasvatīṃ meṣīm //
16.8.2.a.d: आग्नेयं प्रायणीये ऽतिरात्र आलभन्ते । श्वो भूते सारस्वतीं मेषीम् ॥
16.8.2.a.m: On the introductory Atirātra, they immolate an animal sacred to Agni; on the following day, a ewe sacred to Sarasvatī.

16.8.3.a.m: Thus day after day they immolate the animals of the set of eleven according to rule.

16.8.4.a.m: Coming together again and again, they repeat the set of eleven.

16.8.5.a.s: teṣām evam upākurvatāṃ dvādaśāhasya saptadaśa ukthye dvātrim̐śatam ekādaśinyo 'pavṛjyante //
16.8.5.a.d: तेषाम् एवम् उपाकुर्वतां द्वादशाहस्य सप्तदश उक्थ्ये द्वात्रिम्̐शतम् एकादशिन्यो ऽपवृज्यन्ते ॥
16.8.5.a.m: For those performing thus, thirty-two sets of eleven are completed on the seventeenth Ukthya day of the Dvādaśāha.

16.8.7.a.m: On those [days], [they immolate] the bovine surplus animals:

16.8.8.a.s: vaiṣṇavaṃ vāmanam ekavim̐śe / aindrāgnaṃ triṇave / vaiśvadevaṃ trayastrim̐śe / dyāvāpṛthivyāṃ dhenuṃ prathame chandome / tasyā eva vāyavyaṃ vatsaṃ madhyame / ādityām avivaśām uttame maitrāvaruṇīm avivākye / prājāpatyam ṛṣabhaṃ tūparam mahāvrate / āgneyam udayanīya iti pāliṅgāyanikān //
16.8.8.a.d: वैष्णवं वामनम् एकविम्̐शे । ऐन्द्राग्नं त्रिणवे । वैश्वदेवं त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शे । द्यावापृथिव्यां धेनुं प्रथमे छन्दोमे । तस्या एव वायव्यं वत्सं मध्यमे । आदित्याम् अविवशाम् उत्तमे मैत्रावरुणीम् अविवाक्ये । प्राजापत्यम् ऋषभं तूपरम् महाव्रते । आग्नेयम् उदयनीय इति पालिङ्गायनिकान् ॥
16.8.8.a.m: a dwarf bull sacred to Viṣṇu on the twenty-first day; one sacred to Indra-and-Agni on the twenty-seventh; one sacred to the Viśve Devas on the thirty-third; a milch-cow sacred to Heaven-and-Earth on the first Chandoma day; her calf sacred to Vāyu on the middle [Chandoma day]; a barren cow sacred to the Ādityas on the last; a cow sacred to Mitra-and-Varuṇa on the Avivākya day; a hornless bull sacred to Prajāpati on the Mahāvrata; one sacred to Agni on the concluding day: thus say the Pāliṅgāyanikas.

16.8.9.a.s: atha kāṭhakā aikādásinān prativibhajyāprativibhajya vā prāyaṇīyodayanīyayor ālabhante //
16.8.9.a.d: अथ काठका ऐकाद्áसिनान् प्रतिविभज्याप्रतिविभज्य वा प्रायणीयोदयनीययोर् आलभन्ते ॥
16.8.9.a.m: Now the Kaṭhas immolate the sets of eleven, either having distributed them severally or not having distributed them severally, between the introductory and concluding days.

16.8.10.a.m: [They immolate] an animal sacred to Agni at the transition, one sacred to Indra on the days having the Rathaṃtara-sāman as the pṛṣṭha-stotra, and on those having the Bṛhat-sāman as the pṛṣṭha-stotra.

16.8.11.a.m: Or rather, an animal sacred to Agni-and-Indra on the days having the Rathaṃtara-sāman as the pṛṣṭha-stotra, and one sacred to Indra-and-Agni on those having the Bṛhat-sāman as the pṛṣṭha-stotra.

16.8.12.a.d: सौर्यं विषुवत्य् उपालभन्ते ऽथ गव्यान् अतिरिक्तपशून् ॥
16.8.12.a.m: They immolate an animal sacred to Sūrya on the Viṣuvant day; then the bovine surplus animals:

16.8.13.a.s: śitipṛṣṭhaṃ bārhaspatyaṃ trayastrim̐śe / dyāvāpṛthivyāṃ dhenuṃ prathame chandome / tasyā eva vatsaṃ vāyavyaṃ madhyame / vāce pṛśnim uttame / maitrāvaruṇamavivākye / vaiśvakarmaṇam ṛṣabhaṃ tūparaṃ mahāvrata iti vājasaneyakam //
16.8.13.a.d: शितिपृष्ठं बार्हस्पत्यं त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शे । द्यावापृथिव्यां धेनुं प्रथमे छन्दोमे । तस्या एव वत्सं वायव्यं मध्यमे । वाचे पृश्निम् उत्तमे । मैत्रावरुणमविवाक्ये । वैश्वकर्मणम् ऋषभं तूपरं महाव्रत इति वाजसनेयकम् ॥
16.8.13.a.m: a white-backed animal sacred to Bṛhaspati on the thirty-third; a milch-cow sacred to Heaven-and-Earth on the first Chandoma day; her calf sacred to Vāyu on the middle [Chandoma day]; a speckled cow for Vāc on the last; an animal sacred to Mitra-and-Varuṇa on the Avivākya day; a hornless bull sacred to Viśvakarman on the Mahāvrata: thus is the Vājasaneyaka teaching.

16.8.14.a.s: āgneyam agniṣṭoma ālabhante / aindrāgnam ukthye dvitīyam aindraṃ vṛṣṇim̐ ṣoḍaśini tṛtīyam̐ sārasvatīṃ meṣīm atirātre caturthīm ity ekeṣāṃ te yadi prabhavaḥ paśavaḥ syur evam evāharahar ālabheran //
16.8.14.a.d: आग्नेयम् अग्निष्टोम आलभन्ते । ऐन्द्राग्नम् उक्थ्ये द्वितीयम् ऐन्द्रं वृष्णिम्̐ षोडशिनि तृतीयम्̐ सारस्वतीं मेषीम् अतिरात्रे चतुर्थीम् इत्य् एकेषां ते यदि प्रभवः पशवः स्युर् एवम् एवाहरहर् आलभेरन् ॥
16.8.14.a.m: 'They immolate an animal sacred to Agni at the Agniṣṭoma; a second sacred to Indra-and-Agni at the Ukthya; a third, a ram sacred to Indra, at the Ṣoḍaśin; a fourth, a ewe sacred to Sarasvatī, at the Atirātra,' according to some; if they have plenty of animals, they should immolate just in this manner day after day.

16.8.15.a.s: yadi paśvekādaśinyeyur āgneyam eva prathame 'hann ālabherann athetarān anūco yathāpūrvaṃ vāruṇaṃ pettvam uttamaṃ yūnam aparyave teṣv āgneyam eva prathame 'hann ālabherann athetarān anūco yathāpūrvaṃ vāruṇaṃ petvam uttamaṃ tair eva viparyāsam īyuḥ //
16.8.15.a.d: यदि पश्वेकादशिन्येयुर् आग्नेयम् एव प्रथमे ऽहन्न् आलभेरन्न् अथेतरान् अनूचो यथापूर्वं वारुणं पेत्त्वम् उत्तमं यूनम् अपर्यवे तेष्व् आग्नेयम् एव प्रथमे ऽहन्न् आलभेरन्न् अथेतरान् अनूचो यथापूर्वं वारुणं पेत्वम् उत्तमं तैर् एव विपर्यासम् ईयुः ॥
16.8.15.a.m: If they should proceed with a single set of eleven animals, they should immolate only the animal sacred to Agni on the first day, then the other animals in succession as before, the ram sacred to Varuṇa being the last; […] among these, they should immolate only the animal sacred to Agni on the first day, then the other animals in succession as before, the ram sacred to Varuṇa being the last; with those very animals they should proceed in reverse order.

16.8.16.a.m: We shall explain the Utsargiṇām Ayana [the sacrificial session of those who omit days].

16.8.17.a.m: It is explained by the Gavāmayana.

16.8.18.a.m: Throughout the year, they should omit the full-moon day and the new-moon day.

16.8.19.a.s: tān vopeyād vā notsṛjeyus tad eva śvaḥ kuryuḥ / ante 'māvāsyāṃ paurṇamāsīṃ votsṛjeyuḥ / antamasyāhnas trivṛd bahiṣpavamānam \\ vāyo śukro ayāmi te \\ etam u tyaṃ daśa kṣipas \\ iti //
16.8.19.a.d: तान् वोपेयाद् वा नोत्सृजेयुस् तद् एव श्वः कुर्युः । अन्ते ऽमावास्यां पौर्णमासीं वोत्सृजेयुः । अन्तमस्याह्नस् त्रिवृद् बहिष्पवमानम् \\ वायो शुक्रो अयामि ते \\ एतम् उ त्यं दश क्षिपस् \\ इति ॥
16.8.19.a.m: Or they may undertake them and not omit them; on the following day they should do that very rite; or at the end they should omit the new-moon day or the full-moon day; the end of this day is the ninefold Bahiṣpavamāna stotra, with: 'O Vāyu, pure [soma] is offered to you,' and 'This one, indeed, the ten fingers.'

16.8.20.a.s: yad ahar utsṛjeyus tad ahar iṣṭiṃ nirvapeyus ta āgneyamarutvatīyapuroḍāśau nirupyete aindrāvaiṣṇavā aindrābārhaspatyā aindrāvaiśvadevā vādhvarakalpā vā //
16.8.20.a.d: यद् अहर् उत्सृजेयुस् तद् अहर् इष्टिं निर्वपेयुस् त आग्नेयमरुत्वतीयपुरोडाशौ निरुप्येते ऐन्द्रावैष्णवा ऐन्द्राबार्हस्पत्या ऐन्द्रावैश्वदेवा वाध्वरकल्पा वा ॥
16.8.20.a.m: On whichever day they omit, on that day they should offer an iṣṭi; two sacrificial cakes are offered, sacred to Agni and sacred to the Maruts, or offerings sacred to Indra-and-Viṣṇu, sacred to Indra-and-Bṛhaspati, sacred to Indra-and-the-Viśve Devas, or following the Adhvarakalpā rite.

16.8.21.a.s: teṣāṃ ye puroḍāśinas ta upavasanti / ye sāṃnāyinas ta etad ahar vatsān apākurvanti / paśuś ca //
16.8.21.a.d: तेषां ये पुरोडाशिनस् त उपवसन्ति । ये सांनायिनस् त एतद् अहर् वत्सान् अपाकुर्वन्ति । पशुश् च ॥
16.8.21.a.m: Among them, those whose oblation is a sacrificial cake fast; those who offer the curd-and-milk oblation drive away the calves on that day; and there is an animal offering.

16.8.22.a.m: There is an animal sacred to Prajāpati and milk oblations.

16.8.23.a.s: yathā vaiśyas tathā tām asyendrāya vasumata indrāya harivata indrāya bṛhaspativate viśvadevyāvate puroḍāśāḥ / aṣṭāv ekādaśa dvādaśa kapālā ānupūrvyeṇa savanakāla vyākhyātāś ca //
16.8.23.a.d: यथा वैश्यस् तथा ताम् अस्येन्द्राय वसुमत इन्द्राय हरिवत इन्द्राय बृहस्पतिवते विश्वदेव्यावते पुरोडाशाः । अष्टाव् एकादश द्वादश कपाला आनुपूर्व्येण सवनकाल व्याख्याताश् च ॥
16.8.23.a.m: As for a Vaiśya, so for him there are sacrificial cakes for Indra accompanied by the Vasus, Indra accompanied by the bay steeds, Indra accompanied by Bṛhaspati, and Indra accompanied by the Viśve Devas, on eight, eleven, and twelve potsherds, respectively, and their pressings are explained in chronological sequence.

16.8.24.a.m: Saying: 'O ye that have been released…,' they drive away the calves.

16.8.25.a.s: prātaḥ paśum ālabhante tasya vapayā pracaranti / tato vaiśvadevo dvādaśakapālaḥ / vaiśvadevaś carus tṛtīyasavanaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate / pṛṣadājyena carite patnīḥ saṃyājayanti patnīḥ saṃyājayanti //
16.8.25.a.d: प्रातः पशुम् आलभन्ते तस्य वपया प्रचरन्ति । ततो वैश्वदेवो द्वादशकपालः । वैश्वदेवश् चरुस् तृतीयसवनः संतिष्ठते । पृषदाज्येन चरिते पत्नीः संयाजयन्ति पत्नीः संयाजयन्ति ॥
16.8.25.a.m: In the morning, they immolate the animal and proceed with its omentum; then there is a cake on twelve potsherds sacred to the Viśve Devas; a boiled rice oblation sacred to the Viśve Devas constitutes the third pressing; when it has been performed with clotted butter, they perform the Patnīsaṃyājas, they perform the Patnīsaṃyājas.

17.1.1.a.m: The Agniṣṭoma is the archetype of all soma sacrifices.

17.1.2.a.m: For group-rites (nikāyins), however, the first is always [the archetype].

17.1.4.a.m: The Jyotis, the Gauḥ, and the Āyus are the Trikadruka days.

17.1.5.a.m: The first is an Agniṣṭoma or an Ukthya.

17.1.7.a.m: At the Jyotis, he gives a thousand [cows as dakṣiṇā].

17.1.8.a.s: śyaitaniyamād bṛhatpṛṣṭho gaur bhrātṛvyavataḥ / āyuḥ svargakāmasya / agniṣṭomaḥ sabhrātṛvyavataḥ / viśvajid agniṣṭomaḥ sarvastomaḥ sarvapṛṣṭhyaḥ śraiṣṭhyakāmasya / sahasraṃ dakṣiṇāḥ / sarvavedasaṃ vā yāvatīr vā kratoḥ stotriyāḥ //
17.1.8.a.d: श्यैतनियमाद् बृहत्पृष्ठो गौर् भ्रातृव्यवतः । आयुः स्वर्गकामस्य । अग्निष्टोमः सभ्रातृव्यवतः । विश्वजिद् अग्निष्टोमः सर्वस्तोमः सर्वपृष्ठ्यः श्रैष्ठ्यकामस्य । सहस्रं दक्षिणाः । सर्ववेदसं वा यावतीर् वा क्रतोः स्तोत्रियाः ॥
17.1.8.a.m: Due to the rule of the Śyaita sāman, the Gauḥ with the Bṛhat as its pṛṣṭha-stotra is for one who has a rival; the Āyus is for one who desires heaven; the Agniṣṭoma is for one who has a rival; the Viśvajit Agniṣṭoma, containing all stomas and all pṛṣṭhas, is for one who desires pre-eminence; its dakṣiṇā is a thousand cows, or all one's possessions, or as many as there are stotriyā verses in the sacrifice.

17.1.9.a.s: sarvavedase jyeṣṭhaṃ putram apabhajya saṃvido viparyāceta //
17.1.9.a.d: सर्ववेदसे ज्येष्ठं पुत्रम् अपभज्य संविदो विपर्याचेत ॥
17.1.9.a.m: In the case of giving all one's possessions, having apportioned a share to his eldest son, he should distribute his assets.

17.1.10.a.m: At the time of the dakṣiṇā, he gives all his property,

17.1.11.a.s: yad anyad brāhmaṇānāṃ dikṣu vittād bhūmeḥ senābhyaś ca //
17.1.11.a.d: यद् अन्यद् ब्राह्मणानां दिक्षु वित्ताद् भूमेः सेनाभ्यश् च ॥
17.1.11.a.m: except what belongs to brāhmaṇas in the various quarters, the land, and armies.

17.1.12.a.s: uttamāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ nītvodavasāya vā dakṣiṇenaudumbarīṃ prāṅ niṣadya brūyāt \\ yan me 'da ṛṇaṃ yad adas tat sarvaṃ dadāmi \\ iti //
17.1.12.a.d: उत्तमां दक्षिणां नीत्वोदवसाय वा दक्षिणेनौदुम्बरीं प्राङ् निषद्य ब्रूयात् \\ यन् मे ऽद ऋणं यद् अदस् तत् सर्वं ददामि \\ इति ॥
17.1.12.a.m: Having led forward the last dakṣiṇā, or having departed from the sacrificial area, he should sit down facing east to the south of the udumbara post and say: 'Whatever debt is mine there, whatever is that, all that I give.'

17.1.13.a.s: udavasāya rohiṇīṃ vatsacchavīm̐ sakarṇapucchām̐ sakhurām̐ sakhurīkām avācyatāṃ paridhatta / uṣṇīṣeṇa śiro veṣṭayata ādatta audumbaraṃ camasam / audumbarīṃ cābhrim / khādirīṃ vaiṇavīṃ vā / kalmāṣīm̐ suṣirām asuṣirāṃ vobhayataḥkṣṇū / tām anyatarataḥkṣṇū / tāṃ vā mūlabhakṣo vā phalabhakṣo vāraṇye tisra udumbare vasataḥ / khanitreṇa jīvato mūlaṃ parikhāyaudumbare pātre 'vadhāyānyonyam apyādayato mṛnmayena pibato niṣāde tisro vaiśye tisro rājanye tisro brahmaṇa ity ekeṣām //
17.1.13.a.d: उदवसाय रोहिणीं वत्सच्छवीम्̐ सकर्णपुच्छाम्̐ सखुराम्̐ सखुरीकाम् अवाच्यतां परिधत्त । उष्णीषेण शिरो वेष्टयत आदत्त औदुम्बरं चमसम् । औदुम्बरीं चाभ्रिम् । खादिरीं वैणवीं वा । कल्माषीम्̐ सुषिराम् असुषिरां वोभयतःक्ष्णू । ताम् अन्यतरतःक्ष्णू । तां वा मूलभक्षो वा फलभक्षो वारण्ये तिस्र उदुम्बरे वसतः । खनित्रेण जीवतो मूलं परिखायौदुम्बरे पात्रे ऽवधायान्योन्यम् अप्यादयतो मृन्मयेन पिबतो निषादे तिस्रो वैश्ये तिस्रो राजन्ये तिस्रो ब्रह्मण इत्य् एकेषाम् ॥
17.1.13.a.m: Having departed from the sacrificial area, he wears a reddish skin of a calf, with ears, tail, and hooves, worn upside-down; he wraps his head with a turban; he takes an udumbara drinking-vessel, and an udumbara spade, or one of khadira or bamboo, spotted, hollow or solid, sharpened at both ends, or sharpened at one end; eating roots or eating fruits, they dwell three nights near an udumbara tree in the forest; subsisting by means of the spade, having dug around a root and placed it in an udumbara vessel, they feed one another; drinking from an earthen vessel, [they dwell] three nights among the Niṣādas, three among the Vaiśyas, three among the Rājanyas, and three among the brāhmaṇas: thus say some.

17.1.14.a.s: saṃvatsaraṃ dvādaśāhaṃ vā na yācen na dīyamānaṃ pratyācakṣate //
17.1.14.a.d: संवत्सरं द्वादशाहं वा न याचेन् न दीयमानं प्रत्याचक्षते ॥
17.1.14.a.m: For a year or for twelve days, he should not beg, nor do they refuse what is offered to him.

17.1.15.a.s: indrasyābhijid agniṣṭomo 'nabhijitasyābhijityai / ubhe bṛhadrathaṃtare bhavataḥ / parokṣapṛṣṭhe vā //
17.1.15.a.d: इन्द्रस्याभिजिद् अग्निष्टोमो ऽनभिजितस्याभिजित्यै । उभे बृहद्रथंतरे भवतः । परोक्षपृष्ठे वा ॥
17.1.15.a.m: Indra's Abhijit is an Agniṣṭoma, for the conquest of what has not been conquered. Both the Bṛhat and Rathaṃtara [sāmans] are [employed], or [there are] indirect Pṛṣṭhas.

17.1.16.a.m: The Bṛhat, however, belongs to the hotṛ, and there are eleven victims at a single sacrificial post.

17.1.17.a.m: The sacrificial gift is one thousand [cows], or one hundred and twelve chosen ones.

17.1.18.a.s: sarvajitāgniṣṭomena sarvapṛṣṭhena sarvam āpnoti sarvaṃ jayati //
17.1.18.a.d: सर्वजिताग्निष्टोमेन सर्वपृष्ठेन सर्वम् आप्नोति सर्वं जयति ॥
17.1.18.a.m: By means of the Sarvajit Agniṣṭoma having all the Pṛṣṭhas, he obtains everything, he conquers everything.

17.1.20.a.m: Its Pṛṣṭha is the Mahāvrata; the Arkya [śastra] is recited.

17.1.21.a.m: One thousand is the sacrificial gift, or twenty times twenty-eight.

17.1.23.a.s: jyotir agniṣṭomo rathaṃtarasāmā / sahasrāṇāṃ prathamaḥ / prāṇeṣv annādye ca pratitiṣṭhati / gaur ukthyo bṛhatsāmā dvitīyaḥ / paśuṣu pratitiṣṭhati / sarvajyotir agniṣṭoma ubhyasāmā tṛtīyaḥ / sarvasyāptyai sarvasyāvaruddhyai / trirātrasaṃmito 'gniṣṭomo rathaṃtarabṛhatsāmobhayasāmā vā caturthaḥ / trirātrasya phalam avāpnoti //
17.1.23.a.d: ज्योतिर् अग्निष्टोमो रथंतरसामा । सहस्राणां प्रथमः । प्राणेष्व् अन्नाद्ये च प्रतितिष्ठति । गौर् उक्थ्यो बृहत्सामा द्वितीयः । पशुषु प्रतितिष्ठति । सर्वज्योतिर् अग्निष्टोम उभ्यसामा तृतीयः । सर्वस्याप्त्यै सर्वस्यावरुद्ध्यै । त्रिरात्रसंमितो ऽग्निष्टोमो रथंतरबृहत्सामोभयसामा वा चतुर्थः । त्रिरात्रस्य फलम् अवाप्नोति ॥
17.1.23.a.m: The Jyotis is an Agniṣṭoma with the Rathaṃtara sāman, the first of the Sāhasras; he becomes established in vital breaths and food. The Gauḥ is an Ukthya with the Bṛhat sāman, the second; he becomes established in cattle. The Sarvajyotis is an Agniṣṭoma with both sāmans, the third, for the obtaining of everything, for the securing of everything. The one commensurate with a three-day rite is an Agniṣṭoma with the Rathaṃtara or Bṛhat sāman, or with both sāmans, the fourth; he attains the fruit of a three-day rite.

17.1.26.a.s: rathaṃtarasāmā bṛhatsāmobhayasāmā vā prathamaḥ / tasmin kāmāḥ somāhāre prādhānye spardhāyāṃ bhrātṛvyavatas titīrṣā // svargaḥ paśavo vā //
17.1.26.a.d: रथंतरसामा बृहत्सामोभयसामा वा प्रथमः । तस्मिन् कामाः सोमाहारे प्राधान्ये स्पर्धायां भ्रातृव्यवतस् तितीर्षा ॥ स्वर्गः पशवो वा ॥
17.1.26.a.m: The first has the Rathaṃtara sāman, the Bṛhat sāman, or both sāmans. In it the desires are: at the bringing of soma, in primacy, in rivalry, the desire to overcome of one who has an enemy, or heaven, or cattle.

17.1.27.a.s: pūrvedyur āgneyaḥ saumyo bārhaspatyaś ca paśavaḥ //
17.1.27.a.d: पूर्वेद्युर् आग्नेयः सौम्यो बार्हस्पत्यश् च पशवः ॥
17.1.27.a.m: On the previous day, the victims are sacred to Agni, Soma, and Bṛhaspati.

17.1.28.a.s: tadālabha etāsāṃ devatānām ānupūrvyeṇāgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaś carū cetarau //
17.1.28.a.d: तदालभ एतासां देवतानाम् आनुपूर्व्येणाग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपालश् चरू चेतरौ ॥
17.1.28.a.m: Instead of seizing them, in the order of these deities, there is an eight-potsherd cake sacred to Agni, and two boiled rice messes for the other two.

17.1.30.a.m: He sprinkles clarified butter crosswise on the high altar.

17.1.32.a.s: hiraṇyaṃ mukhe 'nvāsyāntarau priyāyai bhāryāyai brahmacārī śete //
17.1.32.a.d: हिरण्यं मुखे ऽन्वास्यान्तरौ प्रियायै भार्यायै ब्रह्मचारी शेते ॥
17.1.32.a.m: Having placed gold in his mouth, he lies between [them] near his beloved wife, living as a celibate student.

17.1.33.a.m: [Saying,] 'I will sacrifice with the offering', the officiating priests have [their fires] mounted [upon themselves].

17.1.34.a.s: tān nidhāya śvo bhūte sarvadiśo 'śvarathā sakṣīradṛtayaḥ somapravākā vidhāvanti //
17.1.34.a.d: तान् निधाय श्वो भूते सर्वदिशो ऽश्वरथा सक्षीरदृतयः सोमप्रवाका विधावन्ति ॥
17.1.34.a.m: Having deposited them, when the morrow has dawned, soma-heralds with horse-drawn chariots and milk-skins run out in all directions.

17.1.35.a.s: tebhyo yan navanītam udīyāt tad ājye 'vanayet //
17.1.35.a.d: तेभ्यो यन् नवनीतम् उदीयात् तद् आज्ये ऽवनयेत् ॥
17.1.35.a.m: Whatever fresh butter should emerge from them, he should pour that into the clarified butter.

17.1.36.a.s: yo jane caturyujā prācyāṃ diśi yugyakrośotsargeṇetarāsu prasavyam̐ sthūriṇāṃ tataḥ parikramayed aśvatarī ratho vaikapradakṣiṇaṃ yojanādīni vā krośāny aśvarathena pradakṣiṇam //
17.1.36.a.d: यो जने चतुर्युजा प्राच्यां दिशि युग्यक्रोशोत्सर्गेणेतरासु प्रसव्यम्̐ स्थूरिणां ततः परिक्रमयेद् अश्वतरी रथो वैकप्रदक्षिणं योजनादीनि वा क्रोशान्य् अश्वरथेन प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
17.1.36.a.m: With a four-horse chariot in the eastern direction at a yojana; in the other [directions], with a single-horse chariot counterclockwise, at an interval of a krośa; from there he should drive around; or a mule-chariot in a single clockwise turn; or a yojana and other krośas clockwise with a horse-chariot.

17.1.38.a.m: A three-year-old uncastrated bull is the soma-purchase price.

17.1.39.a.m: During the Upasads, he should close his eyes three times.

17.1.42.a.m: A threshing floor of barley is the high altar.

17.1.45.a.m: The wooden sword is the sacrificial post, or [a post] with the tip like a wooden sword, or the threshing post.

17.1.46.a.s: agnīṣomīyakāle 'gnīṣomīyam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati / ījānasya gṛhād vasatīvarīr gṛhṇāti //
17.1.46.a.d: अग्नीषोमीयकाले ऽग्नीषोमीयम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपति । ईजानस्य गृहाद् वसतीवरीर् गृह्णाति ॥
17.1.46.a.m: At the time of the animal sacrifice to Agni and Soma, he offers an eleven-potsherd cake sacred to Agni and Soma. He draws the Vasatīvarī waters from the house of one who has sacrificed.

17.1.47.a.m: At the time of the press-day victims, he seizes the victims together:

17.1.48.a.m: the one for Agni and Soma, the one for the press-day, and the concluding animal victim.

17.1.49.a.s: agnīṣomīyasya sthāne 'gnīṣomīya ekādaśakapālo 'nūbandhyāyāḥ sthāne maitrāvaruṇyābhikṣayā yajeta //
17.1.49.a.d: अग्नीषोमीयस्य स्थाने ऽग्नीषोमीय एकादशकपालो ऽनूबन्ध्यायाः स्थाने मैत्रावरुण्याभिक्षया यजेत ॥
17.1.49.a.m: In place of the animal victim for Agni and Soma, there is an eleven-potsherd cake sacred to Agni and Soma; in place of the concluding animal victim, he should sacrifice with a curd-mixture sacred to Mitra and Varuṇa.

17.1.50.a.m: A good white horse is the sacrificial gift.

17.1.51.a.m: He should give it to a descendant of Aṅgiras or to a rival.

17.1.52.a.s: dveṣyaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vṛtvā tasmā aśvam̐ śvetam̐ rukmapratiyuktaṃ dadyāt //
17.1.52.a.d: द्वेष्यं वा ब्राह्मणं वृत्वा तस्मा अश्वम्̐ श्वेतम्̐ रुक्मप्रतियुक्तं दद्यात् ॥
17.1.52.a.m: Or having chosen an enemy brāhmaṇa, he should give him a white horse adorned with gold.

17.1.53.a.s: saṃvatsaraṃ noparyupaviśet / na mām̐sam aśnīyāt / na striyaṃ nāvapadyeta / na pādāv avanenijīta nāñjīta nābhyañjīta / sā dikṣā / yadi saṃvatsaraṃ nodāśam̐sīta / dvādaśāham //
17.1.53.a.d: संवत्सरं नोपर्युपविशेत् । न माम्̐सम् अश्नीयात् । न स्त्रियं नावपद्येत । न पादाव् अवनेनिजीत नाञ्जीत नाभ्यञ्जीत । सा दिक्षा । यदि संवत्सरं नोदाशम्̐सीत । द्वादशाहम् ॥
17.1.53.a.m: For a year he should not sit on a raised seat; he should not eat meat; he should not approach a woman; he should not wash his feet; he should not apply eye-salve nor anoint himself. That is the consecration. If he cannot hold out for a year, [then] for twelve days.

17.2.1.a.s: dvitīyasyaikavim̐śatim agniṣṭomasāma kṛtvāmayāvinaṃ yājayed etenānnādyakāmaṃ prajākāmaṃ paśukāmaṃ vā //
17.2.1.a.d: द्वितीयस्यैकविम्̐शतिम् अग्निष्टोमसाम कृत्वामयाविनं याजयेद् एतेनान्नाद्यकामं प्रजाकामं पशुकामं वा ॥
17.2.1.a.m: Having made the twenty-one-fold chant the Agniṣṭoma sāman for the second, he should make one who is sick sacrifice with it, or one who desires food, or one who desires offspring, or one who desires cattle.

17.2.3.a.m: For the third and fourth, the latter two Pavamānas are eighteen-fold.

17.2.4.a.s: parokṣapṛṣṭhau vā caturaṣṭādaśaḥ / pañcamo hotur ājyam aṣṭādaśāv uttarau pavamānau / hotuḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ parikrīś caturvim̐śabahiṣpavamānaḥ svargakāmā bhavanti //
17.2.4.a.d: परोक्षपृष्ठौ वा चतुरष्टादशः । पञ्चमो होतुर् आज्यम् अष्टादशाव् उत्तरौ पवमानौ । होतुः पृष्ठं परिक्रीश् चतुर्विम्̐शबहिष्पवमानः स्वर्गकामा भवन्ति ॥
17.2.4.a.m: Or [they have] indirect Pṛṣṭhas, four of eighteen [verses]; the fifth is the hotṛ's Ājya-śastra; the latter two Pavamānas are eighteen-fold; the hotṛ's Pṛṣṭha is the Parikrī; the Bahiṣpavamāna is twenty-four-fold: they become desirous of heaven.

17.2.5.a.d: हीनानुजावरो ऽनुक्रिया । तस्य चतुर्विम्̐शाव् उत्तरौ पवमानौ ॥
17.2.5.a.m: For one who is left behind or born after, the Anukriyā [is performed]; its latter two Pavamānas are twenty-four-fold.

17.2.7.a.m: And carrying curd-skin at three krośas, he announces at the end.

17.2.8.a.m: A cow is the soma-purchase price.

17.2.10.a.s: saṃmīlanaṃ vedir havirdhāne 'gnīṣomīyo vasatīvarīr dakṣiṇā ca //
17.2.10.a.d: संमीलनं वेदिर् हविर्धाने ऽग्नीषोमीयो वसतीवरीर् दक्षिणा च ॥
17.2.10.a.m: The closing of the eyes, the altar, the Havirdhāna carts, the animal victim for Agni and Soma, the Vasatīvarī waters, and the sacrificial gift [are identical with the first].

17.2.11.a.m: And here the selection of an enemy is the same as in the first.

17.2.12.a.m: Whatever [is performed] for sovereign rule, he immediately attains sovereign rule.

17.2.13.a.m: By Agni's Agniṣṭoma he secures all food.

17.2.14.a.m: Prajāpati's Ekatrika is an Agniṣṭoma; he attains Prajāpati.

17.2.15.a.s: bhrātṛvyepsāyām anukriyau paśvālambho bhojanam̐ hiraṇyānvasanam̐ śayyāvanayanam / prathamena samānam̐ sadaḥ //
17.2.15.a.d: भ्रातृव्येप्सायाम् अनुक्रियौ पश्वालम्भो भोजनम्̐ हिरण्यान्वसनम्̐ शय्यावनयनम् । प्रथमेन समानम्̐ सदः ॥
17.2.15.a.m: When wishing to harm a rival, there are two Anukriyās: the seizing of the victim, the eating, the placing of gold, the bed, and the pouring out. The Sadas is identical with the first.

17.2.16.a.m: There is a soma-herald and curd-skin.

17.2.17.a.s: atrāśvipadaṃ paraṃ madhye krośa ṛtvijo virahitā bhavanti //
17.2.17.a.d: अत्राश्विपदं परं मध्ये क्रोश ऋत्विजो विरहिता भवन्ति ॥
17.2.17.a.m: Here, at a horse-step beyond in the middle of a krośa, the officiating priests are separated.

17.2.18.a.s: ta enaṃ prātar upasametya prajāpatir godhūmorvarā vedir godhūmānāṃ khala uttaravedir ārohaṇe havirdhāne vimitam̐ sadaḥ / sphyo yūpaḥ sphyāgraḥ khalevālī vā / vaḍavā śvetā dakṣiṇā / brahmaṇe deyā / yathāprakṛtītarebhyaḥ parikriyā caturvim̐śatistotrīyeṇa bhrātṛvyāya procya yajeta / viśvajicchilpena sarvastomena sarvān kāmān avāpnoti //
17.2.18.a.d: त एनं प्रातर् उपसमेत्य प्रजापतिर् गोधूमोर्वरा वेदिर् गोधूमानां खल उत्तरवेदिर् आरोहणे हविर्धाने विमितम्̐ सदः । स्फ्यो यूपः स्फ्याग्रः खलेवाली वा । वडवा श्वेता दक्षिणा । ब्रह्मणे देया । यथाप्रकृतीतरेभ्यः परिक्रिया चतुर्विम्̐शतिस्तोत्रीयेण भ्रातृव्याय प्रोच्य यजेत । विश्वजिच्छिल्पेन सर्वस्तोमेन सर्वान् कामान् अवाप्नोति ॥
17.2.18.a.m: They, approaching him in the morning, [recite]: 'Prajāpati...'. A wheat-field is the altar; a threshing floor of wheat is the high altar; two carts mounted with climbing ladders are the Havirdhāna carts; a shed is the Sadas; the wooden sword is the sacrificial post, or [a post] with the tip like a wooden sword, or the threshing post. A white mare is the sacrificial gift; it is to be given to the brahman priest. For the others, [gifts are] according to the norm. Having proclaimed the hiring by means of a twenty-four-versed stoma for the rival, he should sacrifice. By the craft of the Viśvajit, with all stomas, he obtains all desires.

17.2.19.a.m: Practicing sorcery, one should sacrifice with the Śyena.

17.2.21.a.m: The sacrificial post is of Tilvaka wood or of Bādhaka wood, with a tip shaped like a wooden sword.

17.2.22.a.m: The two pressing-boards are made of the wood of a cart axle or corpse-hearse.

17.2.23.a.m: A red animal is for Agni accompanied by Rudra.

17.2.24.a.m: He sets down the upāṃśu and antaryāma cups.

17.2.27.a.m: The officiating priests perform the rites wearing red turbans, red garments, and wearing the sacred cord around the neck.

17.2.28.a.m: The sacrificial gifts are nine each: [animals that are] crop-eared, hornless, and polled.

17.2.29.a.m: At the time of giving the sacrificial gifts, they should prick them with thorns.

17.2.30.a.s: trayo vācastomās teṣāṃ dvāv agniṣṭomau / sarvastomo 'tirātra uttamaḥ / tasmin sarvā ṛcaḥ sarvāṇi sāmāni sarvāṇi yajūm̐ṣi prayujyeran //
17.2.30.a.d: त्रयो वाचस्तोमास् तेषां द्वाव् अग्निष्टोमौ । सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्र उत्तमः । तस्मिन् सर्वा ऋचः सर्वाणि सामानि सर्वाणि यजूम्̐षि प्रयुज्येरन् ॥
17.2.30.a.m: There are three Vācastomas; of these, two are Agniṣṭomas; the last is a Sarvastoma Atirātra. In that [last one], all Ṛgvedic verses, all Sāmavedic chants, and all Yajurvedic formulas should be employed.

17.2.31.a.m: The Vrātyastomas are for the wandering life of Vrātyas.

17.2.32.a.s: trivṛto 'gniṣṭomo rathaṃtarasāmāna ukthyā dviṣatīḥ ṣoḍaśīḥ sarveṣām //
17.2.32.a.d: त्रिवृतो ऽग्निष्टोमो रथंतरसामान उक्थ्या द्विषतीः षोडशीः सर्वेषाम् ॥
17.2.32.a.m: The Agniṣṭoma is a ninefold chant; the Ukthyas have the Rathaṃtara chant as their Sāman, [or] sixteenfold chants with two hundred verses, for all of them.

17.2.33.a.s: uṣṇīṣaṃ pratodo jyāhroḍo ratho vipathaḥ phalakāstīrṇo 'śvo 'śvataraś ca yugyau kṛṣṇaṃ vāsaḥ kṛṣṇavalakṣe ajine rājato niṣkaḥ //
17.2.33.a.d: उष्णीषं प्रतोदो ज्याह्रोडो रथो विपथः फलकास्तीर्णो ऽश्वो ऽश्वतरश् च युग्यौ कृष्णं वासः कृष्णवलक्षे अजिने राजतो निष्कः ॥
17.2.33.a.m: A turban, a goad, a bow without an arrow, an unpaved rough chariot, a horse and a mule as yoke-animals, a black garment, two black-and-white skins, and a silver ornament—

17.2.35.a.m: Garments with fringed borders and hem-cords belong to the others.

17.2.38.a.m: They join the leader in groups of thirty-three each.

17.2.40.a.s: api vā ṣaṭṣaṣṭir gāvo dakṣiṇā bhavanti //
17.2.40.a.d: अपि वा षट्षष्टिर् गावो दक्षिणा भवन्ति ॥
17.2.40.a.m: Or sixty-six cows become the sacrificial gifts.

17.2.41.a.s: atho khalv āhur yad evaiṣām̐ saṃpāditam̐ syāt tad dadyus tad dhi vrātyadhanam iti vijñāyate //
17.2.41.a.d: अथो खल्व् आहुर् यद् एवैषाम्̐ संपादितम्̐ स्यात् तद् दद्युस् तद् धि व्रात्यधनम् इति विज्ञायते ॥
17.2.41.a.m: Moreover, they say: Whatever wealth they have gathered, that they should give; for it is known [from sacred tradition], 'That is the property of the Vrātya.'

17.2.42.a.s: ṣaṭṣoḍaśī ninditānām / dviṣoḍaśī kaniṣṭhānām / ūrdhvastomo jyeṣṭhānām / catuṣṣoḍaśī sarveṣām //
17.2.42.a.d: षट्षोडशी निन्दितानाम् । द्विषोडशी कनिष्ठानाम् । ऊर्ध्वस्तोमो ज्येष्ठानाम् । चतुष्षोडशी सर्वेषाम् ॥
17.2.42.a.m: A six-ṣoḍaśin rite is for the censured; a two-ṣoḍaśin rite for the youngest; an elevated stoma for the eldest; a four-ṣoḍaśin rite for all.

17.2.43.a.m: The Prayati of the Ādityas is an Ukthya, the first among the Nākasads.

17.2.44.a.m: They attain separation from evil and from the rival.

17.2.45.a.s: agniṣṭomā itare aṅgirasāṃ dvitīyaḥ / sādhyānāṃ tṛtīyaḥ / marutāṃ caturthenaujo vīryam āpnoti / trayastrim̐śaḥ pañcama ity eke / prājāpatyaḥ pañcamaḥ / prajākāmo 'bhibhavā bhrātṛvyam abhibhavati / vinuttyā bhrātṛvyaṃ vinudate //
17.2.45.a.d: अग्निष्टोमा इतरे अङ्गिरसां द्वितीयः । साध्यानां तृतीयः । मरुतां चतुर्थेनौजो वीर्यम् आप्नोति । त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शः पञ्चम इत्य् एके । प्राजापत्यः पञ्चमः । प्रजाकामो ऽभिभवा भ्रातृव्यम् अभिभवति । विनुत्त्या भ्रातृव्यं विनुदते ॥
17.2.45.a.m: The others are Agniṣṭomas: the second belongs to the Aṅgirases; the third belongs to the Sādhyas; through the fourth, belonging to the Maruts, one obtains vigor and heroism; the fifth is a thirty-three-fold chant, according to some; the fifth belongs to Prajāpati; one desirous of offspring overcomes his rival by the Abhibhū rite; by the Vinutti rite, he drives away his rival.

17.2.46.a.m: One desirous of procreation [should perform] the Citistoma.

17.2.47.a.s: gāyatreṇokthyena rathaṃtarasāmnā brāhmaṇaḥ purodhākāmo yajet / dvau gāyatrau pūrvo brāhmaṇasya //
17.2.47.a.d: गायत्रेणोक्थ्येन रथंतरसाम्ना ब्राह्मणः पुरोधाकामो यजेत् । द्वौ गायत्रौ पूर्वो ब्राह्मणस्य ॥
17.2.47.a.m: A brāhmaṇa desirous of the office of domestic priest should sacrifice with an Ukthya based on the Gāyatra tune having the Rathaṃtara as its Sāman; there are two Gāyatra rites, the former is for a brāhmaṇa;

17.2.49.a.s: tejo brahmavarcasaṃ brāhmaṇasya pūrveṇa kṣatriyasyottareṇogramavyathaṃ na tu bahupaśū bhavataḥ //
17.2.49.a.d: तेजो ब्रह्मवर्चसं ब्राह्मणस्य पूर्वेण क्षत्रियस्योत्तरेणोग्रमव्यथं न तु बहुपशू भवतः ॥
17.2.49.a.m: Splendor and spiritual luster belong to the brāhmaṇa through the former; through the latter, terrible power and freedom from pain belong to the kṣatriya; but they do not become rich in cattle.

17.2.50.a.m: An unpurified person should sacrifice with the threefold Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma.

17.2.51.a.m: The introductory formulas are addressed to Agni; the Subrahmaṇyā formula is addressed to Agni.

17.2.52.a.d: आग्नेयीषु स्तुवते ऽजां हिरण्यं च दक्षिणा ॥
17.2.52.a.m: They chant the praise on verses addressed to Agni; a she-goat and gold are the sacrificial gift.

17.2.53.a.s: etam eva catuḥṣṭomaṃ kṛtvā śrotriyo 'kṣahataḥ strīhataḥ kāmahataś caraṇahato vā yajeta //
17.2.53.a.d: एतम् एव चतुःष्टोमं कृत्वा श्रोत्रियो ऽक्षहतः स्त्रीहतः कामहतश् चरणहतो वा यजेत ॥
17.2.53.a.m: A learned brāhmaṇa ruined by dice, ruined by women, ruined by passion, or ruined in his conduct should sacrifice, having made this very rite into a four-stoma one.

17.2.56.a.m: To the others according to the standard model.

17.2.57.a.s: etasyaiva vāyavyāsu pañcadaśam agniṣṭomasāma kṛtvāmayāvinaṃ yājayet / annādyakāmaṃ prajākāmaṃ paśukāmaṃ vā //
17.2.57.a.d: एतस्यैव वायव्यासु पञ्चदशम् अग्निष्टोमसाम कृत्वामयाविनं याजयेत् । अन्नाद्यकामं प्रजाकामं पशुकामं वा ॥
17.2.57.a.m: Having made the fifteenfold chant the Agniṣṭoma-sāman of this very rite on verses addressed to Vāyu, he should cause one who is chronically ill to sacrifice, or one desirous of food, or one desirous of offspring, or one desirous of cattle.

17.2.58.a.s: etasyaiva revatīṣu vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma kṛtvā brahmavarcasakāmam / etasyaiva śakvarīṣu vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma kṛtvā paśukāmam / etam eva catuḥṣṭomaṃ kṛtvā grāmakāmaḥ / apravargyā bhavantīty eke / trivṛtāgniṣṭutā brahmavarcasakāmaḥ / pañcadaśenāgniṣṭutā vīryakāmaḥ //
17.2.58.a.d: एतस्यैव रेवतीषु वारवन्तीयम् अग्निष्टोमसाम कृत्वा ब्रह्मवर्चसकामम् । एतस्यैव शक्वरीषु वारवन्तीयम् अग्निष्टोमसाम कृत्वा पशुकामम् । एतम् एव चतुःष्टोमं कृत्वा ग्रामकामः । अप्रवर्ग्या भवन्तीत्य् एके । त्रिवृताग्निष्टुता ब्रह्मवर्चसकामः । पञ्चदशेनाग्निष्टुता वीर्यकामः ॥
17.2.58.a.m: Having made the Vāravantīya chant the Agniṣṭoma-sāman of this very rite on Revatī verses, for one desirous of spiritual luster; having made the Vāravantīya chant the Agniṣṭoma-sāman of this very rite on Śakvarī verses, for one desirous of cattle; having made this very rite into a four-stoma one, for one desirous of a village; according to some, these rites are without the Pravargya; with the threefold Agniṣṭut, for one desirous of spiritual luster; with the fifteenfold Agniṣṭut, for one desirous of heroism.

17.2.59.a.s: saptadaśenāgniṣṭutāgniṣṭomena yajñavibhraṣṭo yajeta / yasmin vā yajñakratau vibhram̐śet //
17.2.59.a.d: सप्तदशेनाग्निष्टुताग्निष्टोमेन यज्ञविभ्रष्टो यजेत । यस्मिन् वा यज्ञक्रतौ विभ्रम्̐शेत् ॥
17.2.59.a.m: One who has fallen from a sacrifice should sacrifice with the seventeenfold Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma, or at whichever sacrificial rite he may have fallen away.

17.2.60.a.m: The threefold chant is for one who speaks blameable speech.

17.2.61.a.m: The fifteenfold chant is for one who slays someone who ought not to be slain.

17.2.62.a.s: saptadaśo 'nāśānnasya bhojane prāśyaikavim̐śo janaṃ yato gāndhārakaliṅgamāgadhān pāraskarān sauvīrān vā //
17.2.62.a.d: सप्तदशो ऽनाशान्नस्य भोजने प्राश्यैकविम्̐शो जनं यतो गान्धारकलिङ्गमागधान् पारस्करान् सौवीरान् वा ॥
17.2.62.a.m: The seventeenfold chant is for one who has eaten the food of someone whose food should not be eaten; having consumed [such food], the twenty-one-fold chant is for one going among the people of Gandhāra, Kaliṅga, Magadha, Pāraskara, or Sauvīra.

17.2.64.a.s: pañcadaśena vīryakāmaḥ / saptadaśena prajākamaḥ / ekavim̐śena pratiṣṭhākāmaḥ / trayastrim̐śena svargakāmaḥ //
17.2.64.a.d: पञ्चदशेन वीर्यकामः । सप्तदशेन प्रजाकमः । एकविम्̐शेन प्रतिष्ठाकामः । त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शेन स्वर्गकामः ॥
17.2.64.a.m: With the fifteenfold chant, for one desirous of heroism; with the seventeenfold chant, for one desirous of offspring; with the twenty-one-fold chant, for one desirous of stability; with the thirty-three-fold chant, for one desirous of heaven.

17.2.65.a.s: apivā jyotiṣṭoma eva / agniṣṭome sarvān kāmān kāmayet //
17.2.65.a.d: अपिवा ज्योतिष्टोम एव । अग्निष्टोमे सर्वान् कामान् कामयेत् ॥
17.2.65.a.m: Or rather, in the Jyotiṣṭoma alone, in the Agniṣṭoma, he should desire all desires.

17.3.1.a.m: One desirous of food should sacrifice with the threefold Agniṣṭoma without recitation of specific deity names.

17.3.2.a.m: According to some, the morning pressing is without recitation of specific deity names.

17.3.3.a.s: aśvaḥ śveto dakṣiṇā / sa brahmaṇe deyaḥ //
17.3.3.a.d: अश्वः श्वेतो दक्षिणा । स ब्रह्मणे देयः ॥
17.3.3.a.m: A white horse is the sacrificial gift; it is to be given to the brahman priest.

17.3.5.a.s: brāhmaṇo brahmavarcasakāmaḥ purodhākāmo vā yajeta / yaṃ vā sthāpatyāyābhiṣiñceyuḥ //
17.3.5.a.d: ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मवर्चसकामः पुरोधाकामो वा यजेत । यं वा स्थापत्यायाभिषिञ्चेयुः ॥
17.3.5.a.m: A brāhmaṇa desirous of spiritual luster or desirous of the office of domestic priest should sacrifice, or one whom they would consecrate to governorship.

17.3.6.a.m: The hotṛ wears a garland around his neck.

17.3.7.a.m: [The victim is] reddish-brown, blinking, and white-spotted in three places.

17.3.8.a.s: bṛhaspate juṣasva nas iti bārhaspatyam atigrāhyaṃ gṛhṇāti //
17.3.8.a.d: बृहस्पते जुषस्व नस् इति बार्हस्पत्यम् अतिग्राह्यं गृह्णाति ॥
17.3.8.a.m: He draws the extra cup for Bṛhaspati with the mantra: 'O Bṛhaspati, take pleasure in us.'

17.3.9.a.m: An animal sacred to Bṛhaspati is to be seized.

17.3.10.a.s: prātaḥsavane sanneṣu nārāśam̐seṣv ekādaśa dakṣiṇā vyādiśati //
17.3.10.a.d: प्रातःसवने सन्नेषु नाराशम्̐सेष्व् एकादश दक्षिणा व्यादिशति ॥
17.3.10.a.m: At the morning pressing, when the Nārāśaṃsa cups are placed down, he assigns eleven sacrificial gifts.

17.3.11.a.s: ājyena mādhyaṃdine savane 'gnim anvārabdhaṃ kṛṣṇājine 'bhiṣiñcati / yathāgnicityāyām̐ śukrāmanthinor vā sam̐srāveṇa //
17.3.11.a.d: आज्येन माध्यंदिने सवने ऽग्निम् अन्वारब्धं कृष्णाजिने ऽभिषिञ्चति । यथाग्निचित्यायाम्̐ शुक्रामन्थिनोर् वा सम्̐स्रावेण ॥
17.3.11.a.m: At the midday pressing, while [the sacrificer] holds onto the fire, he consecrates him on a black antelope skin with clarified butter, as in the piling of the fire altar, or with the residue of the Śukra and Manthin cups.

17.3.12.a.s: aśvadvādaśa mādhyaṃdine savane tā ubhayīr upākaroti / dvādaśa tṛtīyasavane //
17.3.12.a.d: अश्वद्वादश माध्यंदिने सवने ता उभयीर् उपाकरोति । द्वादश तृतीयसवने ॥
17.3.12.a.m: Twelve, including a horse, at the midday pressing—he brings up both of these; twelve at the third pressing.

17.3.14.a.s: apivāṣṭau prātaḥsavana ekādaśa mādhyaṃdine savane dvādaśa tṛtīyasavane / aśvaṃ tṛtīyaśo 'nusavanaṃ dadyād ity ekeṣām / sarvā mādhyaṃdine savana ity eke //
17.3.14.a.d: अपिवाष्टौ प्रातःसवन एकादश माध्यंदिने सवने द्वादश तृतीयसवने । अश्वं तृतीयशो ऽनुसवनं दद्याद् इत्य् एकेषाम् । सर्वा माध्यंदिने सवन इत्य् एके ॥
17.3.14.a.m: Or else, eight at the morning pressing, eleven at the midday pressing, twelve at the third pressing; according to some, one should give a horse at each pressing in three parts; according to some, all at the midday pressing.

17.3.15.a.s: manasetarayoḥ savanayor na vā manasā ca na //
17.3.15.a.d: मनसेतरयोः सवनयोर् न वा मनसा च न ॥
17.3.15.a.m: Mentally at the other two pressings, or not even mentally.

17.3.16.a.m: Having made the Iṣu rite a modification of the threefold Agniṣṭoma, one practicing malevolent sorcery should sacrifice.

17.3.17.a.m: The rest is the same as the Śyena.

17.3.20.a.s: maraṇakāmo yajeta yaḥ kāmayetānāmayatāṃ svargaṃ lokam iyām iti vijñāyate //
17.3.20.a.d: मरणकामो यजेत यः कामयेतानामयतां स्वर्गं लोकम् इयाम् इति विज्ञायते ॥
17.3.20.a.m: One wishing for death should sacrifice; 'He who desires, "May I go to the heavenly world free from disease,"' so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

17.3.21.a.m: A victim for Yama, yellowish-green like a parrot, is to be seized.

17.3.23.a.s: ārbhave stūyamāne dakṣiṇenaudumbarīm ahatena vāsasā pattodaśena prāvṛtya dakṣiṇāśirāḥ saṃviśati brāhmaṇāḥ samāpayatam etaṃ yajñam iti // yajñasam̐sthām anu saṃtiṣṭhate //
17.3.23.a.d: आर्भवे स्तूयमाने दक्षिणेनौदुम्बरीम् अहतेन वाससा पत्तोदशेन प्रावृत्य दक्षिणाशिराः संविशति ब्राह्मणाः समापयतम् एतं यज्ञम् इति ॥ यज्ञसम्̐स्थाम् अनु संतिष्ठते ॥
17.3.23.a.m: While the Ārbhava-stotra is being chanted, having covered himself to the south of the audumbarī post with an unwashed garment with fringes at the feet, with his head toward the south, he lies down, saying: 'O brahmins, bring this sacrifice to completion!' He departs following the conclusion of the sacrifice.

17.3.24.a.s: pṛthag araṇīṣv agnīn samārohyottaranārāyaṇenādityam upasthāyāraṇyam abhipraiti / yadi grāme vivaset pṛthag araṇīṣv agnīn samārohyottaranārāyaṇenādityam upasthāya gṛheṣu pratyavasyet / yady anabhiprāpnuyāt tān yajñakratūn āha / tena bhūr ukthyo rathaṃtarasāmā / bhūtikāmo yajeta / dhenur dakṣiṇā //
17.3.24.a.d: पृथग् अरणीष्व् अग्नीन् समारोह्योत्तरनारायणेनादित्यम् उपस्थायारण्यम् अभिप्रैति । यदि ग्रामे विवसेत् पृथग् अरणीष्व् अग्नीन् समारोह्योत्तरनारायणेनादित्यम् उपस्थाय गृहेषु प्रत्यवस्येत् । यद्य् अनभिप्राप्नुयात् तान् यज्ञक्रतून् आह । तेन भूर् उक्थ्यो रथंतरसामा । भूतिकामो यजेत । धेनुर् दक्षिणा ॥
17.3.24.a.m: Having mounted the fires separately onto the kindling sticks and worshipped the sun with the Uttaranārāyaṇa hymn, he goes out toward the forest. If he should reside in a settlement, having mounted the fires separately onto the kindling sticks and worshipped the sun with the Uttaranārāyaṇa hymn, he should settle down into the houses. If he should not attain [his wish], he mentions those sacrificial rites: By that, [one performs] the Bhūḥ rite, an Ukthya with the Rathaṃtara-sāman; one desiring prosperity should sacrifice; a milch-cow is the sacrificial fee.

17.3.25.a.m: Imperishable indeed is the good deed of one who performs the seasonal sacrifices.

17.3.26.a.m: A ninefold Agniṣṭoma in place of the Vaiśvadeva.

17.3.27.a.m: An animal victim for the Viśvedevas; a concluding animal sacrifice for Bṛhaspati.

17.3.29.a.m: They do not strew the high altar.

17.3.30.a.s: paridhau paśuṃ niyuñjanti / ulmuke barhiṣi vā / uttareṣu viminvanti / yūpān uttaravedim upavapanti //
17.3.30.a.d: परिधौ पशुं नियुञ्जन्ति । उल्मुके बर्हिषि वा । उत्तरेषु विमिन्वन्ति । यूपान् उत्तरवेदिम् उपवपन्ति ॥
17.3.30.a.m: They tie the animal victim to an enclosure stick, or to a firebrand, or to the sacred grass. In the subsequent ones, they erect [the posts]; they strew the sacrificial posts [and] the high altar.

17.3.31.a.s: tataś caturṣu māseṣu varuṇapraghāsānāṃ loke trirātro 'gniṣṭoma ukthyo 'tirātraḥ / mārutaḥ paśuḥ / vāruṇo dvitīyaḥ / maitrāvaruṇy anūbandhyā //
17.3.31.a.d: ततश् चतुर्षु मासेषु वरुणप्रघासानां लोके त्रिरात्रो ऽग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यो ऽतिरात्रः । मारुतः पशुः । वारुणो द्वितीयः । मैत्रावरुण्य् अनूबन्ध्या ॥
17.3.31.a.m: Then, in the fourth month, in place of the Varuṇapraghāsa rites, a three-day rite consisting of an Agniṣṭoma, an Ukthya, and an Atirātra; an animal victim for the Maruts, a second for Varuṇa; a concluding animal sacrifice for Mitra-Varuṇa.

17.3.32.a.s: tataś caturṣu māseṣu sākamedhānāṃ loke trirātro 'gniṣṭoma utkhyo 'tirātraḥ //
17.3.32.a.d: ततश् चतुर्षु मासेषु साकमेधानां लोके त्रिरात्रो ऽग्निष्टोम उत्ख्यो ऽतिरात्रः ॥
17.3.32.a.m: Then, in the fourth month, in place of the Sākamedha rites, a three-day rite consisting of an Agniṣṭoma, an Ukthya, and an Atirātra.

17.3.33.a.s: āgneyaḥ paśur aindrāgno dvitīyaḥ / aikādaśinās tṛtīye prājāpatyo vā saury anūbandhyā //
17.3.33.a.d: आग्नेयः पशुर् ऐन्द्राग्नो द्वितीयः । ऐकादशिनास् तृतीये प्राजापत्यो वा सौर्य् अनूबन्ध्या ॥
17.3.33.a.m: An animal victim for Agni, a second for Indra-Agni; in the third, eleven animal victims or one for Prajāpati; a concluding animal sacrifice for Sūrya.

17.3.34.a.s: tataś caturṣu māseṣu śunāsīrīyasya loke catuḥṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomaḥ / vāyavyaḥ paśur āśviny anūbandhyā //
17.3.34.a.d: ततश् चतुर्षु मासेषु शुनासीरीयस्य लोके चतुःष्टोमो ऽग्निष्टोमः । वायव्यः पशुर् आश्विन्य् अनूबन्ध्या ॥
17.3.34.a.m: Then, in the fourth month, in place of the Śunāsīrīya, a fourfold-stoma Agniṣṭoma; an animal victim for Vāyu, a concluding animal sacrifice for the Aśvins.

17.3.35.a.s: sarvatrāhataṃ vāso vasāno 'vabhṛthād udetya kratvantarāleṣu / nānṛtaṃ vadati / na mām̐sam aśnāti / na striyam upaiti / noparyāste / jugupsetānṛtāt / prāṅ śete / na madhv aśnāti / nāñjīta / nābhyañjīta / ṛtau jāyām upeyāt //
17.3.35.a.d: सर्वत्राहतं वासो वसानो ऽवभृथाद् उदेत्य क्रत्वन्तरालेषु । नानृतं वदति । न माम्̐सम् अश्नाति । न स्त्रियम् उपैति । नोपर्यास्ते । जुगुप्सेतानृतात् । प्राङ् शेते । न मध्व् अश्नाति । नाञ्जीत । नाभ्यञ्जीत । ऋतौ जायाम् उपेयात् ॥
17.3.35.a.m: Throughout, wearing an unwashed garment after stepping out from the purificatory bath during the intervals between the rites: he does not speak falsehood; he does not eat meat; he does not approach a woman; he does not sit on an elevated seat; he should guard himself against untruth; he sleeps facing east; he does not eat honey; he should not apply collyrium; he should not anoint himself; he may approach his wife in her fertile period.

17.4.1.a.s: pañcāśad vaiśvadevasya dakṣiṇāḥ / śataṃ varuṇapraghāseṣu / adhyardhaśatam̐ sākamedheṣu / dvādaśaśatam̐ śunāsīrīye //
17.4.1.a.d: पञ्चाशद् वैश्वदेवस्य दक्षिणाः । शतं वरुणप्रघासेषु । अध्यर्धशतम्̐ साकमेधेषु । द्वादशशतम्̐ शुनासीरीये ॥
17.4.1.a.m: Fifty are the sacrificial fees of the Vaiśvadeva; a hundred in the Varuṇapraghāsas; one hundred and fifty in the Sākamedhas; one hundred and twelve in the Śunāsīrīya.

17.4.2.a.m: Or [they are given] according to each season, appropriately in the seasonal sacrifices.

17.4.3.a.m: [He gives] calves at the third pressing together with their mothers.

17.4.4.a.s: upahavyenāgniṣṭomena rathaṃtarasāmnā bṛhatsāmnobhayasāmnā vāmayāvinaṃ yājayed etenānnādyakāmaṃ prajākāmaṃ paśukāmaṃ vāśvaḥ śyāvo dakṣiṇā / sa brahmaṇe deyaḥ //
17.4.4.a.d: उपहव्येनाग्निष्टोमेन रथंतरसाम्ना बृहत्साम्नोभयसाम्ना वामयाविनं याजयेद् एतेनान्नाद्यकामं प्रजाकामं पशुकामं वाश्वः श्यावो दक्षिणा । स ब्रह्मणे देयः ॥
17.4.4.a.m: With the Upahavya Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara-sāman, the Bṛhat-sāman, or both sāmans, one should perform the sacrifice for a sick person; with this [he sacrifices] for one desiring food, one desiring offspring, or one desiring cattle; a dark horse is the sacrificial fee; it is to be given to the brahman priest.

17.4.5.a.m: To the others, according to the standard model.

17.4.6.a.m: With the Ṛtapeya Agniṣṭoma having the Bṛhat-sāman, a brahmin desiring heaven [sacrifices].

17.4.7.a.s: ṣaḍ dīkṣāḥ / ṣaḍ upasadaḥ / ghṛtavrato bhavati //
17.4.7.a.d: षड् दीक्षाः । षड् उपसदः । घृतव्रतो भवति ॥
17.4.7.a.m: There are six initiations, six Upasad days; he observes the clarified-butter vow.

17.4.8.a.s: yāvad idaṃ prathamam aṅgulikāṇḍaṃ tāvat krīte some vratam //
17.4.8.a.d: यावद् इदं प्रथमम् अङ्गुलिकाण्डं तावत् क्रीते सोमे व्रतम् ॥
17.4.8.a.m: His vow [subsists on food measuring] as much as this first joint of the finger once the soma is bought.

17.4.9.a.m: With the next [joint], he approaches the vow with the subsequent joint.

17.4.10.a.m: At night he sits facing the fire; by day, facing the sun.

17.4.11.a.s: ṛtam uktvā prasarpanti / ṛtaṃ vadanto bhakṣayanti //
17.4.11.a.d: ऋतम् उक्त्वा प्रसर्पन्ति । ऋतं वदन्तो भक्षयन्ति ॥
17.4.11.a.m: Having spoken the truth, they glide forward; speaking the truth, they consume [the soma].

17.4.12.a.s: audumbaraś camasaś catuḥsraktiḥ somasya pūrṇaḥ sagotrāya priyāya brahmaṇe deyaḥ //
17.4.12.a.d: औदुम्बरश् चमसश् चतुःस्रक्तिः सोमस्य पूर्णः सगोत्राय प्रियाय ब्रह्मणे देयः ॥
17.4.12.a.m: A four-cornered drinking cup made of udumbara wood filled with soma is to be given to a beloved brahman priest belonging to the same gotra.

17.4.13.a.m: To the others, according to the standard model.

17.4.14.a.s: bahuhiraṇyenāgniṣṭomenānaḍuho lokam āpnoti / jyotiṣmato lokāñ jayati //
17.4.14.a.d: बहुहिरण्येनाग्निष्टोमेनानडुहो लोकम् आप्नोति । ज्योतिष्मतो लोकाञ् जयति ॥
17.4.14.a.m: With the Bahuhiraṇya Agniṣṭoma, one attains the world of the draft-ox; he conquers radiant worlds.

17.4.15.a.s: dvādaśamānaṃ hiraṇyaṃ dīkṣaṇīyāyāṃ dadāti / dvis tāvat prāyaṇīyāyām //
17.4.15.a.d: द्वादशमानं हिरण्यं दीक्षणीयायां ददाति । द्विस् तावत् प्रायणीयायाम् ॥
17.4.15.a.m: He gives gold weighing twelve mānas at the initiation offering; twice as much at the introductory rite.

17.4.16.a.s: evam ata ūrdhvaṃ dviguṇābhyāsenātithyāyām upasatsu pravargyeṣv agnīṣomīyasya vapāyām̐ hutāyām agnīṣomīye savanīyasya hutāyāṃ vapāyām̐ savanīye prātaḥsavane //
17.4.16.a.d: एवम् अत ऊर्ध्वं द्विगुणाभ्यासेनातिथ्यायाम् उपसत्सु प्रवर्ग्येष्व् अग्नीषोमीयस्य वपायाम्̐ हुतायाम् अग्नीषोमीये सवनीयस्य हुतायां वपायाम्̐ सवनीये प्रातःसवने ॥
17.4.16.a.m: In this manner, thereafter with twofold doubling: at the guest offering, at the Upasads, at the Pravargyas, when the omentum of the animal for Agni-Soma has been offered, at the Agni-Soma animal rite, when the omentum of the offering-victim has been offered, at the offering-victim, at the morning pressing,

17.4.17.a.s: sanneṣu nārāśam̐seṣv avabhṛtheṣṭāv udayanīyāyām anūbandhyāvapāyām̐ hutāyām anūbandhyāyām udavasānīyāyām antataḥ //
17.4.17.a.d: सन्नेषु नाराशम्̐सेष्व् अवभृथेष्टाव् उदयनीयायाम् अनूबन्ध्यावपायाम्̐ हुतायाम् अनूबन्ध्यायाम् उदवसानीयायाम् अन्ततः ॥
17.4.17.a.m: when the Nārāśaṃsa cups are deposited, at the purificatory bath offering, at the concluding rite, when the omentum of the concluding animal sacrifice has been offered, at the concluding animal sacrifice, [and] at the concluding bath at the end.

17.4.18.a.m: With the ninefold Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara-sāman, a brahmin desiring spiritual splendor [sacrifices].

17.4.19.a.m: With the fifteenfold Indrastuta [or] Indrastoma Ukthya having the Bṛhat-sāman, a kṣatriya desiring valor [sacrifices].

17.4.20.a.m: With the seventeenfold Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma having the Kaṇvarathaṃtara-sāman, a vaiśya desiring cattle [sacrifices].

17.4.21.a.s: pratidhuṣā prātaḥsavane sarvānt somāñ cchrīṇāti / śṛtena mādhyaṃdine savane / dadhnā tṛtīyasavane //
17.4.21.a.d: प्रतिधुषा प्रातःसवने सर्वान्त् सोमाञ् च्छ्रीणाति । शृतेन माध्यंदिने सवने । दध्ना तृतीयसवने ॥
17.4.21.a.m: At the morning pressing, he mixes all the soma libations with fresh warm milk; with boiled milk at the midday pressing; with curd at the third pressing.

17.4.23.a.s: tīvrasutokthyena rathaṃtarasāmnā bṛhatsāmnobhayasāmnā vā somavāminaṃ yājayet //
17.4.23.a.d: तीव्रसुतोक्थ्येन रथंतरसाम्ना बृहत्साम्नोभयसाम्ना वा सोमवामिनं याजयेत् ॥
17.4.23.a.m: With the Tīvrasut Ukthya having the Rathaṃtara-sāman, the Bṛhat-sāman, or both sāmans, one should perform the sacrifice for one who has vomited soma.

17.4.24.a.s: somātipavitaṃ yājayed rājānam aparuddhaṃ grāmakāmaṃ prajākāmaṃ paśukāmam̐ śriyā pratyavarūḍham abhicaran yajetābhicaryamāṇo yajeta //
17.4.24.a.d: सोमातिपवितं याजयेद् राजानम् अपरुद्धं ग्रामकामं प्रजाकामं पशुकामम्̐ श्रिया प्रत्यवरूढम् अभिचरन् यजेताभिचर्यमाणो यजेत ॥
17.4.24.a.m: One should perform the sacrifice for one who has had soma pass through him, for an expelled king, for one desiring a village, for one desiring offspring, for one desiring cattle, or for one fallen from prosperity; one practicing sorcery should sacrifice; one against whom sorcery is practiced should sacrifice.

17.4.25.a.s: pratidhuṣā prātaḥsavane sarvān somāñ chrīṇāti / śṛtena mādhyaṃdine savane / dadhnā tṛtīyasavane / nītamiśreṇa vā //
17.4.25.a.d: प्रतिधुषा प्रातःसवने सर्वान् सोमाञ् छ्रीणाति । शृतेन माध्यंदिने सवने । दध्ना तृतीयसवने । नीतमिश्रेण वा ॥
17.4.25.a.m: At the morning pressing, he mixes all the soma libations with fresh warm milk; with boiled milk at the midday pressing; with curd at the third pressing; or with what is mixed with freshly churned milk.

17.4.27.a.m: They milk cows whose calves are fostered by others for boiled milk as the milk-admixture.

17.4.30.a.m: The priests smell them; they do not consume them.

17.4.31.a.m: They consume them during the chant of the Acchāvāka.

17.4.32.a.m: The subsidiary Hotṛs ask permission from the brahman priest.

17.4.33.a.s: yajamāna ṛtvija ubhāv adhvaryū sarve camasādhvaryavo 'cchāvākāya pratigṛṇanti //
17.4.33.a.d: यजमान ऋत्विज उभाव् अध्वर्यू सर्वे चमसाध्वर्यवो ऽच्छावाकाय प्रतिगृणन्ति ॥
17.4.33.a.m: The sacrificer, the priests, both adhvaryus, and all the cup-adhvaryus make the response to the Acchāvāka.

17.4.34.a.m: The set of eleven posts is erected facing east.

17.4.35.a.m: He raises the altar up to the sacrificial post.

17.4.36.a.s: vaḍavā śvetā dakṣiṇā / sā brahmaṇe deyā //
17.4.36.a.d: वडवा श्वेता दक्षिणा । सा ब्रह्मणे देया ॥
17.4.36.a.m: A white mare is the sacrificial fee; it is to be given to the brahman priest.

17.4.37.a.m: To the others, according to the standard model.

17.4.38.a.m: With the Marutstoma, a king and his domestic chaplain [attain] union.

17.4.39.a.s: athaiṣa rāṭ / yo rājyam āśam̐samāno na labheta sa etena yajeta //
17.4.39.a.d: अथैष राट् । यो राज्यम् आशम्̐समानो न लभेत स एतेन यजेत ॥
17.4.39.a.m: Now this Rāṭ rite: one who, hoping for kingship, does not obtain it, should sacrifice with this.

17.5.1.a.m: With the Virāj, one desiring food [sacrifices]; with the Svarāj, one desiring a firm footing.

17.5.1.b.s: bahu pratigṛhya yo garagīr iva manyeta sa punaḥstomena / anāśyānnasya vā bhuktvā / ayājyaṃ vā yājayitvety eke / yo laghur ivāpratiṣṭhitaḥ syāt sa etena / ekavim̐śenaupacchadena prajākāma ity eke //
17.5.1.b.d: बहु प्रतिगृह्य यो गरगीर् इव मन्येत स पुनःस्तोमेन । अनाश्यान्नस्य वा भुक्त्वा । अयाज्यं वा याजयित्वेत्य् एके । यो लघुर् इवाप्रतिष्ठितः स्यात् स एतेन । एकविम्̐शेनौपच्छदेन प्रजाकाम इत्य् एके ॥
17.5.1.b.m: He who, having accepted much, should consider himself as if swallowing poison, [should sacrifice] with the Punaḥstoma; or having eaten the food of one whose food must not be eaten; or, according to some, having sacrificed for one for whom one should not sacrifice; he who is, as it were, unstable and without a firm footing, should [sacrifice] with this; with the twenty-onefold Upacchada, one desiring offspring [sacrifices], according to some.

17.5.2.a.m: One desirous of firm standing [sacrifices] with the Aupacchada.

17.5.3.a.m: He sings along with each stotriya verse.

17.5.4.a.s: gandharvāpsaraso mādayantām iti prātaḥsavane 'dhastāt pūtabhṛtaḥ pām̐sūn upāsyati //
17.5.4.a.d: गन्धर्वाप्सरसो मादयन्ताम् इति प्रातःसवने ऽधस्तात् पूतभृतः पाम्̐सून् उपास्यति ॥
17.5.4.a.m: With [the mantra]: 'May the Gandharvas and Apsarases rejoice,' he casts dust beneath the pūtabhṛt at the morning soma-pressing.

17.5.5.a.s: gandharvā devā mādayantām iti mādhyaṃdine savane / gandharvāḥ pitaro mādayantām iti tṛtīyasavane //
17.5.5.a.d: गन्धर्वा देवा मादयन्ताम् इति माध्यंदिने सवने । गन्धर्वाः पितरो मादयन्ताम् इति तृतीयसवने ॥
17.5.5.a.m: With: 'May the Gandharvas, the gods, rejoice,' at the midday soma-pressing; with: 'May the Gandharvas, the ancestors, rejoice,' at the third soma-pressing.

17.5.6.a.m: They declare that this is 'scattering away.'

17.5.7.a.s: punastomena bahu pratigṛhya yo garagīr iva manyetābhiśasyamānasya bhūtvaiteṣām //
17.5.7.a.d: पुनस्तोमेन बहु प्रतिगृह्य यो गरगीर् इव मन्येताभिशस्यमानस्य भूत्वैतेषाम् ॥
17.5.7.a.m: With the Punaḥstoma [sacrifices] one who, having accepted much [in gifts], thinks himself as if swallowed poison, or having become the [sacrificial priest] of one accused [of sin]—among these.

17.5.8.a.m: One desirous of cattle [sacrifices] with the two Gotamacatuṣṭomas.

17.5.9.a.m: The second is an Ukthya possessing the Ṣoḍaśin.

17.5.10.a.m: The two victims are as if neuter.

17.5.11.a.m: One desirous of cattle [sacrifices] with the Udbhid and Balabhid.

17.5.12.a.m: Having sacrificed with the Udbhid, he should sacrifice after a year with the Balabhid.

17.5.13.a.m: He fills the interval with an [iṣṭi of] an eight-pot-sherd [cake] to Agni.

17.5.14.a.m: In both cases, he gives dakṣiṇās fully made up of the gāyatrī [number].

17.5.15.a.m: Eight at the first, eight at the second.

17.5.16.a.m: One desirous of honor [sacrifices] with the two Apacitis.

17.5.17.a.m: They are both characterized by both Sāmans.

17.5.18.a.s: pakṣibhyāṃ sāgnicityābhyāṃ yaḥ kāmayeta pakṣī jyotiṣmataḥ svargām̐l lokān anusaṃcareyam iti //
17.5.18.a.d: पक्षिभ्यां साग्निचित्याभ्यां यः कामयेत पक्षी ज्योतिष्मतः स्वर्गाम्̐ल् लोकान् अनुसंचरेयम् इति ॥
17.5.18.a.m: With the two Pakṣin sacrifices accompanied by fire-altar piling, [one sacrifices] who desires: 'May I, possessing wings, traverse the luminous heavenly worlds.'

17.5.19.a.m: With the Ṛṣabha Agniṣṭoma [he sacrifices] for a nobleman desirous of vigor.

17.5.21.a.m: One desirous of sovereignty [sacrifices] with the Gosava, an Ukthya having the Bṛhat and Rathaṃtara sāmans.

17.5.23.a.s: dakṣiṇenāhavanīyam anuddhate vedyai pratidhuṣā māhendrastotraṃ pratyabhiṣicyate // revaj jātaḥ sahasā vṛddhaḥ \ kṣatrāṇāṃ kṣatrabhṛttamo vayodhāḥ / \ mahān mahitve tastabhānaḥ \ kṣatre rāṣṭre ca jāgṛhi / \ prajāpates tvā parameṣṭhinaḥ svārājyenābhiṣiñcāmi \\ iti //
17.5.23.a.d: दक्षिणेनाहवनीयम् अनुद्धते वेद्यै प्रतिधुषा माहेन्द्रस्तोत्रं प्रत्यभिषिच्यते ॥ रेवज् जातः सहसा वृद्धः \ क्षत्राणां क्षत्रभृत्तमो वयोधाः । \ महान् महित्वे तस्तभानः \ क्षत्रे राष्ट्रे च जागृहि । \ प्रजापतेस् त्वा परमेष्ठिनः स्वाराज्येनाभिषिञ्चामि \\ इति ॥
17.5.23.a.m: To the south of the āhavanīya fire, on [ground] not excavated for the altar, he is consecrated with fresh milk during the Māhendrastotra, with [the mantra]: 'Born wealthy, grown with force, greatest bearer of dominion among dominions, bestower of vitality, / great, established in greatness, be watchful over the dominion and realm! / With the sovereignty of Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin, I consecrate you!'

17.5.24.a.s: gosaveneṣṭvā saṃvatsaraṃ dvādaśāhaṃ vā govrato bhavati //
17.5.24.a.d: गोसवेनेष्ट्वा संवत्सरं द्वादशाहं वा गोव्रतो भवति ॥
17.5.24.a.m: Having sacrificed with the Gosava, he observes the vow of a bull for a year or for twelve days.

17.5.25.a.s: upa mātaram iyād upa svasāram upa sagotrām upa nigāyodakaṃ pibati tṛṇāni vā cchinatti //
17.5.25.a.d: उप मातरम् इयाद् उप स्वसारम् उप सगोत्राम् उप निगायोदकं पिबति तृणानि वा च्छिनत्ति ॥
17.5.25.a.m: He may approach his mother, he may approach his sister, he may approach a woman of the same gotra; bending down, he drinks water or crops grass.

17.5.26.a.s: yatrayatrainaṃ viṣṭhā vindet tatratatra vitiṣṭhito 'pavagāhaṃ gaurīva siṣam //
17.5.26.a.d: यत्रयत्रैनं विष्ठा विन्देत् तत्रतत्र वितिष्ठितो ऽपवगाहं गौरीव सिषम् ॥
17.5.26.a.m: Wherever the urge to defecate overtakes him, there he voids it, plunging in like a cow.

17.5.27.a.m: With the Marutstoma, he prospers with boundless prosperity.

17.5.29.a.s: indrastomenokthyena rathaṃtarasāmnā bṛhatsāmnobhayasāmnā vā tena dvau yājayet //
17.5.29.a.d: इन्द्रस्तोमेनोक्थ्येन रथंतरसाम्ना बृहत्साम्नोभयसाम्ना वा तेन द्वौ याजयेत् ॥
17.5.29.a.m: With the Indrastoma, an Ukthya having the Rathaṃtara sāman, having the Bṛhat sāman, or having both sāmans, he should cause two persons to sacrifice.

17.5.30.a.d: ऋषभेणाग्निष्टोमेन बृहत्साम्ना ब्राह्मणो ऽधिपतिः समानानां भवति ॥
17.5.30.a.m: With the Ṛṣabha Agniṣṭoma having the Bṛhat sāman, a Brahmin becomes the overlord of his equals.

17.5.31.a.s: indrāgnyoḥ kulāyena rājapurohitāv ubhāv ekasyāṃ yājayet //
17.5.31.a.d: इन्द्राग्न्योः कुलायेन राजपुरोहिताव् उभाव् एकस्यां याजयेत् ॥
17.5.31.a.m: With the Kulāya of Indra and Agni, he should cause both a king and his domestic priest to sacrifice on the same [rite].

17.5.32.a.s: tejo brahmavarcasaṃ prāvaruddhyai viśam̐ rājā praviśati //
17.5.32.a.d: तेजो ब्रह्मवर्चसं प्रावरुद्ध्यै विशम्̐ राजा प्रविशति ॥
17.5.32.a.m: In order to secure fiery energy and spiritual luster, the king enters the peasantry.

17.5.33.a.s: vighanena vi pāpmānaṃ bhrātṛvyam̐ hate / tena sarvā mṛdho vihate //
17.5.33.a.d: विघनेन वि पाप्मानं भ्रातृव्यम्̐ हते । तेन सर्वा मृधो विहते ॥
17.5.33.a.m: With the Vighana, he smites away evil and his rival; with it he smites away all foes.

17.5.34.a.s: saṃdam̐śena bhrātṛvyavān vajreṇa ṣoḍaśinābhicarañ śyenena vyākhyātaḥ //
17.5.34.a.d: संदम्̐शेन भ्रातृव्यवान् वज्रेण षोडशिनाभिचरञ् श्येनेन व्याख्यातः ॥
17.5.34.a.m: With the Saṃdaṃśa [sacrifices] one who has a rival; performing sorcery with the Vajra and Ṣoḍaśin, he is explained by [the procedure of] the Śyena.

17.5.35.a.m: One desirous of prosperity [performs] a thirteen-night [or] three-night [sacrifice].

17.5.36.a.m: One wishing to thrive [sacrifices] with the Sarvastoma.

17.5.37.a.m: One desirous of cattle [sacrifices] with the Aptoryāma,

17.5.38.a.m: from whom cattle might utterly slip away.

17.5.39.a.m: The animal victims are [offered] in a group of eleven.

17.5.40.a.m: One desirous of offspring [sacrifices] with the Navasaptadaśa.

17.5.41.a.m: By the Viṣuvant, an eldest son born of the senior wife attains supremacy.

17.5.42.a.m: By the Goṣṭoma, one who has a rival.

17.5.46.a.m: One desirous of spiritual luster with the Trivṛt.

17.5.47.a.m: One desirous of vigor with the Pañcadaśa.

17.5.48.a.m: One desirous of offspring with the Saptadaśa.

17.5.49.a.m: One desirous of firm standing with the Ekaviṃśa.

17.6.1.a.m: The ahīna sacrifices beginning with the two-night rite up to the eleven-night rite have an Atirātra at the end.

17.6.2.a.m: Their ritual procedure is explained by the Dvādaśāha in its form as an ahīna.

17.6.3.a.s: dvirātrasya trirātrasya catūrātrasya pañcarātrasya saptarātrasya navarātrasyottamam aindravāyavāgram / śukrāgraṃ vā //
17.6.3.a.d: द्विरात्रस्य त्रिरात्रस्य चतूरात्रस्य पञ्चरात्रस्य सप्तरात्रस्य नवरात्रस्योत्तमम् ऐन्द्रवायवाग्रम् । शुक्राग्रं वा ॥
17.6.3.a.m: For the two-night rite, the three-night rite, the four-night rite, the five-night rite, the seven-night rite, and the nine-night rite, the last [day] has the Aindravāyava cup first, or the Śukra cup first.

17.6.4.a.m: On the second day of the two-night rite, he draws the Ṣoḍaśin cup.

17.6.5.a.m: On the middle [day] of the three-night rite; [and similarly] in the various ahīnas beginning with the four-night rite.

17.6.6.a.s: āṅgirasena yaḥ puṇye 'hīna iva syāt sa etena yajeta //
17.6.6.a.d: आङ्गिरसेन यः पुण्ये ऽहीन इव स्यात् स एतेन यजेत ॥
17.6.6.a.m: With the Āṅgirasa, one who is as if deficient in virtue should sacrifice with this.

17.6.7.a.d: तस्य ज्योतिष्टोमो ऽग्निष्टोमः पूर्वम् अहर् भवति ॥
17.6.7.a.m: Its first day is an Agniṣṭoma Jyotiṣṭoma.

17.6.8.a.m: The second is a Sarvastoma Atirātra.

17.6.9.a.s: gāyatraṃ pūrve 'han sāma bhavati / traiṣṭubham uttare //
17.6.9.a.d: गायत्रं पूर्वे ऽहन् साम भवति । त्रैष्टुभम् उत्तरे ॥
17.6.9.a.m: The sāman on the first day is in the gāyatrī metre; on the second, in the triṣṭubh metre.

17.6.10.a.m: The sāman on the first day is the Rathaṃtara;

17.6.12.a.s: vaikhānasaṃ pūrve 'han sāma bhavati ṣoḍaśy uttare //
17.6.12.a.d: वैखानसं पूर्वे ऽहन् साम भवति षोडश्य् उत्तरे ॥
17.6.12.a.m: The sāman on the first day is the Vaikhānasa; on the second, the Ṣoḍaśin.

17.6.13.a.s: haviṣman nidhanaṃ pūrvam ahar bhavati / haviṣkṛn nidhanam uttaram //
17.6.13.a.d: हविष्मन् निधनं पूर्वम् अहर् भवति । हविष्कृन् निधनम् उत्तरम् ॥
17.6.13.a.m: The first day has the word havis as its finale; the second day has the word haviṣkṛt as its finale.

17.6.14.a.m: The first day is on the new-moon day, the second on the day of sacrifice.

17.6.15.a.m: Whatever desire one may desire, one attains it through the Kāpivana rite.

17.6.16.a.s: tasya jyotiṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomaḥ pūrvam ahar bhavati / atirātra uttaram //
17.6.16.a.d: तस्य ज्योतिष्टोमो ऽग्निष्टोमः पूर्वम् अहर् भवति । अतिरात्र उत्तरम् ॥
17.6.16.a.m: Its first day is a Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma; the second is an Atirātra.

17.6.17.a.m: Through the Caitraratha rite, one secures all edible food.

17.6.18.a.s: tasya trivṛtpañcadaśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ pūrvam ahar āyuratirātra uttaram //
17.6.18.a.d: तस्य त्रिवृत्पञ्चदशो ऽग्निष्टोमः पूर्वम् अहर् आयुरतिरात्र उत्तरम् ॥
17.6.18.a.m: Its first day is a Trivṛt-Pañcadaśa Agniṣṭoma; the second is an Āyus-Atirātra.

17.6.19.a.m: Through the Garga three-day rite, one ascends to the Vasus, the Rudras, [and] the Ādityas.

17.6.20.a.m: One firmly establishes oneself in these worlds.

17.6.21.a.s: agniṣṭoma ukthyo 'tirātras tryahāni rathaṃtaraṃ vāmadevyaṃ bṛhad iti pṛṣṭhāni //
17.6.21.a.d: अग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यो ऽतिरात्रस् त्र्यहानि रथंतरं वामदेव्यं बृहद् इति पृष्ठानि ॥
17.6.21.a.m: The three days are an Agniṣṭoma, an Ukthya, [and] an Atirātra; the pṛṣṭha-stotras are the Rathaṃtara, the Vāmadevya, [and] the Bṛhat.

17.6.22.a.s: āgnāvaiṣṇava ekādaśakapālaḥ sārasvataś carur bārhaspatyaś carur iti // dīkṣaṇīyā traidhātavīyā vā //
17.6.22.a.d: आग्नावैष्णव एकादशकपालः सारस्वतश् चरुर् बार्हस्पत्यश् चरुर् इति ॥ दीक्षणीया त्रैधातवीया वा ॥
17.6.22.a.m: The dīkṣaṇīyā rite consists of an eleven-potsherd cake to Agni-and-Viṣṇu, a pap to Sarasvatī, and a pap to Bṛhaspati, or it is the Traidhātavīyā.

17.6.23.a.s: babhrur aruṇā rohiṇī piṅgākṣy ekahāyanī somakrayaṇī //
17.6.23.a.d: बभ्रुर् अरुणा रोहिणी पिङ्गाक्ष्य् एकहायनी सोमक्रयणी ॥
17.6.23.a.m: The cow with which soma is purchased is brown, ruddy, red, yellow-eyed, and one year old.

17.6.24.a.s: sahasraṃ dakṣiṇā prathame 'ham̐s trīṇi ca śatāni nayet / trayastrim̐śataṃ caivaṃ dvitīye tṛtīye ca sahasryātiricyate / dvirūpā rohiṇy ubhayataeny anyataenī vā //
17.6.24.a.d: सहस्रं दक्षिणा प्रथमे ऽहम्̐स् त्रीणि च शतानि नयेत् । त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शतं चैवं द्वितीये तृतीये च सहस्र्यातिरिच्यते । द्विरूपा रोहिण्य् उभयतएन्य् अन्यतएनी वा ॥
17.6.24.a.m: On the first day, he should bring out three hundred and thirty-three as the sacrificial fee of a thousand; similarly on the second; and on the third, the thousandth cow is left over; [she is] of two colors, red, piebald on both sides, or piebald on one side.

17.6.25.a.d: तां प्रथमे ऽहनि नयेत् । उत्तमे वोत्तमा ॥
17.6.25.a.m: He should bring her on the first day, or the best [cow] on the last [day].

17.6.26.a.s: prathame 'hani deyas tvam agne sahasram ānaya \\ ud balasyābhi nas tvam / \ sa naḥ sahasram ānaya \ prajayā paśubhiḥ saha \ punar māviśatād rayir iti // ud bhṛṣṭis tam anumantrayate / vehad dvitīye tvam apām oṣadhīnām \\ rasena rasinī babhuditha / \ sā mā sahasra ābhaja \ prajayā paśubhiḥ saha \ punar mā viśatād rayir iti vehataṃ vāmanas tṛtīye pratiṣṭhāsi sahasrasya \ vaiṣṇavo vāmanas tvam / \ sa naḥ sahasram ādhehi \ prajayā paśubhiḥ saha \ punar mā viśatād rayir iti //
17.6.26.a.d: प्रथमे ऽहनि देयस् त्वम् अग्ने सहस्रम् आनय \\ उद् बलस्याभि नस् त्वम् । \ स नः सहस्रम् आनय \ प्रजया पशुभिः सह \ पुनर् माविशताद् रयिर् इति ॥ उद् भृष्टिस् तम् अनुमन्त्रयते । वेहद् द्वितीये त्वम् अपाम् ओषधीनाम् \\ रसेन रसिनी बभुदिथ । \ सा मा सहस्र आभज \ प्रजया पशुभिः सह \ पुनर् मा विशताद् रयिर् इति वेहतं वामनस् तृतीये प्रतिष्ठासि सहस्रस्य \ वैष्णवो वामनस् त्वम् । \ स नः सहस्रम् आधेहि \ प्रजया पशुभिः सह \ पुनर् मा विशताद् रयिर् इति ॥
17.6.26.a.m: To be given on the first day: with 'You, O Agni, bring a thousand; raise us above strength; do you bring us a thousand, together with offspring and cattle; may wealth enter into me again,' he consecrates a steer. On the second, a barren cow, with 'You have become juicy with the juice of waters and plants; as such, make me share in a thousand, together with offspring and cattle; may wealth enter into me again.' On the third, a dwarf, with 'You are the support of the thousand, you are a dwarf belonging to Viṣṇu; as such, place a thousand in us, together with offspring and cattle; may wealth enter into me again.'

17.6.27.a.s: vāmanaṃ taṃ jyeṣṭhad yathainaṃ sahasram utsṛjati //
17.6.27.a.d: वामनं तं ज्येष्ठद् यथैनं सहस्रम् उत्सृजति ॥
17.6.27.a.m: Just as he releases that eldest dwarf cow, so he releases the thousand.
